body:
> [!CAUTION]
> This PR ships a build-gated funding-wallet seam (`NEXT_PUBLIC_E2E=1`) that signs `x402.fundWallet` calls with an injected private key. The deploy serving the smoke target **must not** be the canonical `app.grove.city` service. A hostname allowlist (`localhost`, `*.testnet.*`, `e2e.*`) is enforced at runtime as defense-in-depth, but Render env hygiene is still required.

_tl;dr Continuous prod smoke that drives email-OTP login → crypto top-up → earnings → offramp end-to-end against the live site._

## Summary

- **Live prod smoke workflow**: New `.github/workflows/prod-e2e-email-crypto.yml` exercises the full email-login → top-up → offramp path against `https://grove.city`, with auto-incremented `robot+N@grove.city` accounts per run
- **Build-gated injected funding wallet**: New `src/lib/e2eWallet.ts` lets `useCryptoDeposit` sign deposits with a private key seeded by Playwright when `NEXT_PUBLIC_E2E=1`, hostname-allowlisted to `localhost`/`*.testnet.*`/`e2e.*` so the path cannot activate on canonical user-facing domains
- **Gmail OTP automation**: `scripts/gauth/` adds an OAuth refresh-token bootstrap (`gauth:token`) and an inbox poller that retrieves the 6-digit code with context-aware regex, scoping the search to the active `to:` recipient to avoid cross-run collisions
- **Robot identity counter**: `bootstrap-email-login.js` resolves a starting `N` from `ROBOT_COUNTER_START` (or persisted counter file), probes up to 5 fresh accounts, completes new-user registration, and writes `output/playwright/storage-state.json` for the smoke
- **Stale `.next/types` cleanup in `dev-format`**: `make dev-format` now wipes `.next/types`/`.next/dev/types` before `tsc --noEmit` so deleted-route validators don't leak `TS2307` failures across branches

## Feature Diff

| S    | Component                              | Before                                  | After                                                                                |
| ---- | -------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| 🟢   | Prod smoke workflow                    | `N/A`                                   | `prod-e2e-email-crypto.yml` runs email-login → top-up → offramp on dispatch          |
| 🟢   | E2E funding-wallet seam                | `N/A`                                   | `src/lib/e2eWallet.ts` + `normalizePrivateKey.ts` (build-gated by `NEXT_PUBLIC_E2E`) |
| 🟢   | Hostname allowlist guard               | `N/A`                                   | Window-global signer rejected on hosts outside `/(localhost\|127\.0\.0\.1\|.*\.testnet\..+\|e2e\..+)/i` |
| 🟡   | `useCryptoDeposit` signer              | wagmi wallet client only                | Branches on `hasE2eFundingWallet()`; falls through to wagmi otherwise                |
| 🟢   | Gmail OTP retrieval                    | `N/A`                                   | `scripts/gauth/mailbox.js` polls Gmail API, extracts 6-digit code via context regex  |
| 🟢   | Robot+N identity                       | `N/A`                                   | Counter file + `ROBOT_AUTO_INCREMENT` claims fresh `robot+N@grove.city` per run      |
| 🟢   | `NEXT_PUBLIC_E2E` env wiring           | `N/A`                                   | Added to `envs/*.env`, `render.yaml` (both services), GitHub Actions secrets         |
| 🟢   | Playwright prod config                 | `N/A`                                   | `playwright.prod.config.ts` (one chromium project, 1 retry on CI, line reporter)     |
| 🟡   | `make dev-format`                      | Left stale `.next/types` validators     | Wipes them before `tsc --noEmit` to avoid cross-branch `TS2307` noise                |
| ⚙️   | Vitest scope                           | `src/**/*.test.{ts,tsx}` only           | Now also includes `scripts/**/*.test.{ts,tsx}`                                       |
| ⚙️   | ESLint                                 | `no-require-imports` enforced repo-wide | Scoped relaxation for `scripts/**/*.js` (CJS helpers)                                |
| ⚪   | `output/`, `.env.secrets`              | `N/A`                                   | Added to `.gitignore`; new keys documented in `.env.secrets.example`                 |

> 🔴 Critical fix · 🟡 Improvement · 🟢 New feature · ⚪ Neutral · ⚙️ Infra/tooling · ⚠️ Breaking

## Details

<details>
<summary>Technical Details</summary>

### `src/lib/` — funding-wallet seam

- **Build-time gate**: `E2E_ENABLED = process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_E2E === '1'` lets Next.js inline `false` and tree-shake the path when disabled (best-effort, documented in source)
- **Two seed sources**: `window.__groveE2EFundingWallet__` (re-seeded by Playwright `addInitScript` on every navigation) and `localStorage.__groveE2EFundingWallet__` (reload resilience for local runs; gated off in production by `NEXT_PUBLIC_ENV !== 'production'`)
- **Hostname allowlist**: `getE2eFundingWalletConfig()` returns `null` unless `window.location.hostname` matches `/(localhost|127\.0\.0\.1|.*\.testnet\..+|e2e\..+)/i` — defense-in-depth even if `NEXT_PUBLIC_E2E=1` leaks
- **Cached client**: `getE2eFundingWalletClient()` keys on `(privateKey, rpcUrl)` so a re-seed with a different RPC URL refreshes the viem client
- **`normalizePrivateKey()`**: validates `0x`-prefixed 32-byte hex shape and throws a clear error before viem's `privateKeyToAccount` consumes it
- **`useCryptoDeposit`**: resolves `e2eWalletEnabled` once per mount, branches signer + address selection on it, suppresses `walletNeedsReconnection`/`isWrongNetwork` and short-circuits `handleReconnectWallet` (with `cta:` log) when active

### `scripts/gauth/` — Gmail OAuth + OTP harness

- **`script.js`**: interactive OAuth helper that opens a localhost redirect server, exchanges the consent code for a refresh token, and writes it back to `.env.secrets`
- **`mailbox.js`**: refresh-token → access-token exchange + Gmail v1 API client; `findLatestOtpEmail` polls `messages.list` then fetches each `messages/get`, decodes base64url MIME parts, and applies a context regex (`code|otp|verification|...` near 6 digits) before falling back to plain `\b\d{6}\b`
- **`bootstrap-email-login.js`**: launches Chromium against `/welcome`, fills email, scopes the OTP search to `to:${identity.email}`, fills the 6-digit code, races authenticated state vs. new-user dialog, completes registration if needed, and writes Playwright `storageState`. Counter persisted at `output/playwright/robot-counter.json`; up to `MAX_ROBOT_ATTEMPTS=5` per run
- **Test coverage**: `bootstrap-email-login.test.ts` covers `parseBoolean`, `buildRobotIdentity`, counter file round-trips, and `resolveStartingN` precedence; `mailbox.test.ts` covers OTP candidate extraction and the full `findLatestOtpEmail` happy path; new `env.test.ts` covers `loadEnvFile` parsing edge cases

### `tests/prod-e2e/` — smoke spec

- **`happy-path.spec.ts`**: `seedFundingWallet(context)` → `/balances` → Top Up modal → Crypto radio → fill amount → consent checkbox → click `Top Up $X.XX` → wait for `Completing via x402...` → wait for modal close → Withdraw → Cash Out to Wallet → fill `WITHDRAW_ADDRESS` (defaults to `dEaD`, asserted ≠ funding wallet) → fill amount → submit
- **`wallet-setup/funding-wallet.ts`**: derives address from `GROVE__FUNDING_WALLET_PRIVATE_KEY`, asserts it matches `GROVE__FUNDING_WALLET_ADDRESS` to prevent silent secret-store drift, then seeds both `window.__groveE2EFundingWallet__` and `localStorage` via `context.addInitScript`
- **`playwright.prod.config.ts`**: dedicated config (`testDir: './tests/prod-e2e'`, no parallelism, `retries: CI ? 1 : 0`, line reporter, optional `storageState` from env)

### Infra

- **`makefiles/dev.mk`**: new `test-e2e-prod-email-crypto` target sequences `auth:bootstrap-email` → `test:e2e:prod`; required-env banner lists Gmail + funding-wallet keys
- **`render.yaml`**: `NEXT_PUBLIC_E2E` declared with `sync: false` on b

author: luluameh
body:
Closes #1031

Closes #1032

Closes #1034

Closes #1035


Description
This PR addresses several critical backend infrastructure and operational issues required for production readiness. It introduces automated cron jobs for cleaning up old resources, enhances system health monitoring, sets up automated backup verification, and resolves existing test suite errors to ensure the CI pipeline runs smoothly.

Closes #1031 - Setup temporary file cleanup Closes #1032 - Implement session cleanup and expiration Closes #1034 - Implement health check automation Closes #1035 - Setup automated backup verification

Key Changes
Temporary File Cleanup: Implemented TempFileCleanupService utilizing a nightly cron job to purge temporary system files and standard uploads older than 24 hours.
Session & Token Cleanup: Introduced SessionCleanupService to run an hourly sweep, nullifying expired password reset tokens and unlocking user accounts when the lockout duration passes.
Automated Health Checking: Added HealthAutomationService, running every 5 minutes to trigger the existing Terminus indicators (Database, Stellar, Memory). The service automatically alerts the logger about degraded or failing dependencies.
Backup Verification Script: Created scripts/verify-backup.sh and a make verify-backup target to automatically locate the latest pg_dump backup, spin up a temporary database instance, restore the data, and run verification counts on the "user" table to ensure backup integrity.
Bug Fixes & Refactoring:
Fixed a failing edge-case test in payment.service.spec.ts where BadRequestException was thrown before the user notification could be dispatched.
Applied global auto-fix linting across the codebase to ensure all checks pass locally during make ci.
Verification Steps
Run make ci to verify all automated testing, types, and formatting checks pass securely.
Run make verify-backup (assuming a running local Postgres instance) to confirm the backup extraction logic operates smoothly.

## Spec-28 — E2E Bug Hunt & Quality Baseline

This PR closes the spec-28 work executed so far: Wave 1 (Playwright stabilization), Wave 2 (RAGAS harness scaffold), the HITL Live Block (Charter 1 bug investigation), and the Session 5 follow-up (BUG-013 root cause + BUG-014 prevention). Wave 3 (RAGAS evaluation run with user-authored Q-018/019/020) and Wave 4 (treemap, SUMMARY, polish) ship as follow-up PRs against `develop`.

### Wave 1 — Playwright stabilization (`123803d`, `8e1177b`)
- 26/26 Playwright suite green locally; 25/26 in CI (1 known-flaky test under `continue-on-error` per BUG-001 deferred)
- `scripts/validate-bug-records.sh` for spec-28 audit-trail validation
- CI evidence + screenshots committed under `docs/E2E/2026-04-24-bug-hunt/`

### Wave 2 — RAGAS harness (`4050960`)
- `tests/quality/` scaffold: 17 golden Q&A pairs, `[project.optional-dependencies.quality]` group (ragas==0.2.15, datasets, openai, pyyaml)
- Wave 3 will fill in Q-018/Q-019/Q-020 (user-authored) and run RAGAS evaluation

### Live Block — Charter 1 bugfixes
- **BUG-002 collection-scope leak — FIXED** (`97bbe98` + amendment `7c4203e`)
  - Allowlist enforcement on both `search_child_chunks` and `semantic_search_all_collections`
  - 15 regression tests in `tests/unit/test_research_tools.py`
  - Verified e2e: each `/api/chat` trace queries exactly 1 collection (the user's `collection_ids`)
- **BUG-006 cross_encoder_rerank dedup zero-out — FIXED** (`6d8b27a`)
  - Reranked output now updates rerank_score in place by chunk_id instead of being dedup-rejected
  - `TestRerankScoreUpdate` regression tests added
- 13 bug records filed under `docs/E2E/2026-04-24-bug-hunt/bugs-raw/` + session-log

### Session 5 — BUG-013 root cause + BUG-014 prevention
- **BUG-013 SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE on every `/api/chat` — RESOLVED via operational recovery** (`20c1dc5`)
  - True root cause: `data/checkpoints.db` corrupted (multiple double-referenced freelist pages, 91% freelist ratio). All 4 hypotheses in the Session 5 plan refuted.
  - Recovery: `VACUUM INTO 'salvage'` → `REINDEX` → swap. Salvage was 33 MB (10× smaller), all 102 threads / 1,870 checkpoints / 9,962 writes recovered.
  - 3-query smoke (factoid + analytical + OOS) all return clean `done` events post-recovery
- **BUG-014 prune-without-vacuum + rebuild-on-source-change — PARTIALLY FIXED** (`02526c2`)
  - **Layer 1** (code): `_prune_old_checkpoint_threads` now runs `VACUUM` after deleting threads. Prevents the freelist bloat that produced BUG-013.
  - **Layer 2** (observability): new `_check_checkpoint_integrity` helper called at startup. Logs `storage_checkpoint_integrity_failed` (warn-only) with recovery-runbook pointer if `PRAGMA integrity_check` fails.
  - **B1** (DX): `scripts/dev-rebuild-backend.sh` + CONTRIBUTING.md note. Documents that `Dockerfile.backend` has no `backend/` bind mount, so `docker compose restart` does NOT pick up source changes — image must be rebuilt. (This DX gap is what masked Live Block live-verifications: the running image was 2026-04-14, two weeks before the BUG-002/006 fixes landed.)
  - 6 unit tests in `tests/unit/test_checkpoint_lifecycle.py` covering integrity-check (clean / corrupt / exception paths) and prune (disabled / under-limit / VACUUMs-freelist / per-thread-failure resilience)
  - **Deferred to v1.1**: Layer 3 (auto-recovery hook), B2 (dev-mode bind-mount + uvicorn --reload), `auto_vacuum=incremental` migration

### Format hygiene (`6bae8d3`)
- 4 spec-28 files reformatted by ruff-format (pre-existing format violations exposed by required `pre-commit-parity` and `backend-format-check` gates)

### Quality gates
- `validate-bug-records.sh`: 14 OK, 0 errors
- `ruff check`: clean
- `ruff format --check`: clean (after `6bae8d3`)
- SACRED files unchanged: `git diff develop -- Makefile embedinator.sh embedinator.ps1` = 0
- 1 known non-blocking failure: SC-003 frontend-e2e (BUG-001 deferred via `continue-on-error: true`)
- All required CI checks green (rebased onto `develop` tip after the 8 dependabot batch merges)

### Out of scope (follow-up PRs to develop)
- Wave 3 — RAGAS evaluation run + Q-018/019/020 (user-authored)
- Wave 4 — treemap, `SUMMARY.md`, polish
- BUG-014 v1.1 spec (Layer 3 auto-recovery + B2 dev bind-mount + `auto_vacuum=incremental` migration)

### Closes
- Wave 1 mandate (SC-001)
- Charter 1 Blocker triage (BUG-002, BUG-006, BUG-007 user-facing closure, BUG-013)
- BUG-014 layers 1+2 + B1

author: natejsimonsen
body:
## Summary

Add `ROLLOUTS_VERSION` and `ROLLOUTS_DIGEST` build args so consumers can rebuild the plugin image against a newer argo-rollouts controller without forking, and bump the default base from `v1.8.3` to `v1.9.0` so freshly built images track current argo-rollouts releases.

## Why

The current Dockerfile hard-pins `FROM quay.io/argoproj/argo-rollouts:v1.8.3@sha256:...`. The recommended install pattern in `config/argo-rollouts/kustomization.yaml` is to swap the controller image with this plugin image, which means consumers running argo-rollouts v1.9.0 are silently downgraded to v1.8.3 when adopting this plugin.

This is fine when v1.8.3 is current, but becomes a problem as the upstream argo-rollouts release train moves on:
- v1.9.0 has been out for some time and includes CRD changes (e.g. `preserveUnknownFields` removed, `*bool clusterScope`) that don't roundtrip cleanly to v1.8.3.
- Without a build-arg override, downstream consumers either have to fork this repo or accept the silent downgrade.

## What changes

```diff
-FROM quay.io/argoproj/argo-rollouts:v1.8.3@sha256:2b7be...
+ARG ROLLOUTS_VERSION=v1.9.0
+ARG ROLLOUTS_DIGEST=sha256:13346024500167f71815e1dcd7671f46378137e726ef03b2baf69a188224f813
+FROM quay.io/argoproj/argo-rollouts:${ROLLOUTS_VERSION}@${ROLLOUTS_DIGEST}
```

Override at build time:
```
docker build \
  --build-arg ROLLOUTS_VERSION=v1.10.0 \
  --build-arg ROLLOUTS_DIGEST=sha256:... .
```

Default published images now ship with v1.9.0 controller + plugin binary baked in.

## Compatibility

The plugin binary is built in the earlier `FROM golang` stage and dropped at `/home/argo-rollouts/rollouts-plugin-metric-ai`. That path is unchanged across v1.8.3 → v1.9.0, and the plugin↔controller boundary is go-plugin RPC, which is stable across argo-rollouts minor versions.

## Test plan

- [ ] `make docker-build` succeeds with default args (produces v1.9.0-based image).
- [ ] `make docker-build` with `--build-arg ROLLOUTS_VERSION=v1.8.3 --build-arg ROLLOUTS_DIGEST=sha256:2b7be...` reproduces the previous image.
- [ ] Existing kind-based deploy (per AGENTS.md) brings up the controller and the plugin loads.

author: andrewbuilt
body:
## Summary

PR-A follow-up. Drop-from-unscheduled on `/capacity` was writing `hours_allocated = 0` because the handler read two stale sources:

- `subprojects.labor_hours` — legacy column, never written by current estimating code. Always 0.
- `department_allocations` — only seeded by `lib/schedule-seed.ts` when a project auto-advances to 'production'. Sold projects have zero rows.

Fix: lift hours into a shared helper that rolls up `estimate_lines` via `computeSubprojectRollup` — the canonical source the project page, subproject page, and composer staleness already use. Stage-agnostic.

## New helper — `lib/project-hours.ts`

```ts
loadProjectDeptHours(orgId, projectId)
  → { totalHours, deptHours: Record<deptId, hours> }
```

- Loads `orgs.consumable_markup_pct` + `shop_rate` for the rollup ctx.
- Loads subprojects + departments.
- Builds a `LaborDept`-key → `departments.id` map by name match (same heuristic `projects/[id]/page.tsx` uses for actuals).
- For each subproject: `loadEstimateLines` + `loadRateBook` + ctx with `profitMarginPct = 0` (matches `lib/project-totals.ts`), runs `computeSubprojectRollup`, sums `totalHours` and folds `hoursByDept` into the dept-id-keyed map. Departments without a canonical `LaborDept` name skip dept attribution (their hours still fold into `totalHours`).

## Capacity page wiring

- **Drop-from-unscheduled** — replaces the `labor_hours` sum + the `department_allocations`-derived `buildDeptHours()` with one `loadProjectDeptHours` call.
- **Move-between-months — single allocation** — refreshes hours from the helper too, so a stale-zero allocation doesn't propagate.
- **Move-between-months — split group** — preserves per-month hours distribution (intentional split, not stale).
- Drops the `labor_hours` column from the subprojects select + interface so the legacy field doesn't tempt future readers.

## Reports outlook (`lib/reports/bookedProjects.ts`)

- Hours total now comes from `loadProjectDeptHours`. Department allocations are still queried for the timeline (`scheduled_date` / `scheduled_days` are the only timing source) but their hours column is no longer the trust point.
- Stage gate widened from `('production','installed')` to `('sold','production','installed')` so won work counts as booked. Sold projects without department_allocations are still dropped from the chart since they have no timeline yet.

## Verification

```
$ grep -n "loadProjectDeptHours" lib/project-hours.ts 'app/(app)/capacity/page.tsx' lib/reports/bookedProjects.ts
lib/project-hours.ts:68:export async function loadProjectDeptHours(
lib/project-hours.ts:146:    console.error('loadProjectDeptHours', err)
app/(app)/capacity/page.tsx:10:import { loadProjectDeptHours } from '@/lib/project-hours'
app/(app)/capacity/page.tsx:124:  // Hours per project come from estimate_lines via loadProjectDeptHours
app/(app)/capacity/page.tsx:239:        const fresh = await loadProjectDeptHours(org.id, dragProjectId)
app/(app)/capacity/page.tsx:252:      const fresh = await loadProjectDeptHours(org.id, dragProjectId)
lib/reports/bookedProjects.ts:6:// endMonth }. Hours come from estimate_lines via loadProjectDeptHours
lib/reports/bookedProjects.ts:21:import { loadProjectDeptHours } from '../project-hours'
lib/reports/bookedProjects.ts:104:      const r = await loadProjectDeptHours(p.org_id, p.id)

$ grep -n "subprojects.labor_hours\|labor_hours: " 'app/(app)/capacity/page.tsx'
(no output — legacy reads gone)
```

Type-check clean (only the same pre-existing unrelated `capacity/page.tsx:116` `Project[]` cast error from main remains — `stage` vs `status` mismatch, untouched here).

## Smoke test

- [ ] Drop a sold project with known `estimate_lines` hours onto Apr → Apr utilization % moves.
- [ ] Per-dept progress bars on Apr's card match the project page's per-dept breakdown for that project.
- [ ] Reports → Outlook now shows sold projects (provided they have department_allocations rows).

author: koki3070
body:
## この PR の目的

本リポジトリは監査ドキュメントで **公開前ゲート F-1** として「静的解析の正規コマンドは `uv run ruff check .` とする」と既に定めていますが、**GitHub Actions でそのコマンドが自動実行される仕組みがありませんでした**。

この PR は **Issue #23**（タイトル: `[audit][G-4][P0] F-1 CI最低ゲート実装（ruff強制）`）の実装です。**Pull Request および `main` ブランチへの push のたびに**、依存を `uv` で同期したうえで **同じ `ruff check` を CI 上で必ず実行**し、失敗時はジョブを失敗させます。

## 変更ファイル一覧（レビュー観点）

| ファイル | 内容 |
|----------|------|
| `.github/workflows/ruff.yml` | **新規**。ワークフロー名は `Ruff`。下記「ワークフローの流れ」を参照。 |
| `README.md` | 公開前ゲート F-1 の節に、**CI がいつ何をするか**、**マージをブロックするには Branch protection が別途必要**であること、**ローカルで同じ検査を再現するコマンド**を追記。 |
| `docs/audit/reproducibility_checklist.md` | F-1 の「CI最小要件」を **ワークフロー実装済み**に合わせて更新し、**#23 の実装ログ**（日付・対象・反映内容）を追記。 |

## ワークフローの流れ（初見向け）

1. **コード取得**  
   `pyproject.toml` の `[tool.uv.sources]` で **`torch_topological` がローカル path（`pytorch-topological/`）** 参照のため、`actions/checkout` で **`submodules: recursive`** を指定しています（サブモジュールが無い場合でも害はありません）。

2. **ツールチェーン**  
   [astral-sh/setup-uv](https://github.com/astral-sh/setup-uv)（v5）で **uv** と **Python 3.12**（`pyproject.toml` の `requires-python = ">=3.12"` と整合）を用意し、キャッシュを有効化して **初回以降の `uv sync` を軽く**しています。

3. **依存の同期**  
   `uv sync --all-groups --frozen` で **`uv.lock` に固定された解像度**のまま、本パッケージと **dev グループ（`ruff`）** をインストールします。

4. **ゲート**  
   リポジトリ直下で **`uv run ruff check .`** を実行します。終了コードが 0 でない場合、**CI は失敗**します。

5. **権限**  
   `permissions: contents: read` のみに制限しています。

## マージ後に管理者側でやるとよいこと

- **必須ステータスチェック**  
  ブランチ保護ルールで、本ワークフロー（ジョブ名 `ruff`、チェック名は GitHub 上で `Ruff / ruff` のように表示されることが多いです）を **必須チェック**に入れると、**ruff 失敗時にマージできない**運用にできます。ワークフロー単体では「失敗する」までで、**マージ禁止はリポジトリ設定**です。

- **fork からの PR**  
  初回など **「Approve and run workflows」** が必要な場合があります。Actions が動いていないように見えるときは、PR 画面の該当表示をご確認ください。

## ローカルでの同じ検査（任意）

```bash
uv sync --all-groups --frozen
uv run ruff check .
```

解析対象外は `pyproject.toml` の `[tool.ruff]` の `exclude` に従います（例: `ellphi_repo`、`trash` など）。

## 関連リンク

- Issue: https://github.com/uda-lab/TDA-ML/issues/23

Integration for Keycard. Add supports for shielded transactions for `auth-transfers` as well as public/shielded transactions for token program and amm. Each file must be ran consecutively as accounts used in `keycard_tests_2_3.sh` may have been initialized in `keycard_tests_2_1.sh`.**

Builds off of [PR 451](https://github.com/logos-blockchain/logos-execution-zone/pull/451)

author: acautomata
body:
## Summary
- Fixes `torch.compile` producing graph breaks when `engram_enabled=True`
- Achieved by restructuring Engram data from `nn.ModuleDict` (string keys) to nested `nn.ModuleList` (integer indices) and precomputing hash powers
- Adds checkpoint backward compatibility for old-format engram state dicts

## Changes
### Root cause
`EngramModule.forward` had three torch.compile-incompatible patterns:
1. `torch.tensor()` constructed from Python list inside `_ngram_hash` — **forced graph break**
2. Python dict access via dynamically-built string keys (`hash_seeds[key]`, `table_sizes[key]`) — **graph break**
3. `nn.ModuleDict` access via dynamic string keys (`embed_tables[key]`) — **unreliable with Dynamo**

### Fix
- **`nanochat/gpt.py`**: Refactored `embed_tables` to nested `nn.ModuleList`, precomputed `_powers` tensors in `__init__` + `init_weights()`, eliminated `hash_seeds` and `table_sizes` dicts
- **`nanochat/checkpoint_manager.py`**: Added `_patch_removed_state_keys` to strip old `hash_seeds.*` keys and remap `embed_tables.<n>_<k>.*` → `embed_tables.<n_idx>.<k>.*` when loading old checkpoints
- **`tests/test_engram.py`**: Updated `embed_tables.values()` → nested iteration

## Test plan
- [x] 42/42 tests pass (29 engram + 8 engine + 5 attention fallback), 10 skipped (GPU-only)
- [x] `torch.compile(model, dynamic=False)` achieves **0 graph breaks**, full graph compilation
- [x] Compile loss matches uncompiled loss
- [x] Meta device build path verified (`build_model` flow)
- [x] Old checkpoint key remapping verified (hash_seeds removal + embed_tables remap)

body:
## Summary

- **Reduce unneeded VSchema updates**: Only store VSchema in plan when the engine detects a real diff — previously stored vschema.json for all keyspaces unconditionally, causing unnecessary VSchema updates during apply that triggered PlanetScale "schema snapshot in progress" errors
- **Structured apply state machine**: All apply state transitions now flow through `ApplyEvent.NewState` on engine events. Replaces fragile string matching in `deriveApplyPhase` and a manual pre-set for branch preparation. Skips redundant DB writes when the state hasn't changed. Transitions are logged with old/new state in apply_logs.
- **Rename `CreatingBranch` → `PreparingBranch`**: The state covers both creating a new branch and reusing an existing one (schema refresh), so the name now reflects the actual semantics
- **`IsBranchSetupPhase` helper**: Centralizes the "is this a branch setup phase?" check used in the TUI for hiding tables and showing the detach footer
- **Hide queued tables during setup**: TUI hides the table list during branch setup phases (all tables are Queued with no real progress)
- **Snapshot retry**: 5 retries with exponential backoff (20s, 40s, 60s, 60s + jitter), ~3 min total
- **Log readability**: Include keyspace and branch names in log message text
- **Bug fix**: `planNamespacesToChanges` now preserves the `Operation` field when converting storage types to engine types
- **Tests**: TUI rendering tests, state transition tests, VSchema metadata unit test, e2e plan assertion, `IsBranchSetupPhase` tests

author: skgandikota
body:
## Summary

Implements the Phase 7 prompt evaluation harness from issue #22.

- New top-level `evals/` package with a pluggable `ModelClient` Protocol, `EvalRunner`, and a `FakeModelClient` so suites are runnable offline / from CI.
- Pluggable scorers: `substring`, `regex`, `json_shape` (JSON Schema), `classification`, `no_leak` (PII / secret regexes).
- YAML suites under `evals/suites/`: `baseline.yaml` (10 cases spanning the 5 intent classes), `classify.yaml`, `refine.yaml`, `verify.yaml`. Each declares `min_pass_rate` for CI-friendly exit codes.
- `python -m evals run <suite>` CLI with `--fake-client`, `--out-json`, `--out-md`. Exit code is non-zero when a suite drops below its declared threshold.
- `scripts/run_evals.py` wrapper that runs a single suite or `--all` and writes `reports/evals-<timestamp>.md`. Reports record the suite version so regressions are attributable.
- `evals/harness.py` re-export + `run_suite()` to match the file path called out in issue #22.
- `orchestrator/prompts/_loader.py` parses the `# version: N` header convention; loader fails fast if the header is missing.
- `docs/EVALS.md` covers adding a case, running a suite, and bumping a prompt version.
- Live cases that hit Ollama are gated behind a registered `pytest.mark.ollama` marker and excluded from the default `pytest` invocation.
- Wired in via `[project.optional-dependencies] evals` only; no change to required deps. Scope respected: `orchestrator/models/`, `orchestrator/providers/`, `orchestrator/pipeline/` untouched.

## Verification

- `pytest --cov=orchestrator --cov=evals --cov-fail-under=95 -q` → **309 passed, 1 skipped, 1 deselected**, total coverage **98.69%**.
- `ruff check .` → clean.
- `python -m evals run evals/suites/baseline.yaml --fake-client` → **10/10 PASS** (100%, threshold 100%).

Closes #22

Acceptance Criteria met.

`class_<class_number>_<subject>_chapter_<chapter_number>_exercise_<year>`
(e.g. `class_10_nepali_chapter_1_exercise_2083.mp4`) so the Process tab,
Publish tab, and Library tab never disagree about what a run produced.

**The problem:** the MP4 was already using the canonical stem, but the
companion `.pptx` was being written with a different name in both
`routes/runs.py` (`<safe_name>_<operation_id>.pptx`) and
`routes/generate.py` (`<safe_export_stem>.pptx`). That meant the same run
showed two unrelated filenames in the Process tab, and the Library tab
listed PPTX/MP4 files that couldn't be visually paired.

**The fix:**
- New shared helper `youtube_video_stem()` in `backend/routes/helpers.py`
  is the single source of truth for the canonical stem.
- `routes/runs.py` and `routes/generate.py` both now write
  `{stem}.mp4` and `{stem}.pptx` so each run produces a matched pair.
- Duplicated `_slug_part`, `_first_number`, `_chapter_number`, and
  `_youtube_video_stem`/`_youtube_video_output_path` helpers are removed
  from the two route files.

The canonical stem reuses the existing parsing logic (class number from
`class_name`, slugified `subject`, chapter from `title`/`output_name`/
text, default year `2083`), so existing runs keep producing the same
MP4 names they did before — only the PPTX name changes to match.

## Review & Testing Checklist for Human

- [ ] Generate one full Text-to-Video run with a class/subject/title set
      (e.g. Class 10, Nepali, "Chapter 1 …") and confirm the resulting
      `.mp4` and `.pptx` in `output/videos` and `output/presentations`
      share the same `class_10_nepali_chapter_1_exercise_2083` base name.
- [ ] In the Process tab, open the finished run and confirm the MP4 and
      PPTX rows display the matched filenames (no operation-id suffix on
      the PPTX anymore).
- [ ] In the Publish tab, the chapter card should still load the same
      MP4 path it always did and the YouTube template fill-in is
      unchanged. Confirm the video preview opens.
- [ ] In the Library tab, sort the PowerPoint and Videos lists and
      verify both show the new canonical names side-by-side.

### Notes

- The video filename was already canonical, so existing publishable runs
  keep working unchanged. Only the PPTX naming is new.
- `output_name` is still tracked on the run record for display/title
  purposes; it just no longer drives the on-disk filename.
- Re-running with the same class/subject/chapter overwrites the previous
  files (same on-disk name) — this matches the existing behaviour for
  the MP4 and is consistent with the Publish tab's per-chapter dedupe.

author: mkdev5
body:
## Summary

Closes #42011

- Problem: Control UI / Gateway Dashboard chats can stay stuck on `Stop` after a long-running embedded run times out — `Stop` does nothing, the gateway looks healthy, and the run is zombied in the UI until the page is refreshed.
- Why it matters: Crash-class UX bug on a primary surface (Control UI). Reaches any user whose model takes longer than the embedded-run timeout (the reporter saw this with `timeoutMs=600000` per the issue logs).
- What changed: `subscribeEmbeddedPiSession.unsubscribe()` now synthesizes a terminal lifecycle event when the underlying pi-agent never delivered `agent_end` to this subscription, so the gateway's `finalizeLifecycleEvent` always fires and the webchat clears its `Stop` state. Idempotent with `handleAgentEnd` via a shared `lifecycleTerminalEmitted` flag on the subscription state.
- What did NOT change (scope boundary): no changes to `runEmbeddedAttempt`/`runEmbeddedPiAgent` timeout paths, no UI-side defensive timer, no `pi-agent-core` patching, no gateway broadcast logic. The fix sits at the contract seam where the bug actually lives.

## Change Type (select all)

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Refactor required for the fix
- [ ] Docs
- [ ] Security hardening
- [ ] Chore/infra

## Scope (select all touched areas)

- [x] Gateway / orchestration
- [ ] Skills / tool execution
- [ ] Auth / tokens
- [ ] Memory / storage
- [ ] Integrations
- [ ] API / contracts
- [ ] UI / DX
- [ ] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue/PR

- Closes #42011
- [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression

## Root Cause (if applicable)

- Root cause: The embedded runner aborts the active pi-agent session via fire-and-forget `void activeSession.abort()` and then runs its inner-finally `unsubscribe()` synchronously. pi-agent-core's `runWithLifecycle` emits `agent_end` only after `await handleRunFailure → processEvents("agent_end")` completes — which lives in a separate task chain. When the runner's `unsubscribe()` removes the listener first, `agent_end` lands on zero subscribers, `handleAgentEnd` never runs, no `phase:"end"|"error"` is emitted on the agent-events bus, the gateway's `finalizeLifecycleEvent` never calls `emitChatFinal`, and the webchat client never receives `state:"final"|"error"` to clear `chatRunId`.
- Missing detection / guardrail: `subscribeEmbeddedPiSession` did not enforce the contract "exactly one terminal lifecycle event before teardown" — `handleAgentEnd` was the only emitter and it depends on an `agent_end` race that can be lost.
- Contributing context: Reporter's logs show the timeout triggered at `timeoutMs=600000`; the same race is platform-agnostic (it lives in async task scheduling) but was surfaced on Windows in the report — could plausibly hit other platforms with enough latency on the abort/teardown path.

## Regression Test Plan (if applicable)

- Coverage level that should have caught this:
  - [x] Unit test
  - [ ] Seam / integration test
  - [ ] End-to-end test
  - [ ] Existing coverage already sufficient
- Target test or file: `src/agents/pi-embedded-subscribe.unsubscribe-fallback.test.ts`
- Scenario the test should lock in: `subscribeEmbeddedPiSession.unsubscribe()` always emits exactly one terminal lifecycle event (`phase:"end"` or `phase:"error"`) via both `emitAgentEvent` and `params.onAgentEvent`, regardless of whether the underlying session ever delivered `agent_end`. Idempotent with `handleAgentEnd`. Respects `setTerminalLifecycleMeta` overrides.
- Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail: Pinning the contract at the subscription seam directly prevents the race; covers every caller of `subscribeEmbeddedPiSession`, not just the timeout path.
- Existing test that already covers this (if any): None. `pi-embedded-subscribe.handlers.lifecycle.test.ts` covers `handleAgentEnd` only.
- If no new test is added, why not: N/A — new test added.

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

- Control UI / Gateway Dashboard chats no longer get stuck on `Stop` after embedded run timeouts or aborts that race past `agent_end`. Stuck runs now finalize as `state:"final"` (or `state:"error"` if the last assistant message recorded an error stopReason) with `livenessState:"abandoned"` and `replayInvalid:true` so observability/replay paths can distinguish a synthesized terminal from a clean one. No config or default changes.

## Diagram (if applicable)

```text
Before:
[timeout] → abortRun(true) → void activeSession.abort()
   ↓ (sync)
finally: unsubscribe() removes listener
   ↓ (later, lost race)
pi-agent: handleRunFailure → processEvents("agent_end") → no listeners → ∅
   ↓
gateway never sees phase:end/error → UI stuck on Stop

After:
[timeout] → abortRun(true) → void activeSession.abort()
   ↓ (sync)
finally: unsubscribe()
   → emitFallbackTerminalLifecycle(ctx)   ← synthesizes phase:end (or error)
   → sessionUnsubscribe()
   ↓
gateway finalizeLifecycleEvent → emitChatFinal → state:"final"
   ↓
UI clears chatRunId → Stop button gone

## Summary

Three new plugin skills that close the full task lifecycle loop for vault-pkm users:

- **`vault-pkm:add-task`** — Fast task capture from a title. Parses priority shorthands (`h`/`high`, `u`/`urgent`) and due dates, runs a semantic duplicate check before creating, and uses the `task` template for consistent frontmatter.
- **`vault-pkm:triage-tasks`** — Surfaces pending/active tasks as a numbered list with `[priority]` labels and ⚡ git completion hints. Accepts shorthand batch updates in a single reply (e.g. `1,3 done | 2 active | 4 cancel`). Defaults to current project, supports `all` scope.
- **`vault-pkm:tackle-task`** — Works a task end-to-end: reads the task note, explores vault context (linked ADRs, recent activity, git log), classifies complexity into trivial/standard/significant, routes to the appropriate workflow, and closes the task (`status: done` + completion timestamp) when finished.

## Motivation

Tasks were frequently left as `pending` after completion because there was no proactive workflow for reviewing and updating them. The `triage-tasks` skill surfaces stale tasks with git hints; `tackle-task` enforces the open→active→done lifecycle on every task worked.

## Eval results

All three skills were evaluated with the skill-creator framework (with-skill vs. without-skill subagent runs):

| Skill | With-skill pass rate | Baseline pass rate | Delta |
|---|---|---|---|
| add-task | 0.917 | 0.917 | +0.000 (assertions need improvement — key differentiators are duplicate check and full title preservation) |
| triage-tasks | 0.750 | 0.333 | **+0.417** |
| tackle-task | 1.000 | 0.556 | **+0.444** |

## Test plan

- [ ] `/reload-plugins` in Claude Code to pick up the new skills
- [ ] `vault-pkm:add-task` — capture a task with a title and priority, verify duplicate detection fires on a second identical capture
- [ ] `vault-pkm:triage-tasks` — run for current project, verify numbered list with ⚡ hints, reply with shorthand and verify frontmatter updates
- [ ] `vault-pkm:tackle-task` — run on a trivial task (verify no brainstorming invoked) and a significant task (verify brainstorming/design questions surface before code)

author: larryliang-inetsoft
body:
## Root Cause Analysis

`UsersSettingsPageComponent` tracks a pending passwordless new user via `newUserIdentity`. Several existing actions already guard against this state before proceeding:

- **`newUser()`** (line 211) — checks `newUserIdentity`, opens a confirmation dialog, and only calls `createNewUser()` after the user confirms deletion of the incomplete entry
- **`selectionChanged()`** (line 156) — same check when clicking a different tree node
- **`changeProvider()`** (line 147) — silently clears the incomplete user when switching providers
- **`usersSettingsSaveGuard`** — fires on Angular route deactivation

However, **`newGroup()`** and **`newRole()`** made the HTTP call unconditionally, with no check for `newUserIdentity`. Clicking either button while a passwordless new user existed silently created the group/role, refreshed the tree (causing the new user to be persisted without a password), and showed no warning at all.

## Fix

Extracted the HTTP requests from both `newGroup()` and `newRole()` into private `createNewGroup()` / `createNewRole()` helpers, then applied the same guard as `newUser()` to both public methods:

## Summary
Polish pass after first design review of the rebuilt onboarding, plus a menu consolidation.

### Persona card — type hierarchy
Three Fraunces elements at similar sizes were competing. Now three distinct typographic roles:
- **Mono caps** — role + publication, "— Brief" label
- **Serif** — brief (editor's voice), screen headline
- **Sans** — name (SF Pro 20/500, bio metadata)

Headline drops 30 → 26 so the brief is the largest serif. Card content is vertical-centered (`justify-content:center`) so the void below the brief disappears.

### Carousel debounce
Active-index updates fired on every scroll tick, flickering the dots mid-flight during inertial scroll. Debounced to ~80ms after the last scroll event so the dot only updates once the snap settles.

### Spacing around the pager
- Pager → switch line: 6px → 14px
- Switch line → CTA: 14px → 22px (CTA gains explicit margin-top)

### Terms screen
- `"What you're agreeing to."` widowed `to.` on its own line. Replaced with `"Before you begin."` — fits one line, in voice.
- `THE TERMS` eyebrow dropped for consistency with the other onboarding screens.

Toggle gone. AI is on for everyone. The `aiEnabled` constant stays in `App.jsx` so the `aiEnabled && …` call sites still resolve; the localStorage key is no longer read or written. Re-introduce a setter when the toggle returns.

## Summary

Adds the celebratory layer playtests kept calling out: positive feedback as the solution progresses, plus a moment of real ceremony when the pair solves it.

### Two states

**Partial** — fires every time you make tangible progress.
- Builder: Test-solution submission with ≥1 correct → confetti burst over the canvas + the existing arpeggio.

author: adsharma
body:
Detect CSR-compatible rowid projections in the Arrow collector path and attach CSR metadata directly to ArrowQueryResult instead of rebuilding it later from a materialized row result.

This adds collector-side tracking for:
- src,dst rowid projections
- src,rel,dst rowid projections

The Arrow result still preserves any additional projected columns in the Arrow table, while exposing CSR metadata alongside the chunked Arrow batches for the relationship-shaped prefix.

On the Python side, query_as_arrow() now maps to the native Arrow execution path and the dedicated Arrow result type in the submodule can read CSR from ArrowQueryResult metadata without going through the older row-oriented QueryResult path.

CSR metadata is intentionally dropped when multiple local Arrow collectors merge, because unordered fan-in would make the grouped CSR structure invalid.

## Change

const hasMissInSession = Array.isArray(sessionState.misses) && sessionState.misses.length > 0;

<!-- START COPILOT ORIGINAL PROMPT -->



<details>

<summary>Original prompt</summary>

## Bug

The app is crashing with:

```
ReferenceError: hasMissInSession is not defined
    at buildDirectiveQueue (file:///var/task/api/reflection-coach.js:2066:5)
```

## Root Cause

`hasMissInSession` is used inside `buildDirectiveQueue` (around line 2066, in the `honest_why_growth` directive condition) but is never declared inside that function. It is declared in two other places — `buildSessionContext` and the handler body — but those are separate scopes.

## Fix

Add a single line inside `buildDirectiveQueue`, right after the existing `mergedChecklist` derivation (around line 1780):

```js

```

This mirrors the identical expression used in both `buildSessionContext` and the handler body. Place it near the other derived locals at the top of `buildDirectiveQueue` (alongside `mergedChecklist`, `mostlyKeptCheckin`, etc.).

**Do not change any other logic.** This is a one-line addition only.

The following is the prior conversation context from the user's chat exploration (may be truncated):

User: okay I like this idea, and I want this implemented in both wins and honest. let's make it a separate question to ask in the workflow for both. and there should be a max of 3 of these questions for each wins and honest, based on ai's idea of most important, or some other metric we can track.

and then look at how we already update whys with why whys array when we create a commitment and ask them why it's importnat, and I think we should add the same or similar thing here with how the why can be updated, changed, or improved, or added upon over time based on the cumulative response to these types of questions. 

Assistant: Good, I have the full picture now. Let me also check the honest stage's kept expansion directive to understand the parallel structure there.

Assistant: Good, I have the full picture now. Let me lay out the complete design before making the PR:

---

## Full Design

### The Core Mechanic: `why_probe` questions

A new concept: **why-probes** are questions that use the user's existing whys as premises — testing, challenging, or deepening them in real conversation. They're distinct from both the wins collection and the honest depth probe.

**Scoring what to ask (the max-3 selection):** For each goal that has a relevant win or miss surfaced this session, assign a score based on:
- **Has a fragment with a stated why context** → highest score (the why is specific and recent)
- **Has a profile why that's shallow (original only, short text)** → medium (good candidate to deepen)
- **motivation_signal is "low", "struggling", or "unknown"** → boost (more valuable to probe)
- **Goal hasn't been mentioned in 7+ days** → boost

AI picks top 3 from that ranked list, asks them sequentially (one per turn), not all at once.

### State tracking

Add two new session state fields:
- `wins_why_probes_remaining: number` — starts at the count selected (≤3), decrements each time one is asked
- `honest_why_probes_remaining: number` — same

And in `extracted_data`, a new field:
- `goal_why_probe_insight: { goal_id, text, action, replace_index }` — same write-back structure as `goal_why_insight`, but with `source: 'why_probe'` — a new source bucket

### Why source: `why_probe`

Currently sources are: `original`, `commitment_planning`, `reflection_session`, `evolve_pass`

Add: **`why_probe`** — max 2 retained per goal, oldest pruned (sits alongside `MAX_SESSION_WHYS` under the `MAX_WHYS_TOTAL` cap)

The write-back logic is identical to `goal_why_insight` — replace if deeper, add if distinct, skip if nothing meaningful. The AI sets `goal_why_probe_insight` instead of `goal_why_insight` to keep the signal source clean.

### Where they fire

**`wins_why_probe` directive:**
- Fires in `wins` stage after `wins_asked_for_more` is true (wins are collected)
- Condition: `wins_why_probes_remaining > 0` and goals with relevant context exist
- Instruction: pick the most important goal from the ranked list, use the why-as-premise pattern, expect a real answer
- Fires once per turn, decrements counter

**`honest_why_probe` directive:**
- Fires in `honest` stage after the core honest depth beat is satisfied (`honest_depth: true`)
- Same ranked list logic, using misses and blockers as context instead of wins
- Same max-3, same write-back

### The question pattern in the instructions

> *"You said this was about [their stated why]. When you actually [did/didn't do X today] — did that hold true, or has something shifted for you?"*

Or for a shallow/original why with no recent signal:
> *"You said [goal] matters because [why]. Is that still the reason — or has it become something else?"*

The AI evaluates the response and decides replace/add/skip just like it does today with goal_why_insight.

author: railway-app[bot]
body:
## Problem

Long-distance and cross-network WebRTC calls were failing or degrading due to insufficient TURN server coverage (only a single open-relay provider with no TCP/TLS fallback), an ICE candidate pool of 10 (too small for fast gathering), no ICE gathering timeout, no ICE restart retry logic, and no mobile network awareness. UDP-blocking mobile carriers and symmetric NAT environments had no viable relay path.

## Solution

Expanded the ICE server configuration in `webrtc-service.ts` with a layered multi-provider strategy: 9 STUN endpoints (Google ×5, Cloudflare, Mozilla, Blackberry, stunprotocol), Metered TURN on UDP 80/3478 + TCP 443 + TLS 443, Twilio TURN on UDP/TCP/TLS with env-configurable credentials, and a Numb/Citrix fallback. Raised the ICE candidate pool from 10 to 50. Added a 20-second ICE gathering timeout with diagnostic logging, a 30-second WebRTC handshake timeout with auto-cleanup, and up to 3 ICE restart attempts on disconnection. Mobile networks are detected via `navigator.connection` and user-agent — TCP/TLS TURN endpoints are moved to the front of the list and video is reduced to 640×480 @ 15fps. mDNS candidates (`.local` hostnames) are filtered to prevent LAN IP leaks. Created `useWebRTC.ts` as a clean React hook exposing call state, streams, and ICE diagnostics. Updated `socket-signaling.ts` to relay `webrtc-ice-restart` events, log ICE diagnostic payloads from clients, and run a 30-second server-side handshake watchdog. Added `TURN_STUN_CONFIG.md` with full troubleshooting, regional recommendations, coturn deployment guide, and network diagnostics tips.

### Changes
- **Modified** `cyrus-ui/src/lib/webrtc-service.ts`
- **Created** `cyrus-ui/src/hooks/useWebRTC.ts`
- **Modified** `server/comms/socket-signaling.ts`
- **Created** `TURN_STUN_CONFIG.md`

The case study page headings used raw `clamp()` values that vastly exceeded the site's design token scale, making project deep-dives feel visually disconnected from the landing, projects listing, and resume pages.

Multiple layered overrides (including `!important` blocks) set case study headings well beyond `--font-size-hero: 3.75rem`:

author: pedapudi
body:
## Summary

PR #294's audit flagged `DefaultSteerer._active_session` as a real
cross-session hazard but didn't fix it. Empirical evidence in
`/tmp/demo-v14.log`: v14 PlanRevised events stamped with v12's
`run_id` because the shared Steerer's instance attribute leaked
across the two sessions' refine windows.

This PR swaps the plain attribute for a per-instance
`contextvars.ContextVar`. All four write sites set via tokens; both
read sites read via `.get()`. `asyncio.gather` copies the parent
context into each child task, so concurrent `runner.run` calls
sharing one Steerer keep their session pointers isolated regardless
of how the tasks interleave.

- `_handle_drift`, `_promote_drift_to_steer`, `observe_refine`, and
  the user-steer state-application block now use ContextVar tokens.
- `_span_context_for_planner` + `_emit_planner_refine_validation_failed`
  read from `.get()`.
- Per-instance (not module-level) ContextVar so parallel test cases
  instantiating their own Steerer never collide.

No public API change.

## Test plan

- [x] New regression test `tests/test_steerer_concurrent_sessions.py`
  with three cases:
  1. Two concurrent `observe_refine` blocks each see their own
     session via the planner's span-context provider.
  2. Planner-side drift emitter routes to the calling task's
     session (`run_id` stamped on `DriftDetected`).
  3. ContextVar resets to its default after the block.
- [x] Tests 1 + 2 fail on `origin/main` -- test 2 fails with
  `A-side drift leaked to session B: run_id=run-B, expected run-A`,
  the exact leak shape `/tmp/demo-v14.log` exhibits.
- [x] All 3 tests pass with the fix.
- [x] Full suite: 1442 passed, 103 skipped (no delta).
- [x] `ruff check` + `ruff format --check` clean on changed files.

author: 0x3k
body:
## Summary

- Adds `POST /v1/settings/alpr/disclaimer/ack` (session-only) which records the operator's acknowledgement of the ALPR disclaimer for a declared jurisdiction (`us|eu|uk|ca|au|other`). Mismatched `version` returns 409 with `{error: "disclaimer_version_mismatch", current_version}`; the happy path persists the `version`/`acked_at`/`jurisdiction` triple and emits an `alpr_disclaimer_ack` audit row.
- Updates the `PUT /v1/settings/alpr` 412 envelope: when `disclaimer` is among the missing prerequisites the response now uses `error: "alpr_disclaimer_required"` and includes `current_version` so the frontend can re-prompt without an extra GET round-trip.
- Adds a new settings key `alpr_disclaimer_acked_jurisdiction` (in `internal/settings`) and surfaces it on `GET /v1/settings/alpr` along with the version-aware `disclaimer_required` flag.
- Bumps `ALPRDisclaimerCurrentVersion` to `2026-04-v1` and converts it from `const` to `var` so tests can simulate a server-side version bump. When a new ack supersedes a prior ack at a different version, the handler also writes a `disclaimer_ack_superseded` audit row capturing the prior `version`/`acked_at`/`jurisdiction` before overwriting.

## Implementation notes

- Built on top of `alpr-config`'s existing `missing_prerequisites: ["disclaimer"]` precondition path -- the change preserves the prerequisites list (so the encryption-key-only case still works) and only specializes the error string + `current_version` when disclaimer is involved.
- Audit rows are stamped with the session user via `actorFromContext` (mirrors the existing `requesterFromContext` pattern in `route_data_request.go`); JWT callers get a NULL actor (this endpoint is session-only so JWT should never reach it, but the audit row stays honest if it does).
- Audit-log writes are tolerant of failure (logged, not propagated) so a transient DB blip can't refuse a legitimate ack -- the audit log is observability, not a hard invariant.

## Test plan

- [x] `go test ./internal/api/... -run "ALPR|AckDisclaimer"` -- 27 subtests, all pass
- [x] `go test ./internal/settings/...` -- pass
- [x] `go vet ./...` -- clean
- [x] `gofmt -l .` -- clean
- [x] Acceptance criterion #8 covered: ack with mismatched version => 409; PUT enabled=true without ack => 412 with `disclaimer_required` shape; PUT enabled=true with stale version after constant bump => 412; happy path (ack then enable) => 200; toggle off/on within version does NOT re-prompt
- [x] Acceptance criterion #9 covered: `alpr_audit_log` records `alpr_disclaimer_ack` with `{jurisdiction, version}` payload on every successful ack; supersede row written only when a prior ack at a different version existed
- [ ] Manual end-to-end against a running backend + Postgres (deferred until the frontend `alpr-settings-onboarding-ui` feature lands)

body:
## Summary

- CPUがエネルギーをつけられず攻撃できなかったバグを修正
- EASY / NORMAL / HARD / ML（PPO強化学習）の4段階CPU難易度をAPI・UIに追加
- PPO強化学習のための学習実行スクリプトと依存ライブラリ整備

## 変更内容

### バグ修正
- `cpu/cpu_ai.py`: `_attach_energy_normal` / `_attach_energy_smart` でエネルギーカードを `evolution_stage == "エネルギー"` のみで検索していたが、デッキビルダー経由のカードは `card_type == "energy"` で `evolution_stage = None` のため未検出。`card_type == "energy"` も条件に追加し修正

### バックエンド
- `cpu/cpu_runtime.py`: `CpuRuntime` に `fixed_mode` / `fixed_model_path` を追加しセッション別CPU戦略を固定可能に。EASY難易度も追加
- `cpu/game_session.py`: `_cpu_runtimes` dict を追加してゲームセッションに `CpuRuntime` を紐付けて保持
- `api/game.py`: `StartGameRequest` に `cpu_difficulty` フィールドを追加。ゲーム開始時にCPUランタイムを生成してセッションに紐付け
- `cpu/train.py`: **新規作成** — PPO学習の実行スクリプト（`python -m cpu.train`）
- `requirements.txt`: `torch`, `stable-baselines3`, `gymnasium`, `numpy` を追加

### フロントエンド
- デッキ選択画面にCPU難易度チップ選択UI（🟢かんたん / 🟡ふつう / 🔴むずかしい / 🤖AI学習済み）を追加
- `game-api.service.ts` の `startGame()` に `cpuDifficulty` パラメータを追加

## ML学習の実行方法

```bash
cd pokeca/backend
pip install torch stable-baselines3 gymnasium numpy
python -m cpu.train  # cpu/models/ppo_final.zip に保存される
```

学習後、UIで「AI（学習済み）」を選択すると PPO モデルが使用される（モデル未生成時は HARD にフォールバック）。

## Test plan

- [ ] CPUがターン開始後にエネルギーをつけ、数ターン後に攻撃することを確認
- [ ] デッキ選択画面で難易度チップが4種類表示される
- [ ] EASY: ランダム行動でゆるい動きになる
- [ ] HARD: 積極的に攻撃・進化する
- [ ] ML（未学習）: HARD にフォールバックされることを確認
- [ ] `python -m cpu.train --envs 2 --phase1 10000 --phase2 10000` が完走しモデルが生成される

body:
## Summary

Canonicalize two v0.9.1 retro lessons into the `.pipeline-templates/` shape. No framework code touched — pipeline-template + docs only.

| Issue | Action Tracker | Gate |
|---|---|---|
| #1173 | #181 | Stage 5 forbids CHANGELOG edits; Stage 9 (feature) / Stage 5 (ship) is the canonical CHANGELOG commit boundary |
| #1174 | #182 | bugfix-state.json Stage 6 mandates 3 clean full-suite runs for pollution-class fixes |

Closes #1173
Closes #1174

## Why

**Two-commit shape (#1173)**: v0.9.1 PRs #1163 + #1164 ran two implementer agents concurrently on the same checkout. Both edited `[Unreleased]`; the first commit captured the second's CHANGELOG hunks. Stage 11 caught it as a 🔴. Three subsequent v0.9.1 PRs (#1166, #1168, #1170) used the two-commit shape and shipped clean. Encoding it as a template gate prevents the regression class.

**3-clean-runs (#1174)**: v0.9.1 PR #1159 (the #1134 bisect) caught a hidden second polluter (`sys.modules` rebind) on the third verification run. Single-run pass is insufficient for pollution-class fixes by definition. Lives in `bugfix-state.json` because feature-state.json hardcodes `pipeline_type: \"feature\"` — the conditional would be unreachable there.

## Changes

- `.pipeline-templates/feature-state.json` — Stage 5 forbids CHANGELOG; Stage 9 docs-only gate added.
- `.pipeline-templates/bugfix-state.json` (new) — clone of feature with `pipeline_type: \"bugfix\"` + Stage 6 3-clean-runs gate.
- `.pipeline-templates/ship-state.json` — Stage 5 (Documentation) marked as canonical CHANGELOG commit boundary; docs-only gate added for symmetric protection on ship-pipelines.
- `.pipeline-templates/README.md` — document all three gates with provenance back to v0.9.1 retro Action Tracker #181/#182.

## Stage 11 review notes

Initial review (2025-04-27) found 3 🔴:
- R1: conditional Stage 6 was unreachable in feature-state.json (hardcoded `pipeline_type: \"feature\"`). Fixed in `499c0249` — removed from feature, created bugfix-state.json.
- R2: PR title `(closes #N, closes #M)` syntax doesn't auto-close. Fixed in this PR body — explicit `Closes #1173` / `Closes #1174` lines.
- R3: ship-state.json retained permissive language. Fixed in `499c0249` — symmetric Stage 5 gates added.

🟡 follow-up filed for executor-side programmatic enforcement (post-stage hooks).

## Test plan

- [x] `jq . .pipeline-templates/{feature,bugfix,ship}-state.json` all valid
- [x] Stage 11 reviewer agent verified diff integrity + all three template files
- [ ] Future v0.9.2 drain PRs honor the new gates (verified by next iteration)

body:
## What
Public `/contact-the-board` form (name, street, message) persists to Convex, emails board via Resend (`bcc` to configured recipients, `to` from `RESEND_TO`). Board-only admin page for recipient list and read-only submission log.

## Deploy notes
Set `RESEND_API_KEY`, `RESEND_FROM`, and `RESEND_TO` on the Convex deployment. Nuxt `.env` alone will not feed the action.

## Chaos interlude
The scheduled job was theoretically fine but also theoretically asleep. The action now does the save and the send in one breath so Resend stops ghosting us in the dashboard.

`RESEND_TO` is not your enemy; it is legally distinct from the board BCC list and mostly exists because email APIs have opinions.

Residents get a generic toast on failure. Admins get error codes that decode into human sentences. Everyone wins except spam bots (v1 intentionally does not invite them to the party).

author: oagr
body:
## Summary

Adds a deterministic Wikidata-QID gate inside `suggestUrls()` that drops candidate URLs whose primary subject doesn't match the parent entity. QUA-650's retro-scan caught 76 system-wide verdicts where this pattern hit *after* the fact (e.g. xAI press releases attached to Anthropic funding-rounds); this gate catches the same shape at suggest time, before storage.

Fail-open by design — if either QID is unknown the candidate passes — mirroring the `relevance-gate` / QUA-426 contract. The LLM verify step downstream remains the backstop.

## Changes

- `crux/lib/sourcing/wikidata-matcher.ts` — new `extractQidFromHtml()` so a candidate URL can be checked against pre-fetched HTML (`<link rel>`, `sameAs`, body links).
- `crux/lib/sourcing/subject-identity-gate.ts` (new) — pure gate function; takes any candidate shape with `{ url, html? }`. Accepts a `null` entity QID (full fail-open).
- `crux/lib/sourcing/entity-wikidata-qid.ts` (new) — looks up the parent entity's QID from `data/external-links.yaml`. The ticket's `entities.wikidata` / `wikidata_qid` columns don't actually exist; `external-links.yaml` is the source-of-truth.
- `crux/lib/sourcing/suggest-urls.ts` — accepts `entityWikidataQid`, returns `subjectMismatches[]` for observability. Gate runs after dedup+cap; doesn't backfill from providers (that belongs in the unified pipeline, QUA-722).
- `crux/commands/sourcing-suggest-urls.ts` — looks up the entity's QID per verdict row, plumbs it into `suggestUrls`, prints `[subject-mismatch]` lines and bumps a new `subject_mismatches_dropped` summary counter.

## Acceptance from the ticket

- [x] New gate in `crux/lib/sourcing/suggest-urls.ts`
- [x] Mismatched-QID candidate dropped with `subject-mismatch` reason
- [x] Matching-QID candidate passes
- [x] Null-on-either-side ⇒ pass (fail-open)
- [x] Logging captures dropped candidates with detail for observability (per-record `[subject-mismatch]` log line + summary counter)
- [x] Smoke can be run via `crux sourcing-suggest-urls --entity=anthropic --verdict=contradicted --dry-run` — gate exercises Anthropic's QID `Q108542504` lookup. (Dry-run skips network so HTML-fetch path is untested in dry-run; URL-mode mismatches show in the log.)

## Out of scope (per ticket)

- Retro-sweep over the 76 existing contradicted verdicts → sibling ticket
- Wider entity QID backfill (records without a QID stay fail-open)
- Pre-fetching HTML inside `suggestUrls` itself — that fetch belongs in the unified pipeline (QUA-722) at step 5; the gate accepts pre-fetched HTML via the candidate's optional `html` field

## Test plan

- [x] `pnpm vitest run crux/lib/sourcing/{subject-identity-gate,wikidata-matcher,suggest-urls,entity-wikidata-qid}.test.ts crux/commands/sourcing-suggest-urls.test.ts` — 88 tests pass (24 new)
- [x] Full sourcing test surface: `pnpm vitest run crux/lib/sourcing/ crux/commands/sourcing-suggest-urls.test.ts` — 569 tests pass
- [x] `pnpm crux w validate gate --fix` — 61 checks pass, 4 pre-existing advisory warnings unrelated

Fixes QUA-724

author: komainu8
body:
Update compiler flags to -std=c++20 from -std=c++17.
Because since version 24.0.0, Apache Arrow requires "std::span", which was introduced in C++20.
Ref: apache/arrow@df9dbbc

This change resolves the following error in Autotools workflow:

```
/usr/include/arrow/buffer.h:239:8: error: 'span' in namespace 'std' does not name a template type
  239 |   std::span<const T> span_as() const {
      |        ^~~~
/usr/include/arrow/buffer.h:239:3: note: 'std::span' is only available from C++20 onwards
  239 |   std::span<const T> span_as() const {
      |   ^~~
/usr/include/arrow/buffer.h:272:8: error: 'span' in namespace 'std' does not name a template type
  272 |   std::span<T> mutable_span_as() {
      |        ^~~~
/usr/include/arrow/buffer.h:272:3: note: 'std::span' is only available from C++20 onwards
  272 |   std::span<T> mutable_span_as() {
      |   ^~~
```

Additionally, use C++17 as the minimum standard, falling back from C++20 where unavailable.
Because we use C++17 as the default version in CMake.

Since the "AX_CXX_COMPILE_STDCXX_20" macro was not being expanded correctly,
I changed the syntax to "AX_CXX_COMPILE_STDCXX([20], ...)" to ensure proper macro expansion.

body:
## Summary

The repo had been dormant for ~5 years. Three things had killed the deployment: Heroku free dynos were retired (Nov 2022), Node 10 is EOL, and idle MongoDB Atlas free clusters get deleted after ~120 days. This PR brings everything back to a deployable state on **Render's free tier** with a **fresh MongoDB Atlas M0 cluster**, with the **smallest set of dependency upgrades** required to build on Node 20.

- Backend now runs on Node 20 with Mongoose 7, JWT 9, Express 4.21, Socket.io 4.7. Env-driven config (no committed secrets), boot fails fast in production if `CORS_ORIGIN` is unset, SPA fallback so `/leaderboard` no longer 404s on hard refresh.
- Frontend builds on Node 20 with react-scripts 5 + axios 1 + socket.io-client 4.7. React 17 / antd 4 / Redux classic / react-router 5 are intentionally untouched (out of scope per "minimum to deploy"). Hardcoded Heroku URLs replaced with same-origin via `REACT_APP_API_URL`.
- New `render.yaml` blueprint, `.nvmrc`, `.env.example`, plus a GitHub Actions CI job (lint + format + frontend build).

## Out of scope (intentionally deferred)

- React 18/19, antd 5, Redux Toolkit, react-router 6 migrations
- TypeScript migration (CI's typecheck step is therefore N/A; only lint + format + build run)
- `react-native-leaderboard` removal (it's an RN package on the web — works at build time but flag for runtime cleanup if it errors)
- Pre-existing `register`/`login` error-handling that swallows DB save failures
- Custom domain wiring

## Test plan

- [ ] CI green on this PR (lint + format:check + frontend build)
- [ ] Locally: `nvm use && npm install && npm install --prefix frontend && npm run build --prefix frontend` succeeds
- [ ] Locally: `cp .env.example .env`, fill `MONGO_URI` + `SECRET_OR_KEY`, `npm run dev` starts both servers
- [ ] Locally: register a new user, log in, log out
- [ ] Locally: open two browser windows, both join an online game, place pieces, win condition fires
- [ ] Locally: chat messages persist across refresh
- [ ] After merge: Render Blueprint creates the service from `render.yaml`; `MONGO_URI` and `CORS_ORIGIN` filled in the dashboard; first deploy goes green
- [ ] Production: hard refresh `/leaderboard` returns the SPA, not a 404 (verifies `app.get("*", ...)` fallback)
- [ ] Production: Socket.io upgrades to `wss://` in DevTools

## Reviewer notes

- Squash-merge per repo convention; commit history on the branch is split by area (backend / frontend / infra / docs).
- Independent code-reviewer pass already flagged and addressed: build-time devDeps stripping by Render's `NODE_ENV=production` (sass + ajv moved to `dependencies`, plus `NPM_CONFIG_PRODUCTION=false` set in `render.yaml`); CORS fail-fast added; passport `User` lookup now via direct require.

body:
## Summary

Implements the complete onboarding/discovery intake form pipeline that feeds into Fluency Blueprint automation. This is Phase 5 of the brief→fulfillment workflow, enabling PMAs to submit property details, brand assets, and marketing preferences through a structured anti-slop form that validates completeness, detects AI-generated content, and routes gaps to Community Managers for verification.

## Key Changes

**Onboarding Routes & State Machine**
- New `routes/onboarding.py` with 8 endpoints for intake submission, state transitions, manager name derivation, color extraction, and asset uploads
- `onboarding_state.py` implements a 10-stage lifecycle state machine with legal transition validation and SLA breach detection
- Stateless helpers for deriving RPM manager names from email convention (`first.last@rpmliving.com` → "First Last")

**Gap Review Engine**
- `gap_review.py` scores intake form completeness per field, validates forced-fact fields (concession amounts, occupancy percentages, email formats), detects typos via extended dictionary, and runs Claude Haiku as an AI-slop classifier on free-text fields
- Generates structured gap questions for Community Manager portal response form
- Integrates with HubSpot workflow automation via property triggers (no direct task API calls)

**Blueprint Asset Pipeline**
- `blueprint_assets.py` handles logo/hero photo validation, resizing to Fluency-required variants, color extraction via k-means clustering, and HubSpot Files CDN upload
- Logos must be transparent PNG; heroes must be ≥1200px on shortest side
- Extracted brand colors (primary/secondary) stored in HubDB for PMA/CSM approval workflow

**ILS Research Integration**
- `ils_research.py` fetches and extracts structured data from public listing sites (apartments.com, zillow, rent.com, etc.)
- Graceful failure pattern: blocked requests or parse errors return empty dict, brief drafter proceeds with available context
- Real resident review excerpts used as anti-slop grounding for AI brief generation

**Fluency Exporter**
- `fluency_exporter.py` abstract interface supporting Phase 1 (CSV/sFTP) and Phase 2 (REST API) exports
- Handles Fluency's match-type syntax (`|exact|`, `"phrase"`, `broad`, `-negative`)
- Serializes HubDB state (keywords, variables, tags, assets) to Blueprint-compatible format

**Frontend & Templates**
- `onboarding-intake.html` form with 6-layer anti-slop architecture: system pull, structured picks, AI strawman + this-or-that, artifact upload, forced-fact fields, free text
- `onboarding-intake.js` wires form to Flask API with live manager name preview, logo color swatch extraction, and multi-step submission
- CSS styling in `client-portal.html` and dedicated `onboarding-intake.css`

**HubSpot Integration**
- `create_onboarding_properties.py` provisions 12 company properties (status enum, timestamps, CM/RM contacts, gap-review workflow triggers)
- `create_hubdb_onboarding_tables.py` creates 5 HubDB tables: intake submissions, gap responses, Blueprint variables/tags/assets
- Workflow spec in `HUBSPOT_GAP_REVIEW_WORKFLOW.md` documents the 3-stage email escalation (CM → RM → escalate)

**Deployment & Documentation**
- `provision_onboarding_pipeline.sh` orchestrates credential validation, property creation, and table provisioning
- `ONBOARDING_DEPLOYMENT_RUNBOOK.md` step-by-step checklist for production rollout
- `FLUENCY_OUTREACH_EMAIL.md` template for coordinating with Fluency on ingestion path
- Sample CSVs in `docs/fluency-samples/` for Fluency validation before live export

**Testing**
- Unit tests for state machine transitions, gap review validators, asset validation/resize, keyword formatting, ILS provider detection, and name derivation
- Auth coverage tests updated to include onboarding context resolver

## Summary

- Adds `repo-analyze-full`, `repo-analyze-quick-full`, and `repo-analyze-strict-full` — full-coverage siblings of the existing repo-analyze skills that dispatch one Sonnet swarm agent per audit section (15 sections, max 5 concurrent agents per wave) so every file is analyzed instead of a sampled subset
- Adds `worktree-cleanup` — audits every git worktree, classifies it into one of five states (`CLEAN_PRUNE_OK` / `NEEDS_COMMIT` / `NEEDS_PUSH` / `NEEDS_PR` / `KEEP`), prunes safe worktrees, and prints exact remediation commands for the rest — never deletes branches (that is `gh tidy`'s exclusive responsibility)
- Updates `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` and `plugin.json` to register all four new skills

## Design Decisions

- **`-full` variants are separate skill files, not flags** — users who want sampling keep the existing skills; users who want full coverage invoke the `-full` sibling
- **One Sonnet agent per audit section** — 15 sections → 3 waves of 5 agents (respects the Myrmidon swarm 5-concurrent constraint); each agent reads every file in its bucket via `Read` with `offset/limit` chunking if needed
- **`worktree-cleanup` never deletes branches** — branch deletion authority stays exclusively with `gh tidy`; `worktree-cleanup` only runs `git worktree remove` (no `--force`) and defers all destructive ops to the user via printed commands
- **3-method audit pattern** from ProjectMnemosyne `git-worktree-cleanup-preservation-audit` v1.0.0 embedded verbatim: PR state → patch-id (`git cherry`) → tree diff

author: runnel
body:
## Summary

Addresses voog-mcp code-review follow-up **#6**: the `_simplify_pages` and `_simplify_products` functions were byte-identical between `voog_mcp/tools/<group>.py` and `voog_mcp/resources/<group>.py`. The modules' docstrings called the duplication "deliberate", but the same docstrings also promised that callers can't tell which surface produced the data — a contract that a single one-sided typo can silently break.

This PR moves the projections to a single source of truth.

## Changes

- New `voog_mcp/projections.py` exposes `simplify_pages`, `simplify_products`, `simplify_articles`, and `simplify_layouts` — pure stdlib, no MCP/client deps.
- `voog_mcp/tools/pages.py`, `voog_mcp/tools/products.py`, `voog_mcp/resources/pages.py`, `voog_mcp/resources/products.py`, `voog_mcp/resources/articles.py`, `voog_mcp/resources/layouts.py` import from `voog_mcp.projections` instead of carrying their own copy.
- Module docstrings updated — the "deliberately duplicated" notes are gone, replaced with pointers to `projections.py`.
- Articles and layouts only had a single caller (resources side), but the four projections sit together so a future tools-side surface gets the same shape for free.

## Why a contract, not just dedup

The duplicated functions weren't just incidental — they were two implementations of the same promise (the "products_list tool and voog://products resource produce identical shapes" promise from PR #30). With two copies, that promise depended on humans remembering to update both at once. With one source, the promise is structural: the tools-side and resources-side imports are pinned to the exact same callable.

## Tests

- New `tests/test_projections.py` — 16 unit tests covering empty inputs, full inputs, missing fields (graceful `.get()`), extra fields (stripped), and the `layout` nested-fallback precedence in `simplify_pages`.
- The PR #30 cross-module invariant test in `tests/test_tools_products.py` is rewritten: instead of comparing byte-equal outputs of two duplicated functions (which becomes vacuous once both call the same import), it asserts structural identity (`products_tools.simplify_products is projections.simplify_products`) plus a heavy-field-stripping check.
- `tests/test_tools_pages.py`'s two `_simplify_pages` tests now reference the shared `voog_mcp.projections.simplify_pages`.

**409 tests pass** (was 392 — added 16 unit tests in `test_projections.py` plus 1 net-add in `test_tools_products.py`).

## Test plan

- [x] `.venv/bin/python -m unittest discover tests` → green
- [ ] Reviewer to spot-check that no tools/* or resources/* file has a stray local `_simplify_*` left behind (search: `_simplify_`)

author: arxialayer1
body:
# Commit 040 — `arxia-proto::validate_transport_frame_bytes` pre-decode size cap

**Severity:** high
**Bug reference:** PHASE1_AUDIT_REPORT.md ID **HIGH-010**
**Scope:** `crates/arxia-proto/src/{lib.rs, validation.rs}` only.

## Vulnerability

`arxia-proto` exposes prost-generated wire types (TransportFrame,
GossipEnvelope, NonceSync*, Ping, Vote, etc.) but had no
pre-decode size validation. The audit (HIGH-010):

> **Attack:** send a 4 GB `bytes payload` in a frame.
> **Impact:** prost decoder allocates; OOM.
> **Exploitability:** trivial.
> **Suggested fix direction:** wrap decode in a length-prefixed
> reader with a hard cap (e.g., 2 × LoRa MTU for a single frame;
> 1 MB for a batch frame), reject larger.

A peer that sends 4 GB of bytes claiming to be a TransportFrame
forces every receiving node to allocate that buffer before prost
even attempts to parse it. Parse failure is a DoS amplifier
because the allocation already happened.

The fix lives in `arxia-proto` so every transport binding
(`arxia-transport`, future LoRa / BLE / SMS adapters) inherits
the same protocol-level limit and the same validator.

## Fix

Add a new module `validation.rs` that exposes a pure-bytes
validator callable BEFORE `prost::Message::decode`:

```rust
pub const MAX_TRANSPORT_FRAME_BYTES: usize = 1_048_576; // 1 MiB

pub enum ProtoError {
    TransportFrameTooLarge { size: usize, max: usize },
}

pub fn validate_transport_frame_bytes(bytes: &[u8]) -> Result<(), ProtoError> {
    if bytes.len() > MAX_TRANSPORT_FRAME_BYTES {
        return Err(ProtoError::TransportFrameTooLarge {
            size: bytes.len(),
            max: MAX_TRANSPORT_FRAME_BYTES,
        });
    }
    Ok(())
}
```

Re-exported at the crate root so callers do
`arxia_proto::validate_transport_frame_bytes(&bytes)?;` then
`arxia_proto::arxia::TransportFrame::decode(bytes)?`.

### Why pure-bytes validation

The existing build pipeline runs `prost-build` only when `protoc`
is locally available. Without `protoc` (the common case in CI
sandbox / contributor laptop), `arxia.rs` is a stub and no proto
types are compiled. A validator that operates on `&[u8]` works
regardless of protoc availability — it's the **transport layer's
guard**, not the **proto layer's guard**.

Once protoc / the prost-built types land, callers will pair this
validator with `prost::Message::decode` at every transport
ingress site. The validator is the cheapest possible OOM-vector
closure: a single `len()` comparison against the constant.

### Cap value (1 MiB)

Aligned with the audit's batch-frame ceiling. Rationale:
- The largest known single envelope is `NonceSyncResponse` capped
  at ~720 KB by commit 028 (10 000 entries × 72 B each).
- 1 MiB leaves comfortable headroom (≈300 KB) for any future
  envelope additions.
- 1 MiB is far below the 4 GB attack the audit describes — the
  OOM amplifier is closed.

A future per-link tightening (e.g. `MAX_LORA_FRAME_BYTES = 512`)
can be added on top of this protocol-level ceiling without
loosening the global guard.

## Tests added

8 new tests in `arxia_proto::validation::tests`:

- `test_max_transport_frame_bytes_constant` — pin the cap at
  1 MiB. Future revision must update both const and assertion.
- `test_validate_accepts_empty_frame` — boundary: empty slice.
- `test_validate_accepts_small_frame` — realistic 64-byte Ping.
- `test_validate_accepts_realistic_batch_frame` — 720 KB
  (NonceSyncResponse near commit 028's cap).
- `test_validate_accepts_at_max` — boundary: exactly 1 MiB
  (cap is INCLUSIVE — `>`, not `>=`).
- `test_validate_rejects_just_above_max` — off-by-one:
  MAX + 1 must reject.
- `test_validate_rejects_attacker_scale_frame` — **PRIMARY
  HIGH-010 PIN.** 10 MiB attacker payload (the audit cites 4 GB;
  10 MiB is tractable in test memory while still well above the
  cap).
- `test_proto_error_display_format` — Display surface.

`arxia-proto` had **0 tests** before this commit. Total:
0 → 8.

## Order dependency

Standalone. No dependency on commits 023-039. Apply on top of
`ddb728b` directly.

## Breaking change disclosure

**No breaking change.** The new module + symbols are entirely
additive:
- `validation` module (new, public)
- `MAX_TRANSPORT_FRAME_BYTES` constant
- `ProtoError` enum
- `validate_transport_frame_bytes` function

Workspace caller audit:
- 0 callers today. The intended consumer is a future
  `arxia-transport` ingress that sits between the wire bytes and
  `prost::Message::decode`. The validator is exposed and ready.

## Known limitations

- **Validator is purely length-based.** Prost's own decode will
  still produce its own errors on malformed bytes (proto-level
  field mismatch, invalid varints, etc.). This validator only
  closes the OOM amplifier — it does NOT replace prost's
  parse-time checks.
- **No per-link cap.** A future enhancement could add
  `MAX_LORA_FRAME_BYTES = 512` or similar for constrained-link
  per-frame caps. Out of scope for HIGH-010 which is about the
  protocol-level OOM ceiling.
- **Adoption follow-up.** This commit adds the validator;
  wiring it at every `prost::Message::decode` site in
  `arxia-transport` and future LoRa / BLE / SMS adapters is a
  separate commit. The validator is exposed; consumers will
  inherit the cap when they call it.
- **No fuzz harness.** Single-comparison validator;
  exhaustively covered by 6 boundary tests (empty, small,
  realistic, at-max, MAX+1, 10 MiB).
- **HIGH-011 (GossipEnvelope unknown oneof) is the natural next
  step.** It depends on the prost-generated `GossipEnvelope`
  type which requires protoc; queued as commit 041.

Refs: PHASE1_AUDIT_REPORT.md HIGH-010.
