body:
## Description

This Pull Request transforms the Stage 2 Profile Intelligence System into a secure, multi-interface platform. Key implementations include:

- **Authentication**: Secure GitHub OAuth with PKCE support for both CLI and Web clients.
- **Session Management**: Dual-token strategy using short-lived JWT Access Tokens (3 min) and DB-persisted Refresh Tokens (5 min) with immediate rotation.
- **RBAC**: Centralized Role-Based Access Control enforcing `admin` and `analyst` permissions across all endpoints.
- **Security**: 
    - DB-backed sliding-window Rate Limiting (10/min for Auth, 60/min for API).
    - Structured JSON Logging for audit trails (Method, Endpoint, Status, Response Time).
- **API Updates**: 
    - Mandatory API versioning via `X-API-Version: 1` header.
    - Updated HATEOAS pagination shape including `total_pages` and navigation `links`.
    - CSV Profile Export endpoint with specific column ordering.

## Related Issue (Link to issue ticket)
Relates to: **HNG Backend Track - Stage 3 Technical Requirements**

## Motivation and Context
These changes are required to transition the system from a public prototype into a production-ready internal product. It ensures user identity ownership, protects against unauthorized data access, and provides a unified backend that consistently serves the new CLI and Web Portal interfaces.

## How Has This Been Tested?
The system has been verified through a comprehensive automated test suite and manual end-to-end integration:

- **Automated Tests**: 10 tests passed covering:
    - API Versioning enforcement.
    - RBAC logic (Analyst vs Admin access).
    - Rate limit triggers (429 responses).
    - Pagination structure validation.
- **Manual Verification**: 
    - Verified the PKCE flow using the local `insighta-cli`.
    - Confirmed HTTP-only, SameSite:Strict cookie delivery for the web portal.
- **Environment**: Tested against a local PostgreSQL instance and Python 3.12.

## Summary

Surfaces the backend audit (BE-213) on the multisig proposal page. Next to **Approve proposal** there's now a secondary button that:

- **Run audit** — fires `POST /v2/proposals/:id/audit` when no audit is cached on the proposal yet, with a loading state for the ~15–30s round-trip.
- **Show audit** — opens the dialog instantly with the cached audit once one is persisted on the proposal document (no extra cost).

The result is rendered in a dedicated dialog with:
- A colour-coded risk badge (low → green, medium → orange, high / critical → red)
- Summary
- Per-finding cards (severity tag + category + description, plus action index when applicable)
- Recommendations list
- Tenderly trace link

Linear: [APP-625](https://linear.app/aragon/issue/APP-625)
Backend PR: aragon/app-backend#1275 (BE-213)

## Visibility rules

| Proposal state | Has cached audit | Button |
|---|---|---|
| Open | No | **Run audit** |
| Open | Yes | **Show audit** |
| Executed | No | hidden |
| Executed | Yes | **Show audit** (review post-execution) |

## Test plan
- [ ] Open a non-executed multisig proposal that has actions and no cached audit → button reads **Run audit**
- [ ] Click → ~15–30s loading → dialog opens with the audit; refetch flips the button to **Show audit**
- [ ] Click **Show audit** on the same proposal → dialog opens instantly with the cached audit
- [ ] Open an executed proposal with a cached audit → button reads **Show audit**
- [ ] Open an executed proposal with no audit → button is hidden
- [ ] Backend not reachable → request fails cleanly (no UI crash, dialog stays closed)

`config/.env.preview` is temporarily flipped to point at sandbox so the Vercel preview exercises the new audit endpoint. **Revert before merging to main.**

author: rakshitgondwal
body:
## Summary

Pre-public OSS security hygiene, scoped down to one piece:

- **`.github/dependabot.yml`** — weekly version-update PRs for Go modules and for the GitHub Actions used in workflows.

## What this PR does NOT include (intentionally)

- **CodeQL workflow** — code scanning on private repos requires GitHub Advanced Security (paid). On public repos it's free. Plan: enable via **Settings → Code security → Code scanning → default setup** after the repo flips public; that gives you CodeQL with no workflow file. If more configuration is wanted later, the workflow form can come back as a follow-up.
- **`SECURITY.md`** — removed per request; can revisit as a separate change later if needed.
- **govulncheck in CI.** Locally, `govulncheck ./...` against current `main` flags **22 vulnerabilities** the code reaches into — mostly older `golang.org/x/*` and stdlib advisories that need dep bumps to clear. Adding govulncheck to CI today would land main on red. The right order is: merge this → enable repo-level Dependabot → let it open the bump PRs → fix any remaining vulns → then add govulncheck to CI in a follow-up so it stays green.

## Repo-level toggles to enable (UI, not code)

The dependabot.yml is inert until **Settings → Code security → Dependabot version updates** is on. Recommended toggles for the public flip:

- ✅ Dependency graph
- ✅ Automatic dependency submission
- ✅ Dependabot alerts
- ✅ Dependabot malware alerts
- ✅ Dependabot security updates *(opens CVE patch PRs automatically)*
- ✅ Grouped security updates *(one PR per ecosystem when multiple advisories drop simultaneously)*
- ✅ Dependabot version updates
- ❌ Dependabot on self-hosted runners
- ✅ Secret scanning + Push protection *(in the secret-scanning section)*
- ✅ Code scanning → default setup *(after the repo goes public; free for public repos)*

## Test plan
- [ ] Merge this PR.
- [ ] Enable the repo-level toggles above (Code scanning waits until after public).
- [ ] Wait one cycle; confirm Dependabot opens its first wave of PRs (Go modules + Actions).
- [ ] After dep bumps land, open a follow-up PR adding `govulncheck` to ci.yml. CI should stay green.

body:
## Problem

When launching wave-code in a new project and installing a plugin before sending any messages, `recreateAgent()` captures the sessionId, destroys the agent, then calls `initializeAgent(currentSessionId)`. Since no messages have been saved yet, the session file doesn't exist on disk, and `handleSessionRestoration` throws `Session not found`.

## Fix

In `handleSessionRestoration`, when `restoreSessionId` is provided but the session doesn't exist on disk, return `undefined` (starting fresh) instead of throwing. A warning is logged for visibility.

## Changes

- `packages/agent-sdk/src/services/session.ts`: Graceful fallback when session not found
- `packages/agent-sdk/tests/services/session.extra.test.ts`: Update test to verify new behavior

# Diagrama de Clases


```mermaid
classDiagram
    %% Nodos
    class LLNode~T~ {
        -T m_data
        -Ref m_ref
        -Node* m_next
        +getData() T
        +getNext() Node*
    }
    class DLLNode~T~ {
        -Node* m_pPrev
        +getPrev() Node*
    }
    LLNode <|-- DLLNode

    %% Contenedores
    class LinkedList~Trait~ {
        #Node* m_pRoot
        #Node* m_tail
        #size_t m_size
        #shared_mutex m_mtx
        +insert(val, ref)
        +push_front(val, ref)
        +pop_front()
        +ForEach(func)
    }
    class DoubleLinkedList~Trait~ {
        +pop_back()
        +ReverseForEach(func)
    }
    class CircularLinkedList~Trait~ {
        +circularForEach(loops, func)
    }
    class CircularDoubleLinkedList~Trait~ {
        +circularForEach(loops, dir, func)
    }

    LinkedList <|-- DoubleLinkedList
    LinkedList <|-- CircularLinkedList
    DoubleLinkedList <|-- CircularDoubleLinkedList
```

author: khaliqgant
body: ## Summary - Adds `workflows/wave11-flat-layout-collapse/01-collapse-packages-into-src.ts`, a deterministic workflow that collapses the current npm-workspaces layout (`packages/{shared,runtime,product,cloud,local,cli}`) into a single sage-style `src/` tree with topical subfolders and a `src/surfaces/cli/` directory (room for future `slack/`, `web/`, `mac/`). - Drives the migration via TDD: a new `test/flat-layout-proof/` is authored first and runs **RED** on the current layout, the workflow performs the moves + import-rewrite codemod + config consolidation, and only then drives typecheck + full test suite + flat-layout proof to **GREEN** before sign-off. - Replaces (not silently deletes) the existing `test/package-proof/` — the old proof asserts the very layout we are removing, so the new flat-layout proof is its successor. - Layer boundaries are enforced by folder convention only (matching sage). No path aliases, no eslint boundaries plugin. ## Workflow shape DAG with deterministic gates between every agent step: 1. `preflight` — capture before-snapshot, source inventory, and config baselines; refuse if working tree is dirty or `src/` already exists. 2. `write-flat-layout-proof` (test-author) → `red-gate` — assert the new test runs RED and inverts exit code so a passing test here fails the workflow. 3. `write-migration-plan` (migrator) → `plan-gate` — produce a TSV file map; gate verifies every source from the inventory has a destination row. 4. `execute-migration` (migrator) → `migration-structural-gate` — moves via `git mv`, recorded codemod for `@ricky/*` → relative imports, single root `package.json`/`tsconfig.json`/`vitest.config.ts`, deletes `packages/` and `test/package-proof/`, regenerates lockfile. 5. `green-validation` → `fix-loop` (fix) → `green-gate` — 80→100 loop until typecheck + `npm test` + flat-layout proof all exit 0 together. 6. `final-review` (reviewer) → `final-review-pass-gate` → `final-hard-validation` → `signoff`. ## Why a workflow and not a hand migration - Reproducibility: the codemod for the import rewrites is committed to `${artifactDir}/codemod.{mjs,ts}`, so the rewrite is auditable. - Safety: each gate is deterministic; nothing relies on agent self-report. - TDD discipline: the contract for "what flat looks like" lives in the test, not in the workflow prose — so the test survives as the long-term layout proof after the workflow run. ## Test plan - [ ] Code review of the workflow file against `workflows/shared/WORKFLOW_AUTHORING_RULES.md` and `docs/workflows/WORKFLOW_STANDARDS.md`. - [ ] Dry-run: `agent-relay run workflows/wave11-flat-layout-collapse/01-collapse-packages-into-src.ts --dry-run` (or repo-equivalent) to validate step graph and shell expansions. - [ ] On a throwaway branch, run the full workflow and confirm: `src/{shared,runtime,product,cloud,local,surfaces/cli}` populated, `packages/` removed, `test/package-proof/` removed, `test/flat-layout-proof/` present, `npm run typecheck` clean, `npm test` clean, `node bin/ricky --help` works. - [ ] Verify no `@ricky/*` import or `file:../` dep remains in the resulting tree. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) ---

body:
## Resumo

A aba Conteúdo agora é um **calendário diário** começando por **Amanhã**. Cada experiência é atribuída automaticamente ao seu melhor dia de postagem em função da proximidade do evento — o operacional não precisa mais decidir o que postar quando.

## Regra de atribuição (curadoria, sem urgência fake)

| Formato | Quando posta |
|---|---|
| **LinkedIn** | D-5 (descoberta institucional / B2B) |
| **TikTok** | D-4 (descoberta orgânica) |
| **Reels** | D-3 (peça principal de conversão) |
| **Feed** | D-2 (reforço editorial) |
| **Stories** | D-1 (última chamada elegante) |

Se a data ideal já passou (evento muito próximo), o post **cai pra amanhã** com label *"Última chamada · evento amanhã"* / *"Curto prazo · evento em Nd"*. Nunca publicamos no passado.

Experiências **semanais / sem data fixa** viram **evergreen** distribuídas pela semana via hash estável do id (Reels num dia, Feed em outro, Stories num terceiro). Estabilidade do hash garante que toda semana o mesmo evergreen cai em dias diferentes — evita previsibilidade do feed.

## UI

- Cada dia é uma seção com header **"Amanhã · 28/04"** / **"Quarta · 29/04"**
- Contador de posts no header
- Cards filhos com badge de formato + lead label (ex: *"Evento em 3d"*)
- Dias sem post mostram placeholder (visibilidade da semana inteira)
- Filtro de formato continua funcionando (filtra cards dentro do calendário)
- Filtro "Próximos 7/14/30 dias" agora controla só o horizonte visível

## Test plan

- [ ] Abrir admin → Conteúdo → ver primeiro dia rotulado como "Amanhã · DD/MM"
- [ ] Cada experiência cadastrada com data deve aparecer em ~5 dias diferentes (D-5 a D-1)
- [ ] Trocar formato pra "Reels" → ver só Reels no calendário, em D-3
- [ ] Experiências "Semanal" devem aparecer espalhadas, não no mesmo dia
- [ ] Botão "Copiar texto" continua funcionando dentro de cada card

author: kevinguitar
body:
This PR adds a compiler test for generating providers in a generated dependency graph. 
~This PR supports FIR-generated providers to be processed in a generated dependency graph.~

Previously, when you added a provider in a generated graph:
```kotlin
@DependencyGraph
interface FeatureGraph {
  @Provides
  fun provideParam(): String = "foo"
}
```
the compilation would fail with this error:
```
No expected factory class generated for /MyActivity.FeatureGraph.provideParam. Report this bug with a repro case at https://github.com/zacsweers/metro/issues/new. This is possibly a bug in the Metro compiler, please report it with details and/or a reproducer to https://github.com/zacsweers/metro.
org.jetbrains.kotlin.fir.pipeline.IrGenerationExtensionException: No expected factory class generated for /MyActivity.FeatureGraph.provideParam. Report this bug with a repro case at https://github.com/zacsweers/metro/issues/new. This is possibly a bug in the Metro compiler, please report it with details and/or a reproducer to https://github.com/zacsweers/metro.
```
**Edit**: Annotated the dependency graph with `@IROnlyFactories` resolves the issue.

~and this is because when a `@Provides` function is generated by a FIR extension, it's generated at a phase after Metro's `ProvidesFactoryFirGenerator` has already looked at the `classSymbol.declarationSymbols` (is this expected?!) to find provider functions and generate corresponding factory classes.~

~Generating the factory in IR phase (`BindingContainerTransformer`) resolves the issue.~

author: devin-ai-integration[bot]
body: ## Summary Stacks on PRs #1–#5. Gets the backend production-deployable on Fly.io with managed Postgres and tightens the parent-side auth surface. ### Auth hardening - Refresh tokens are now persisted to the existing `RefreshToken` model (sha256-hashed at rest). `/auth/refresh` **rotates**: it issues a new refresh + access pair and revokes the old refresh atomically. Reusing a revoked refresh token is treated as theft and revokes every refresh in that parent's chain. - `/auth/logout` revokes the presented refresh token. - `/auth/password-reset/request` + `/auth/password-reset/confirm` — 30-minute one-shot tokens stored as `PasswordResetToken` (sha256-hashed). Request endpoint always 200's to avoid email enumeration. The reset URL is logged via the notifier console adapter; replace `sendEmail` in `notifier.ts` to dispatch real emails. - `express-rate-limit` on `/auth/register`, `/auth/login`, `/auth/password-reset/request` with deterrent windows (10/hr register, 20/15min login, 5/hr reset). - `app.set("trust proxy", 1)` enabled when `NODE_ENV=production` or `TRUST_PROXY=1` so rate limits and `req.ip` see the real client behind Fly's edge. ### Parent UI - `/audit` — paginated audit log using cursor pagination over `GET /api/audit`. - `/password-reset` (request form) and `/password-reset/confirm` (set-new-password form, accepts `?token=` query). - "Forgot password?" link on the login page. - "Audit" link added to the header alongside "Notifications". ### Deploy infrastructure - `apps/backend/Dockerfile` — multi-stage (deps → build → prod). Uses pnpm workspaces, builds `@getkids/shared` and `@getkids/backend`, ships production deps only. ~150 MB image. - `apps/backend/scripts/start.sh` runs `prisma migrate deploy` and then `node dist/index.js` so the first deploy auto-applies migrations against Fly Postgres. - `apps/backend/fly.toml` — `sin` region (Singapore, closest to target users in Indonesia), `/health` HTTP check, auto-stop machines, `min_machines_running=1`. - `docs/DEPLOY.md` — end-to-end runbook covering the SQLite → Postgres provider switch, Fly app + Postgres provisioning, secret setup, web app static hosting (Vercel/Netlify), notification provider wiring, signed Android release. - `.dockerignore` to keep dev artifacts out of the build context. The dev schema stays on SQLite (`provider = "sqlite"`) for local convenience. DEPLOY.md walks through the two-line provider switch + migration rebaseline before first prod deploy. ## Review & Testing Checklist for Human - [ ] **Refresh rotation** — login, copy refresh token, hit `/auth/refresh`, confirm response includes a *new* refresh token. Try `/auth/refresh` again with the *old* token — should 401 `refresh_reuse_detected`. Confirm all that parent's refresh tokens are now revoked in the DB. - [ ] **Password reset** — `POST /auth/password-reset/request {email}` → check backend stdout for `[auth:password-reset] parent=... token=...`. Hit `/password-reset/confirm` with that token + new password → 200. Try logging in with the old password → 401. Try the reset token a second time → `invalid_or_expired`. - [ ] **Rate limits** — fire 30 `POST /auth/login` from one IP; confirm a `429` after limit. Try the same from a different IP via header rewrite (after `TRUST_PROXY=1`); confirm independent counter. - [ ] **Audit page** — make a few policy edits and command actions, confirm `/audit` shows them with newest first. - [ ] **Docker build** — `docker build -f apps/backend/Dockerfile -t getkids-backend .` succeeds locally. ### Notes - This PR does NOT switch the dev schema to Postgres; the steps to do so are in `docs/DEPLOY.md`. Doing it inline would force every dev to install Postgres before working on unrelated tasks. - Push token registration (FCM `device.fcmToken`) is documented but intentionally left for the same future PR that wires real provider keys — without a Firebase project ID, the registration is just dead code. - 2FA TOTP isn't in this PR. It's a meaningful addition but doubles the surface area; happy to do it as a follow-up if you want. Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/82d5957c75884e51881e6a6ebdeb7e08 Requested by: @groxce ---

body:
## Summary

First of two PRs that lift parsedmarc's mailbox abstraction into mailsuite so applications can read/manage mail across multiple providers behind one interface. After both land, parsedmarc consumes mailsuite for this layer instead of maintaining its own copy.

This PR adds:

- `mailsuite.mailbox.MailboxConnection` — ABC with `create_folder`, `fetch_messages`, `fetch_message`, `delete_message`, `move_message`, `keepalive`, `watch`, and a new `send_message` method
- `mailsuite.mailbox.IMAPConnection` — wraps `mailsuite.imap.IMAPClient`, IDLE-based watch loop (lifted from parsedmarc)
- `mailsuite.mailbox.MaildirConnection` — backed by stdlib `mailbox.Maildir` (lifted from parsedmarc)

`send_message()` raises `NotImplementedError` on these two receive-only backends with a pointer to `mailsuite.smtp.send_email` for standalone sending. The Microsoft Graph and Gmail backends — which natively combine receive and send — land in PR2.

The existing `mailsuite.imap`, `mailsuite.smtp`, `mailsuite.utils`, and `mailsuite.dkim` modules are untouched, so existing users (including parsedmarc's current `mailsuite.imap.IMAPClient` consumer) are unaffected.

Class names match parsedmarc's exactly (`MailboxConnection`, `IMAPConnection`, `MaildirConnection`) so the parsedmarc migration is a one-line import change per file.

Version bumped to 1.13.0.

💡 What: Replaced multiline regex code fence stripping in `SchemaParser.stripCodeFences` with a manual string scanning logic using `indexOf` and `substring`.

author: buckz1lla
body:
Add _rule_systemic_prior_auth() — a new cross-claim rule that fires when CO-197 (prior authorization missing) or CO-57 (referral absent) appears on 2+ distinct claims. This distinguishes a systemic provider workflow failure from an isolated denial and produces a qualitatively different recommendation:

- Identifies whether pattern is single-provider (most likely billing workflow failure) vs multi-provider (plan-wide auth requirement or referral tracking issue)
- Surfaces the dominant code (CO-197 vs CO-57) and counts of each
- Recommends contacting the provider's authorization department and requesting retroactive authorization across all affected claims simultaneously
- Estimated savings: 50% of total at-risk patient responsibility

Also expand harness runner to support systemic_only_check sentinel — allows asserting that a single-claim CO-197 produces exactly 1 appeal opp (from reason_code_analysis) and not 2 (which would indicate the systemic rule incorrectly fired on a single-claim input).

Harness: 29/29 PASS (TP:18 FP:0 FN:0 TN:11)

author: runnel
body:
## Summary

Review follow-up #1 (BLOCKING) from `docs/handoff-prompts/voog-mcp-review-followups.md`.

`voog_mcp/errors.py:7` returned `list[TextContent]`, which the MCP SDK's `Server.call_tool()` decorator wraps as `CallToolResult(isError=False)`. Per spec § 7 (`docs/specs/2026-04-26-mcp-server.md`), every tool error must surface as `isError=True` content blocks so clients (Claude included) can distinguish a tool-level failure from a successful response. As-is, both paths looked identical on the wire.

Verified the SDK behaviour locally:

```
.venv/bin/python -c "import inspect; from mcp.server.lowlevel.server import Server; print(inspect.getsource(Server.call_tool))"
```

— the handler short-circuits with `if isinstance(results, types.CallToolResult): return ServerResult(results)`, so a fully-formed `CallToolResult` from us is passed through untouched.

## What changed

- `voog_mcp/errors.py`: `error_response()` now returns `CallToolResult(content=[…], isError=True)`. `success_response()` stays as `list[TextContent]` — the SDK's default `isError=False` wrapping is correct for that path.
- `voog_mcp/tools/*.py` (8 files): return-type annotations updated to `list[TextContent] | CallToolResult` on the public `call_tool` and on every internal `_*` helper that propagates `error_response()`.
- Tests (`tests/test_errors.py` + 8 `tests/test_tools_*.py`): error-path assertions migrated from `result[0].text` to `result.content[0].text`, with an explicit `assertTrue(result.isError)` so the spec contract is asserted, not just the payload shape.
- New unit test in `tests/test_errors.py` asserts the type/shape contract directly: `error_response` is a `CallToolResult` with `isError=True`; `success_response` is `list[TextContent]`.
- New integration test in `tests/test_mcp_integration.py::TestMCPInitialize::test_tool_validation_error_returns_iserror_true`: end-to-end check that calls `page_delete` without `force=true` over the JSON-RPC transport (dummy token, no live API) and asserts `result.isError == True` plus the expected `force=true` error message.

## Verification

```
.venv/bin/python -m unittest discover tests
# 393 tests pass (was 392) — net +1 from the new integration test;
# the new unit test in test_errors.py replaces an existing one in place,
# so the unit count is unchanged.
```

## Acceptance checklist

- [x] 392+ tests pass
- [x] New unit test (test_errors.py) asserts `CallToolResult(isError=True)` for `error_response`
- [x] New integration test (test_mcp_integration.py) asserts `isError=True` on the wire for a tool-validation failure
- [x] Faulty tool calls now return `isError=True`

body:
## Summary

Five-commit batch hardening the `/v1/messages/stream` SSE endpoint. The headline change is a real production bug fix: provider streams kept billing tokens after the client disconnected, because Node's `IncomingMessage` 'close' event doesn't fire reliably on socket teardown once the request body has been fully consumed.

### Commits

1. **`flushHeaders`** — ship SSE `Content-Type` + `X-Accel-Buffering: no` immediately so reverse proxies / browsers see them before the first delta, instead of letting Node buffer the response start until enough body is queued.
2. **`[DONE]` is last on success** — regression test locking that `[DONE]` is the final SSE sentinel emitted on the happy path. Anything after it is silently dropped by clients.
3. **`[DONE]` is last on error** — same guarantee on the provider-throws-mid-stream catch path. Without it, error-recovering clients hang on the read loop.
4. **Listen on `res`, not `req`, for client disconnect** — the production fix. Switches `ctx.req.on('close')` → `res.on('close')` (gated on `!res.writableEnded` so `res.end()` from normal completion doesn't trigger the abort path). Adds a regression test that parks the upstream generator on the abort signal and asserts it flips within the test budget — proves the cancel chain reaches the provider in production-equivalent conditions.
5. **Swallow `res 'error'`** — a mid-stream socket error (ECONNRESET, EPIPE) emits 'error' on the ServerResponse. With no listener, Node escalates it to unhandled and the API process can crash. Treat it like a client disconnect: cancel upstream and let the for-await throw exit cleanly.

### Why this matters

Before commit 4, the controller already threaded an `AbortSignal` through to each provider (merged in #135), but the signal never aborted in practice because the close detection was on the wrong event source. Paid OpenAI / Anthropic / Perplexity streams kept running and billing until they completed naturally.

body:
Load Config from a file called config.json on boot. Create it if it doesn't exist, using existing defaults.

Create a ButtonPin class and use this to configure the ButtonDef with the hardware source and pin. This allows us to load the config and read the device and pin matching each button from config, meaning each saxophone build can have its own button to pin mapping.

Finally, in order to write to the filesystem from the circuitpython code, we have to do this hack to storage. The storage can only be writable by the saxophone or your computer when plugged in, but not both.  boot.py makes this work:

1. by default only the saxophone code can write to storage. This allows it to write config.json as needed. It also means when you plug the saxophone into a computer it will be read-only.
2. to write from your computer, you must hold down any two buttons on the right hand keys while plugging in the device, and it must be powered off before plugging in. in this mode, the saxophone will not be able to write config.json but will be able to read config.

author: chen3feng
body:
## Summary

The `Sanitizers (ubuntu-latest)` job finally told us the real story: the
non-MSVC CI failure is **not** a GCC/Clang miscompile of `BitCopyFast.cpp`.
It is a dangling-reference bug in our own CI shim, `CI/ue_shim.h`, that
happened to be invisible at `-O0` and loud at `-O2`.

AddressSanitizer report (from the last failing run on `main`):

```
==2344==ERROR: AddressSanitizer: stack-use-after-return on address 0x7fceec600030
    #0 BitsCopyFastUnaligned  Source/FastBitCopy/Private/BitCopyFast.cpp:183
    #1 appBitsCpyFastImpl     Source/FastBitCopy/Private/BitCopyFast.cpp:352
    #2 main                   CI/test_main.cpp:249

Address 0x7fceec600030 is located in stack of thread T0 at offset 48 in frame
    #0 FMath::Min<int,int>(int, int)   CI/ue_shim.h:52
  This frame has 2 object(s):
    [48, 52) 'a' (line 52) <== Memory access at offset 48 is inside this variable
```

The memory being read by `BitsCopyFastUnaligned` at line 183 belongs to
`FMath::Min`'s own stack frame, specifically parameter `a`. That only
makes sense if `Min` was returning a reference to `a`, not a copy.

## Root cause

```cpp
template <class A, class B>
static constexpr auto Min(A a, B b) -> decltype(a < b ? a : b)
{
    return a < b ? a : b;
}
```

`decltype(a < b ? a : b)` where `a` and `b` are same-typed **lvalues**
evaluates to an **lvalue reference type** (`int&`). So the trailing
return type is `int&`, and `Min` returns a reference to its
by-value parameter -- a dangling reference the moment `Min` returns.

Why it stayed hidden:

* **`-O2`**: the caller (`BitsCopyFastUnaligned`) has `const int CopyBits
  = FMath::Min(CopySrcBits, BitCount);`. The compiler materialises
  `CopyBits` by reading from the returned reference slot *after* `Min`
  has returned, by which time the stack has been reused. That is the
  UB. ASan's `detect_stack_use_after_return=1` (default on this
  toolchain) is what made it a deterministic error.
* **`-O0`**: no stack reuse, the dead slot still had the correct value,
  so the job kept passing. That is why every `Standalone test -O0` run
  was green and we kept (wrongly) concluding that the helpers
  themselves needed to be pinned to `-O0`.
* **MSVC**: different codegen for same-type `?:` + different stack
  layout meant the read happened to still be valid.

Essentially every "fix" we tried on `BitCopyFast.cpp` itself --
`optnone`, `noinline`, `asm ("" ::: "memory")` barriers, forcing
`uint32` intermediates for the shifts -- was treating a symptom of a
bug that lives two files away.

## Fix

Return by value, matching UE's real `FMath::Min<T>(T, T)`:

```cpp
template <class T>
static constexpr T Min(T a, T b) { return a < b ? a : b; }
template <class T>
static constexpr T Max(T a, T b) { return a > b ? a : b; }
```

`BitCopyFast.cpp` only ever calls `FMath::Min(int, int)` /
`FMath::Max(int, int)`, so collapsing the two template parameters into
one `T` is safe. The shim is only used by the standalone CI harness;
the in-engine plugin build links against real UE `FMath` and was
never affected.

## Verification (actual CI on this branch)

| Job | Before (`main`) | After (this PR) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Standalone test **(ubuntu-latest, -O2)** | :x: | :white_check_mark: |
| Standalone test **(macos-latest, -O2)**  | :x: | :white_check_mark: |
| Standalone test (windows-latest, MSVC)   | :white_check_mark: | :white_check_mark: |
| Standalone test -O0 (ubuntu / macos)     | :white_check_mark: | :white_check_mark: |
| arm64 cross-build (linux)                | :white_check_mark: | :white_check_mark: |
| Dump -O2 assembly (linux)                | :white_check_mark: | :white_check_mark: |
| Validate .uplugin                        | :white_check_mark: | :white_check_mark: |
| **Sanitizers (ubuntu-latest)**           | :x: (SUAR)        | :x: (*different* bug -- see below) |

The `-O2` functional failures on Linux and macOS -- the entire
motivation for this PR -- are **fixed**.

## What remains red and why I am *not* fixing it in this PR

The `Sanitizers` job is still red, but with a completely different
error that only became reachable once we stopped crashing on the
stack-use-after-return:

```
BitCopyFast.cpp:133:20: runtime error: load of misaligned address
0x521000000101 for type 'long unsigned int', which requires 8 byte alignment
```

Line 133 is `const WordType Word = Src[i];`, i.e. dereferencing a
`uint64*` that was cast from `uint8*` at an arbitrary byte offset.
On x86/x64 the hardware is happy to do this (that is exactly what
`PLATFORM_SUPPORTS_UNALIGNED_LOADS=1` promises), so the code is
*functionally* correct -- which is why every non-sanitized job is
now green. But it is language-level UB according to C++, and UBSan
with `-fsanitize=alignment` (on by default in the Sanitizers job) is
specifically there to catch exactly this.

This is a pre-existing issue, not regressed by this PR. It was
simply masked before: the earlier stack-use-after-return aborted the
sanitized run inside `BitsCopyFastUnaligned` long before execution
ever reached this aligned-path load. Now that the crash is gone,
UBSan runs further and surfaces the next latent issue.

I am keeping it out of this PR deliberately, because:

1. It is a different class of bug (language-level alignment UB vs
   lifetime UB).
2. The fix touches production code (`BitCopyFast.cpp`), not the
   test shim, so the reviewer's attention should be separate.
3. This PR's claim -- "fix the `-O2` Linux/macOS failures" -- is
   already fully substantiated by the table above, and inflating
   scope would muddy the bisect story.

## Follow-ups (tracked separately, not in this PR)

1. `BitCopyFast.cpp`: replace raw `uint64*` dereferences with
   `std::memcpy`-based reads/writes so the code is both
   language-legal and optimal (Clang/GCC collapse `memcpy(&w,p,8)`
   to a single load). Closes the Sanitizers alignment warning.
2. `BitCopyFast.cpp`: revert the defensive noise accumulated while
   we were chasing the wrong bug -- `optimize("O0")` /
   `__attribute__((optnone))` / `asm ("" ::: "memory")` barriers /
   manual `uint32` promotions for the shift chain. None of it was
   needed; it was all treating symptoms of the shim bug.
3. `FastBitCopyModule.cpp`: re-enable the hook on non-MSVC builds
   (we disabled it defensively while fallback was believed
   necessary; now that the helpers are provably correct, the hook
   can go back on).
4. `README.md`: drop the "Linux / macOS: partial" language and
   close #2.
5. `agent-skills`: record the lesson
   (`decltype(cond ? a : b)` on same-typed lvalues yields
   `T&`; never use it as a trailing return type for a function
   that took its operands by value).

## Summary

Hotfix for user-reported \"map oversized in the canvas\" on `/explore/emotion-pulse/`.

## Root cause

After the Phase 3a fit-iframe hotfix (#78) made `.plot-wrap` fill 100% of the iframe, Plotly rendered the chart at the full iframe height — which is `desktop_height: 1100` from `data/canonical.json`. On a typical laptop viewport (1366×768 / 1440×900 MBP 13\"), 1100px chart + page H1 + intro + footnote + \"Keep exploring\" cards forces scroll to see the full plot.

## Change

One line in `data/canonical.json`: `emotion-pulse.desktop_height` 1100 → 700.

Why 700: industry editorial median (NYT Upshot, The Pudding, FT Visual Storytelling, Bloomberg Graphics all sit in 600-800px). 700px = ~64% of original, fits a 1366×768 viewport with editorial surround visible without scroll, leaves clearance for the 240×240 radar overlay in the top-right corner, and still reads distinct for 5 archetype clusters.

## Strict scope (per user instruction)

- ✅ `emotion-pulse.desktop_height` ONLY
- ❌ `mobile_height` (640) untouched — mobile work is Phase 2
- ❌ Other 3 charts' heights untouched (community-dynamics: 1000, weather-report: 1200, inner-life-currents: 1000)
- ❌ Chart bake script untouched

## Summary
Captura **quem finalizou, de onde e com qual cliente HTTP** no momento da transição → FINALIZADO. Dados gravados na própria tabela `reports`, imutáveis após finalização (trigger SQL cobre), e **nunca expostos em DTO** — auditoria só interna.

## Mudanças
- **`V1_17` alterada** (em dev, pode mexer na original): adiciona `finalized_by_user_id UUID`, `finalized_by_ip VARCHAR(45)`, `finalized_user_agent VARCHAR(500)` + atualiza trigger `prevent_finalized_report_update` pra imutabilizar todos os 5 campos de finalização (existing 2 + new 3)
- **`ContextHolder`**: data class `Context` ganha `ipAddress` e `userAgent`. Métodos `getIpAddress()` e `getUserAgent()`
- **`JwtAuthenticationFilter`**: popula context com IP (`X-Forwarded-For` com fallback `remoteAddr`, truncado em 45 chars) e `User-Agent` (truncado em 500 chars)
- **`Report` (domain) + `ReportJpaEntity`**: ganham os 3 campos
- **`ReportPersistenceAdapter.save`**: comparação de imutabilidade expandida; mapper preenche os campos
- **`ReportServiceImpl.update`**: quando `finalizing == true`, captura do `ContextHolder` e seta antes do save

## NÃO expõe
- `ReportResponse` DTO **não inclui** esses campos
- `published_reports` (cross-tenant, schema public) **não recebe** esses dados — continua com snapshot mínimo
- Profissional não vê seu próprio IP no perfil — zero benefício UX, só audit

## LGPD
Base legal sólida:
- **Legítimo interesse** (LGPD art. 7º IX) — segurança da informação e prevenção de fraude
- **Execução de contrato** (art. 7º V) — garantir integridade do laudo, que é o serviço

Mencionar na política de privacidade. Retenção indefinida por enquanto (revisar pós-launch).

## Validações
- `./gradlew build -x test` ✅ (ktlint inclusive)

## Test plan
- [ ] Finalizar relatório → conferir no banco que `finalized_by_user_id`, `finalized_by_ip`, `finalized_user_agent` foram preenchidos
- [ ] `GET /reports/{id}` (response API) — campos NÃO devem aparecer no JSON
- [ ] `UPDATE reports SET finalized_by_ip = '0.0.0.0' WHERE status = 'FINALIZADO'` direto no banco → trigger barra
- [ ] Header `X-Forwarded-For: 1.2.3.4, 5.6.7.8` → grava `1.2.3.4` (primeiro IP da cadeia, IP real do cliente)
- [ ] Sem header X-Forwarded-For → grava `request.remoteAddr`

author: bushidocodes
body:
## Summary

The course's COBOL examples were authored for Micro Focus COBOL and rely on dialect features GnuCOBOL doesn't accept by default. This PR converts them to portable syntax so students can compile each example with a plain `cobc -x file.cbl` (or `cobc -m` for subprograms).

After this change, all 73 standalone `.cbl`/`.CBL` source files in the repo compile cleanly under GnuCOBOL 3.x.

## What changed

**Format conversions** (applied to `.CBL`/`.cbl` sources and the matching `<pre>` blocks in HTML pages):

- `      $ SET SOURCEFORMAT"FREE"` → `>>SOURCE FORMAT IS FREE` (Micro Focus directive replaced with the COBOL 2002 standard form, which GnuCOBOL auto-detects).
- `      $ SET NESTCALL` removed — not needed by GnuCOBOL; nested programs work natively.
- Lines starting with `*` at column 1 (Micro Focus free-format comment) → `*>` (the standard free-format comment marker). In free-format COBOL, a bare `*` is the multiplication operator.
- Stripped non-breaking-space (U+00A0) artifacts from inside `<pre>` blocks in six pages where they were breaking parsing (`course/RefMod.html`, `course/Search.html`, `course/Selection.html`, `course/Usage.html`, two exercise pages).

**Targeted bug fixes** (also propagated to the embedded HTML where applicable):

- `examples/Perform/PERFORM3.CBL`: `VALUES ZEROS` → `VALUE ZEROS`.
- `examples/SubProg/DayDiff/DayDiffDriver.cbl`: `END PROGRAM DayDriver` → `END PROGRAM DayDiffDriver`.
- `exercises/Exm-BookshopLectReqRpt/BookshopRpt91.Cbl`: PROGRAM-ID had a stray `.Cbl` extension.
- `course/IndexedFiles.html`: missing period after `VALUE HIGH-VALUES`.
- `course/Resources/progs/INX-EG2.CBL`: missing period after `FD VideoFile`.
- `course/Resources/progs/{INX-EG2,INX-EG3,REL-EG2}.CBL`: trailing sample-run console output was being parsed as code; commented out with `*>`.
- `course/Search.html`: renamed variable `Pos` → `PosNum`. `POS` is a context-sensitive reserved word in GnuCOBOL (used by the `DISPLAY ... POS(row, col)` extension), and the parser misinterprets `DISPLAY x Pos` as the start of a POS clause.

## Compile commands

- Standalone programs: `cobc -x file.cbl`
- Subprograms (have `PROCEDURE DIVISION USING ...`): `cobc -m file.cbl`. The seven affected files: `Fickle.cbl`, `Steadfast.cbl`, `MultiplyNums.cbl`, `ValiDate.cbl`, `getpostage.cbl`, `getcustomeraddress.cbl`, `POSTAGE-RATE.CBL`.

## Reviewer notes

A handful of `<pre>` blocks in the `course/` pages still don't compile after this PR — they're all illustrative snippets, not standalone programs:

- `course/Copy.html` (8 blocks): demos of the `COPY` directive that reference nonexistent `CopyFile1`/`CopyFile2`/etc. copybooks.
- `course/Subprograms.html` (3 blocks): snippets with `?` placeholders, partial syntax (e.g., `PROGRAM-ID DateValidate IS INITIAL` without period), and multi-program layouts.
- `course/RefMod.html` block 6: uses the COBOL 2014 `(ALL)` subscript (`FUNCTION MAX(Ielement(ALL))`), which GnuCOBOL doesn't support.
- `course/Unstring.html` block 1 (`CDFILE`): non-standard OCCURS DEPENDING followed by a fixed field. Compiles only with `cobc -fcomplex-odo -x`.

These would need rewrites (or in some cases, replacement copybook files) to be standalone-compilable, so they're left as-is.

## Test plan

- [x] All 73 standalone source files compile under `cobc` 3.3 on Windows (`cobc -x` for executables, `cobc -m` for the subprograms listed above).
- [x] 80/96 COBOL `<pre>` blocks across all HTML pages extract and compile; the 16 remaining failures are documented snippets as listed above.
- [ ] Spot-check a few rendered pages (Perform3, DayDiffDriver, IndexedFiles, Search) in a browser to confirm the embedded code still displays correctly.

`_run_schema_migrations` runs a one-time dedup DELETE before creating the unique index (guarded by `pg_indexes` existence check — runs only once). Existing production data is safe; the DELETE removes duplicate `(job_id, patient_id)` rows only if the index doesn't yet exist.

```sql
-- Runs automatically on first startup after deploy:
DELETE FROM measure_results a USING measure_results b WHERE a.id < b.id AND a.job_id = b.job_id AND a.patient_id = b.patient_id;
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS uq_measure_results_job_patient ON measure_results (job_id, patient_id);
ALTER TABLE measure_results ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS error_details JSONB;
ALTER TABLE measure_results ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS error_phase VARCHAR(32);
```

author: delightech28
body:
## Description
This PR introduces resumable upload functionality for verification evidence. Large evidence uploads (up to 50MB) are now supported via a chunking mechanism to ensure network stability and recovery semantics without having to restart from zero when a connection drop occurs.

## Changes
* **Database Schema:** Introduced `UploadSession` and `UploadChunk` models to `schema.prisma` to track upload state, file constraints, expiration (24h TTL), and strictly guarantee sequential block delivery. 
* **Uploads Module:** Created a new `UploadsModule` and wired it into the core `AppModule`.
* **Endpoints:**
  * `POST /uploads/session`: Initializes a multipart upload and asserts valid content types (`image/*`, `application/pdf`, etc.) and payload size limits.
  * `PUT /uploads/session/:id/chunks/:chunkIndex`: Idempotent binary ingestion endpoint for individual chunks, enabling resume semantics seamlessly over unstable networks.
  * `POST /uploads/session/:id/finalize`: Asserts chunk integrity (contiguous chunk indexing, total size alignment) and validates ownership before permanently marking the upload session as completed.

## Validation & Security
* Idempotent chunk logic ensures that multiple retries of a failing chunk on a spotty connection do not corrupt the database state.
* Strict 24-hour expiration prevents orphaned upload sessions from persisting indefinitely.
* Server-side chunk size aggregation ensures the final received data matches the initial declared `totalSize` bytes.
* Ownership validation assertions guarantee that only the initiator of an upload session can finalize it.

author: rowan
body:
## Summary

- Change MimeParser pin in `Package.swift` from `branch: "master"` → `revision: "0903ca7e..."` (current upstream master HEAD)
- Update CHANGELOG under `[Unreleased]`
- No source changes — this is a dependency-resolver fix only

## Why

SwiftPM rejects a graph where a stable-version consumer depends on a branch-pinned transitive dep, so downstream apps (e.g. MailTriage) can't pin SwiftIMAP via `exactVersion`, `upToNextMajor`, etc. They were forced to pin by commit SHA, which works but loses the human-readable version reference.

## Why `revision:` and not `from: "0.2.5"`

MimeParser publishes SemVer tags (latest `0.2.5`), but master is **8 commits ahead** of `0.2.5`, including the upstream PR #15 fix for "Header parser fails with empty headers". Pinning to `0.2.5` would silently drop that fix. Revision-pinning to current master HEAD preserves exact behaviour.

The `revision:` SHA gives consumers an audit point and SwiftPM treats it as a stable pin. Trade-off: consumers see a SHA in `Package.resolved` rather than a SemVer string. Acceptable given the alternative would regress parser correctness.

## Follow-up

Filed #13 to consider forking MimeParser to HokuNZ org — upstream is dormant (no pushes since 2023-06-09), and there are real correctness gaps (RFC 2047 encoded-words, 8-bit UTF-8) that we'll want to fix ourselves over time.

## Test plan

- [x] `swift build` clean
- [x] `swift test` — all suites pass
- [x] `Package.resolved` (after full reset) shows clean `revision`-only state with no `branch` field

author: timmiballz22
body:
## Summary
This PR introduces a new Artifacts panel that provides a centralized interface for managing uploaded PDF documents and exported analysis reports. The panel displays document metadata, extraction status, and provides quick actions for viewing, downloading, and removing files.

## Key Changes

- **New Artifacts Panel UI**: Added a fixed-position side panel (accessible via new "Artifacts" button in header) that displays:
  - Documents currently being extracted (with progress indicators)
  - Uploaded PDF documents with metadata (page count, text size, scanned status)
  - Exported HTML reports with timestamps and file sizes
  - Quick action buttons (View, Download, Remove) for each artifact

- **Scanned PDF Detection & Handling**: Enhanced document processing to detect image-based/scanned PDFs by analyzing extracted text. When detected:
  - Marked with visual warning indicator in the Artifacts panel
  - AI is instructed to inform users that text extraction failed and suggest OCR conversion or manual text input
  - Prevents misleading analysis attempts on unreadable documents

- **Export Artifact Tracking**: Modified the PDF export function to register exported HTML reports as separate artifacts with:
  - Unique blob URLs for independent lifecycle management
  - Metadata (name, size, timestamp) for display in the panel
  - Proper cleanup on unmount to prevent memory leaks

- **State Management**: Added two new state variables:
  - `artifactsOpen`: Controls panel visibility
  - `exportedArtifacts`: Tracks exported reports with blob URLs and metadata

- **Memory & Response Handling**: Improved fallback display text generation to ensure responses are always shown even if parsing strips all content, with better handling of memory updates

- **Blob URL Cleanup**: Added dedicated useEffect to revoke exported artifact blob URLs on component unmount, preventing memory leaks

## Implementation Details

- Artifacts panel uses consistent styling with existing UI (dark theme, animations)
- Scanned PDF detection uses regex to strip page markers and check remaining text length
- Panel displays item count badge and shows empty state with helpful guidance
- All artifact actions (view, download, remove) are non-destructive to original files
- Session-based storage with clear user messaging about reload behavior

author: yemfan
body:
## Summary

Companion to PR #165's per-agent settings. Where each agent edits their own routing rule on `/dashboard/settings`, this new surface (`/dashboard/admin/lead-routing`) shows the **combined pool** — DB rules plus the env allowlist union — sorted by recent activity so you can see who's getting leads and who's idle.

## What it shows

### Roster table

| Column | What |
| --- | --- |
| Agent | display name + agent id |
| Source | `DB` / `ENV` / `DB + ENV` pill — answers "where does this agent's rule come from?" |
| Enrolled | `Active` / `Off` (off rows render dimmed — admin needs to see who opted out, not just enrolled folks) |
| ZIP coverage | dedup'd + sorted; collapses to `+N more` past 4 |
| Priority | reserved column for future weighted RR |
| Last assigned | "today" / "3 days ago" / date |
| 30d | count of IDX leads routed in the last 30 days |

Sort order: `assignmentCountLast30Days desc → lastAssignmentAt desc → displayName asc → agentId asc`. Recent activity rises to the top, idle agents sink. Stable on ID for deterministic rendering.

### ZIP coverage grid

Inverted index — for each declared ZIP, lists every enrolled agent eligible for it. Lets the admin spot uncovered ZIPs and verify market coverage at a glance.

### KPI strip

- Enrolled in pool
- Total roster (incl. opted-out)
- Leads routed (30d)

### Env-fallback hint

When zero DB rows exist but env is configured, an amber callout makes it explicit: "pool is currently driven by `IDX_ROUND_ROBIN_AGENT_IDS`."

## Architecture

- **`lib/leadAssignment/adminRoster.ts`** (pure) — `buildLeadRoutingRoster(input)` folds DB rules + env allowlist + per-agent metadata + last-assignment metrics. DB rule wins on overlap; env-only agents get implicit `inRoundRobin = true`. Plus `buildZipCoverageMap(roster)` for the inverted-index section.
- **`lib/leadAssignment/adminService.ts`** (server) — runs three reads in parallel: `agent_lead_routing` (all rows), `agents` (display names), `contacts` (last 30d IDX assignments). Folds in env vars via the existing `parseAllowlist` + `parseAgentZipCoverage` helpers.
- **`/api/dashboard/admin/lead-routing`** — GET endpoint. Auth via `getCurrentAgentContext` (operational data, any authed agent can view).
- **`/dashboard/admin/lead-routing`** — page + client. KPI strip, env-fallback callout, roster table, ZIP coverage grid.

**Read-only.** No write endpoint here — edits still happen on each agent's per-agent settings panel from PR #165. Avoids the "who's authorized to flip another agent's rule?" question for v1.

## Tests

13 new tests in `lib/leadAssignment/__tests__/adminRoster.test.ts`:

- DB-only: row per rule, source='db', preserves `inRoundRobin=false`, dedup + sort ZIP coverage.
- Env-only: row per env agent, source='env', missing metadata still appears with `displayName=null`.
- Overlap: source='both', DB rule wins (in_round_robin / zips / priority), dedups to ONE row.
- Sort: activity-desc, last-assignment-desc tiebreak, displayName-asc tiebreak, ID-asc final.
- `buildZipCoverageMap`: empty input, indexed by enrolled agents only (opted-out filtered).

Full suite: **68 files / 886 tests** passing.

## Test plan

- [ ] Visit `/dashboard/admin/lead-routing` with no DB rules + a populated `IDX_ROUND_ROBIN_AGENT_IDS` env → confirm rows render with `ENV` pill + amber fallback callout.
- [ ] Add an `agent_lead_routing` row for one of the env agents → next refresh shows `DB + ENV` pill, DB rule values shown.
- [ ] Mark another agent's DB rule `in_round_robin = false` → row stays in roster, dimmed, with `Off` badge.
- [ ] Generate IDX leads via `/api/idx/lead-capture` → confirm last-assigned + 30d-count update on the roster.
- [ ] Confirm the ZIP coverage section only lists enrolled agents (opted-out agents shouldn't appear there).

## Out-of-scope follow-ups

- Admin-level **edit** of another agent's rule (today: each agent edits their own from settings). Needs a permission model first.
- **Top-nav link** — currently only reachable via direct URL.
- Real **percentile** of "leads routed" so admins can compare against the team average.
- **Termination signal** ("agent X opted out 3 days ago, may want to remove from env") — small banner on rows where `inRoundRobin=false` AND `source='both'`.

author: rainxchzed
body:
## Summary
- Wires the E6 product-telemetry pipeline against the live `POST /v1/telemetry/events` backend.
- Adds first-launch consent sheet on home + sibling toggle in privacy settings.
- Migrates the six E1 import events from `TelemetryRepository` to `ProductTelemetry` atomically (no double-emission); deletes the five out-of-scope legacy import calls listed in the handoff §3.4.
- Wires the remaining 19 events: CRASH, OPERATION_FAILED, COLD_START_MS, FIRST_PAINT_MS, CACHE_HIT/MISS, SEARCH_EXECUTED, DETAILS_VIEWED, UPDATE_INSTALLED, PROXY_CONFIGURED, PROXY_USED, SESSION_DURATION (MIRROR_USED skipped — no mirror endpoint exists in code yet; constant remains for future wiring).
- Adds `PrivacyAuditTest` pinning the client allowlist to the backend's locked schema; adds bounded-flush hooks on Android `ProcessLifecycleOwner` ON_STOP and JVM `Runtime.addShutdownHook`.
- Threads `from` nav arg into `DetailsScreen` so DETAILS_VIEWED can carry a categorical "search" / "category" / "library" / "link" prop without leaking repo identity.
- Bumped the branch to current main first to pick up the E1 work the §3.4 migration depends on.

## Test plan
- [x] `./gradlew :composeApp:compileKotlinJvm :composeApp:compileDebugKotlinAndroid` — both targets compile clean.
- [x] `./gradlew :core:domain:jvmTest` — `PrivacyAuditTest` passes (allowlist matches backend, no PII keys, all prop keys snake_case ≤32 chars).
- [ ] Manual against staging: fresh-install device → consent sheet appears once → "Got it" → use app for 30s → kill → query `telemetry_events` on the VPS, expect rows for `app_launched`, `cold_start_ms`, `first_paint_ms`, plus whatever other events were exercised. Toggle off in Settings → use → re-query → no new rows.

<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->
## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **New Features**
  * Opt-in product telemetry: consent UI, settings toggle, persistence/gating, privacy screens/strings, first-paint and lifecycle events (app launch, session, crashes, screen views, cache/proxy/update/import events).
  * Telemetry emission from multiple app areas (UI, background services, downloads).

* **Chores**
  * Buffered, batched telemetry delivery with background flush and shutdown best-effort.

* **Documentation**
  * Client handoff roadmap for telemetry schema, privacy rules, and rollout.

* **Tests**
  * Privacy audit enforcing allowlist and rejecting PII.

* **Behavioral Change**
  * Search queries are no longer collected/hashed.

author: bernhardunger
body:
## Fix: Konflikt mit moziloCMS Query-Parametern

### Problem
URLs der Form `/Kategorie/Seite%20Name.html?cat=Kategorie&page=114&action=114`
wurden fälschlicherweise vom Plugin umgeleitet. Dabei ging der komplette Query-String
verloren und moziloCMS konnte die Zielseite nicht mehr finden – der User landete
auf der Startseite.

Betroffen waren vor allem versteckte Seiten die über interne moziloCMS-Parameter
direkt angesteuert werden.

### Ursache
Das Plugin hat den Pfad `/Kategorie/Seite Name.html` als umzuschreibende
Umlaut/Leerzeichen-URL erkannt und einen 301-Redirect ausgelöst – ohne zu prüfen
ob moziloCMS die Seite über `?cat=` und `?page=` bereits aufgelöst hatte.

### Fix
In `handleRequest()` wird jetzt zu Beginn geprüft ob `$_GET['cat']` oder
`$_GET['page']` bereits gesetzt sind. In diesem Fall hat moziloCMS die URL
bereits aufgelöst und das Plugin greift nicht ein.

### Tests
- 1 neuer Test: `testHandleRequestGetMoziloCmsQueryParamsWerdenIgnoriert()`
- 57 Tests, alle grün

### Motivation
- Provide a printable monthly attendance register where the user selects a standard, month and year and the sheet prints with student names filled and Sundays marked automatically. 
- Replace the per-student daily toggle UI with a focused monthly-generation flow so attendance can be printed for the whole class at once.

### Description
- Simplified the attendance modal UI in `AttendanceRegisterForm.tsx` to accept `Standard`, `Month`, and `Year`, removed per-student day toggles, and precomputes Sundays for the selected month/year using `useMemo`.
- When generating, the form now builds a `Map<string, { month: number; year: number; days: boolean[] }>` where `days` is a boolean array with Sundays set to `true` for all students and passes it to the PDF generator via `handleGenerate`.
- Reworked `generateAttendanceRegisterPDF` in `pdfGenerator.ts` to a tabular printable layout (No / Student Name / day columns), auto-shade Sunday columns and render an `S` in Sunday cells, and paginate when needed for long rosters.
- Updated generated filename logic in `generateMultiplePDFs` to use the selected month/year from the attendance payload (instead of the current system month/year).

Adds a focused `openclaw sessions explain <key>` command to inspect how a stored session resolves today.

### What changed
- adds `openclaw sessions explain <key>`

  - session key
  - agent id

  - final effective provider/model
  - final effective workspace

OpenClaw already had the pieces to resolve a session's effective model/provider/workspace, but there was no focused CLI explain surface for a real stored session. This makes it easier to debug why a given session is behaving the way it is.

author: copilot
body:
Research document analyzing how to embed LLM-generated HTML and images into TBE learning content—covering showcase, storage, and update strategies.

### Findings

- **MDXRenderer** already supports inline HTML (`markdown-it` with `html: true`) and images via standard Markdown syntax — no schema changes needed for this path
- **StudyGuide model** stores structured JSON with `Schema.Types.Mixed` sections but has no explicit image/HTML block type — needs extension for rich content
- **Resources app** renders full HTML documents via `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` with scoped styles — already handles arbitrary HTML

### Recommendations

- **Image storage:** External CDN (Cloudinary/S3/R2) with URLs referenced in content strings — avoids DB bloat, enables caching and format optimization
- **Structured content:** Extend StudyGuide schema with typed content blocks (`image`, `html`, `text`, `code`) for granular control
- **Updates:** Section-level replacement by existing `id` field for targeted LLM regeneration without losing unchanged content
- **Security:** Add DOMPurify sanitization before all `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` usage
- **Performance:** Lazy loading, responsive `srcset`, CDN auto-format (WebP/AVIF)

### Changes

- Added `docs/research-embed-html-image-content.md` with full analysis and next steps

## Summary
This PR adds the ability to resize columns in the task list by dragging column dividers. Users can now adjust column widths to better fit their workflow and preferences.

## Key Changes
- **Column width state management**: Added `colWidths` array to state with default widths for all 11 columns, and `colResize` object to track active resize operations
- **Column header rendering**: Implemented `renderColHdr()` function to dynamically generate column headers with resizer handles positioned at the right edge of each column
- **Column width application**: Created `applyColumnWidths()` function to apply stored widths to both the header and all task rows using CSS Grid
- **Resize interaction handlers**: 
  - `onColResizerDown()` initiates resize operation on mousedown
  - `mousemove` listener updates column width in real-time with minimum width constraint (20px)
  - `mouseup` listener finalizes resize and cleans up UI state
- **Styling**: Added CSS for `.resizer` element with hover and active states, positioned absolutely within column headers

## Implementation Details
- Column resizers are 5px wide with visual feedback on hover/drag
- Minimum column width enforced at 20px to prevent columns from becoming too narrow
- Resize state tracked separately from main state to avoid unnecessary re-renders during drag
- Column header is rendered at the start of `renderTaskList()` to ensure it's always in sync with task rows
- Grid template columns applied to both header and all task rows for consistent alignment

author: depfu[bot]
body:
🚨 Your current dependencies have known security vulnerabilities 🚨 This dependency update fixes known security vulnerabilities. Please see the details below and assess their impact carefully. We recommend to merge and deploy this as soon as possible!
Here is everything you need to know about this update. Please take a good look at what changed and the test results before merging this pull request. ### What changed? #### ✳️ postcss (8.4.47 → 8.5.12) · [Repo](https://github.com/postcss/postcss) · [Changelog](https://github.com/postcss/postcss/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md)
Security Advisories 🚨

🚨 PostCSS has XSS via Unescaped in its CSS Stringify Output

PostCSS: XSS via Unescaped </style> in CSS Stringify Output

Summary

PostCSS v8.5.5 (latest) does not escape </style> sequences when stringifying CSS ASTs. When user-submitted CSS is parsed and re-stringified for embedding in HTML <style> tags, </style> in CSS values breaks out of the style context, enabling XSS.

Proof of Concept

const postcss = require('postcss');

// Parse user CSS and re-stringify for page embedding
const userCSS = 'body { content: "</style><script>alert(1)</script><style>"; }';
const ast = postcss.parse(userCSS);
const output = ast.toResult().css;
const html = `<style>${output}</style>`;

console.log(html);
// <style>body { content: "</style><script>alert(1)</script><style>"; }</style>
//
// Browser: </style> closes the style tag, <script> executes

Tested output (Node.js v22, postcss v8.5.5):

Input: body { content: "</style><script>alert(1)</script><style>"; }
Output: body { content: "</style><script>alert(1)</script><style>"; }
Contains </style>: true

Impact

Impact non-bundler use cases since bundlers for XSS on their own. Requires some PostCSS plugin to have malware code, which can inject XSS to website.

Suggested Fix

Escape </style in all stringified output values:

output = output.replace(/<\/(style)/gi, '<\\/$1');

Credits

Discovered and reported by Sunil Kumar (@TharVid)

Release Notes

Too many releases to show here. View the full release notes.

Commits

See the full diff on Github. The new version differs by more commits than we can show here.

#### ↗️ nanoid (_indirect_, 3.3.7 → 3.3.11) · [Repo](https://github.com/ai/nanoid) · [Changelog](https://github.com/ai/nanoid/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md)
Security Advisories 🚨

🚨 Predictable results in nanoid generation when given non-integer values

When nanoid is called with a fractional value, there were a number of undesirable effects:

  1. in browser and non-secure, the code infinite loops on while (size--)
  2. in node, the value of poolOffset becomes fractional, causing calls to nanoid to return zeroes until the pool is next filled
  3. if the first call in node is a fractional argument, the initial buffer allocation fails with an error

Version 3.3.8 and 5.0.9 are fixed.

3.3.8 (from changelog)

author: daishiman
body:
## Summary

- `task-claude-code-permissions-decisive-mode` を `spec_created` / `docs-only` / `NON_VISUAL` で Phase 1-13 揃える（Phase 13 は `user_approval_required=true` で `blocked`）
- aiworkflow-requirements skill に再利用可能な reference `claude-code-settings-hierarchy.md` を切り出し、関連 5 タスク wave の skill 索引を同期
- 派生 unassigned task 3 件（apply / deny-bypass-verification / project-local-first-comparison）を formalize

## Implementation Guide

> 出典: `docs/30-workflows/completed-tasks/task-claude-code-permissions-decisive-mode/outputs/phase-12/implementation-guide.md`

本ガイドは別タスクで実機反映する実装担当者に渡す手順書。
Part 1 は概念を中学生向けに、Part 2 は技術詳細を Engineer 向けに記述する。

---

### Part 1（中学生レベル）: 鍵の例え話

なぜ必要か。
家のドアに「開けますか？」と毎回聞いてくる電子ロックが付いていると想像してください。
家族（=自分が普段使う作業環境）が出入りするだけなのに、毎回確認が出ると面倒で作業が止まります。
たとえば、家の中を移動するたびに玄関まで戻って許可を取るようなものです。

何をするか。
このタスクでは次の 3 つを揃えます。

1. **家の中の鍵の設定を全部「家族は確認なしで通す」に統一する**
   - Claude Code には設定ファイルが 3 段階あり、上の段が下を上書きします。
   - 段ごとに違う値が書かれていると、起動するたびに「確認するモード」へ戻る事故が起きます。
   - だから 3 段全部を `bypassPermissions`（=確認スキップ）に揃えます。
2. **玄関を開ける合言葉（起動コマンド）にも「最初から確認をスキップ」と書いておく**
   - `cc` というショートカットに `--permission-mode bypassPermissions --dangerously-skip-permissions` というオプションを足す案を作ります。
   - ただし、危ない操作を止める貼り紙が本当に効くかは未確認なので、実際の反映は別タスクで確認してからにします。
3. **「これはやって OK / これは絶対ダメ」のリストを玄関に貼る**
   - `permissions.allow` には「pnpm install」「git status」など読み取り中心の安全なコマンドを並べます。
   - `permissions.deny` には「git push --force」など取り返しの付かないコマンドを並べます。
   - 確認をスキップしても、ダメ集にあるコマンドが止まるかを別タスクで確認します。

なぜ大事？: 起動のたびに確認が出ると集中が切れます。階層がバラバラだと「どの値が効いているか」が誰にも分からなくなります。揃えて、貼り紙を出して、玄関の合言葉にも書く——この三重で再発を防ぎます。

#### 今回作ったもの

- 設定ファイルをどの順番で読むかを説明する設計メモ。
- `cc` ショートカットをどう変えるかの差分案。
- やってよい操作と止めたい操作のリスト案。
- 実機で確認するための手順書とチェック表。

---

### Part 2（技術詳細）

#### E-1: settings 階層の `defaultMode` 統一

対象 3 ファイルを `bypassPermissions` で統一する（採用案 A）。

| Layer | Path | defaultMode |
| --- | --- | --- |
| global | `~/.claude/settings.json` | `bypassPermissions` |
| globalLocal | `~/.claude/settings.local.json` | `bypassPermissions` |
| projectLocal | `<project>/.claude/settings.local.json` | `bypassPermissions`（必要な project のみ） |

> 本リポジトリの `<project>/.claude/settings.json` は既に `bypassPermissions` であることを Phase 1 で確認済み。

#### E-2: `cc` エイリアスへの `--dangerously-skip-permissions` 併用

```zsh
# ~/.zshrc
alias cc='claude --verbose --permission-mode bypassPermissions --dangerously-skip-permissions'
```

理由: settings の読み込み順や parser の挙動に依らず、起動時点で確実に bypass を確定させるため。
TC-R-01 で `grep -nE '^alias cc=' ~/.zshrc` の結果が 1 行のみであることを必ず確認する。

#### E-3: `permissions.allow` / `deny` whitelist

```jsonc
{
  "permissions": {
    "allow": [
      "Bash(pnpm install)",
      "Bash(pnpm typecheck)",
      "Bash(pnpm lint)",
      "Bash(pnpm test)",
      "Bash(git status)",
      "Bash(git diff:*)",
      "Bash(git log:*)"
    ],
    "deny": [
      "Bash(git push --force:*)",
      "Bash(git push -f:*)",
      "Bash(rm -rf /:*)",
      "Bash(curl * | sh:*)"
    ]
  }
}
```

- `Edit` / `Write` の whitelist 化は Phase 10 MINOR として保留（Phase 12 で別タスク化候補に登録）
- 公式 docs URL は `system-spec-update-summary.md` に列挙

#### 階層優先順位

```
project/.claude/settings.local.json   (最優先)
  > project/.claude/settings.json
    > ~/.claude/settings.local.json
      > ~/.claude/settings.json       (最弱)
```

- 同名キーは上が下を上書き
- `permissions.allow` / `deny` は配列マージではなく上層が完全上書きする前提で設計（実機 TC-04/TC-05 で確認）
- enterprise managed settings は本タスク対象外

#### APIシグネチャ

```bash
claude --verbose --permission-mode bypassPermissions --dangerously-skip-permissions
```

```ts
function resolvePermission(layers: ClaudeCodeSettingsLayer[]): ResolvedPermission;
```

#### 設定項目と定数一覧

| Key | 値 | 備考 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `defaultMode` | `acceptEdits` \| `bypassPermissions` | typo は TC-F-01 で挙動確認 |
| `permissions.allow` | `string[]` | tool(pattern) 形式 |
| `permissions.deny` | `string[]` | bypass 下で実効するかは TC-05 / U2 で確認してから採用 |
| `CC_ALIAS_EXPECTED` | `claude --verbose --permission-mode bypassPermissions --dangerously-skip-permissions` | `cc` alias の正準形 |

#### エラーハンドリング

| Case | 期待挙動 | 検証 TC |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 不正な `defaultMode` 文字列 | エラーまたは安全側 fallback | TC-F-01 |
| alias オプション typo | `unknown flag` エラー | TC-F-02 |
| `cc` alias 重複定義 | 1 行のみであるべき | TC-R-01 |
| bypass + deny の衝突 | 未確認。deny が実効しない場合は `--dangerously-skip-permissions` を alias から外す | TC-05 / Remaining Blocker |

#### エッジケース

| Case | 扱い |
| --- | --- |
| project local が global を上書きする | 最上位の project local を優先し、実装時に source layer を記録する |
| `permissions.allow` と `permissions.deny` が同じ操作を含む | deny 優先が確認できない限り、安全成立条件として扱わない |
| 別プロジェクトで `cc` alias を使う | global alias の影響を受けるため U3 で project-local-first 案と比較する |
| shell に alias が複数ある | TC-R-01 で 1 行に正規化する |

#### テスト構成

| Test | 目的 | 証跡 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| TC-01〜TC-03 | mode 維持と settings 階層確認 | `outputs/phase-11/manual-smoke-log.md` |
| TC-04 | allow 対象コマンドの prompt 有無 | `outputs/phase-11/manual-smoke-log.md` |
| TC-05 | bypass 下の deny 実効性確認 | U2 の実装前ブロッカー |
| TC-F-01〜TC-F-02 | invalid mode / flag typo | `outputs/phase-11/manual-smoke-log.md` |
| TC-R-01 | alias 重複検出 | `outputs/phase-11/manual-smoke-log.md` |

#### 視覚証跡（NON_VISUAL 説明）

- 本タスクは UI 変更なし。証跡は CLI 出力テキスト（mode 表示・prompt の有無・grep 結果）で取得する。
- スクリーンショットは生成しない。`screenshots/.gitkeep` も置かない。
- 主証跡: `outputs/phase-11/manual-smoke-log.md` / 補助: `outputs/phase-10/final-review-result.md`

#### 実装着手前提

- HIGH ブロッカー（bypass + deny の優先関係 / project-local-first 適用方針）解消後に実機反映
- 実機反映は別実装タスクで行い、本タスクは `spec_created` のまま完了

#### Reference Contracts (TypeScript)

```ts
type PermissionMode = "acceptEdits" | "bypassPermissions";

interface ClaudeCodeSettingsLayer {
  name: "global" | "globalLocal" | "project" | "projectLocal";
  path: string;
  defaultMode?: PermissionMode;
  permissions?: { allow?: string[]; deny?: string[] };
}

interface ResolvedPermission {
  effectiveMode: PermissionMode;
  sourceLayer: ClaudeCodeSettingsLayer["name"];
  allow: string[];
  deny: string[];
}

function resolvePermission(layers: ClaudeCodeSettingsLayer[]): ResolvedPermission;
```

---

## Skill Sync

aiworkflow-requirements skill に再利用可能な reference を切り出し、関連索引を同期した（skill-feedback-report.md HIGH 提案 3.1 の反映）。

author: bingqinglyu
body:
## Problem

When a user message arrives during an active run in **interrupt** queue mode, the scheduling layer rejects it with _"⚠️ Previous run is still shutting down"_ and the message is lost.

### Root cause

Two registries track run activity: `ACTIVE_EMBEDDED_RUNS` (scheduling) and `ReplyOperation` (delivery). After abort:

1. `waitForEmbeddedPiRunEnd` resolves when `ACTIVE_EMBEDDED_RUNS.delete()` fires
2. But `isEmbeddedPiRunActive()` checks **both** registries via OR
3. `ReplyOperation.clearState()` runs in the old runs `finally` block — not yet complete
4. New message scheduling calls `resolveBusyState()` → `isActive` still true → rejected

## Changes

### 1. Two-phase wait (`waitForEmbeddedPiRunEnd`)
After the embedded run handle is removed, chain `waitForReplyRunEndBySessionId` with remaining timeout budget so callers see a fully idle session.

### 2. Force-detach fallback (`forceDetachEmbeddedRun`)
When abort+wait times out, remove the old runs handle from `ACTIVE_EMBEDDED_RUNS` so a new run can register immediately. The old runs finally block detects handle mismatch → no-op.

### 3. Retry with force (`agent-runner.ts`)
On `ReplyRunAlreadyActiveError`, wait 500ms for the reply-op to clear, then retry with `force: true`. **Only in interrupt mode** — collect/followup modes preserve the existing run to avoid dropped assistant progress.

### 4. Reply-run-registry hardening
- `skipNotify` option prevents premature waiter resolution during force-supersede
- `isReplaced` branch returns immediately without mutating maps the replacement op may reference
- Normal clear path iterates all `waitKeysBySessionId` aliases to remove stale entries after session rotation

## Known Limitations

- **Tool execution continues after force-detach** — tools run to natural completion. Framework-level abort race or per-tool signal handling is planned as a separate feature.
- **Steer messages during long tool execution** are queued but not processed until the tool returns. Steer-aware tool yield is future work.
- **`sessions_send` HTTP connections** cannot be cancelled after abort.

## Tests

29 tests passing across 3 test files:
- `runs.test.ts`: force-detach, `isEmbeddedPiRunActiveForSessionKey`, handle identity guard
- `get-reply-run-queue.test.ts`: force-detach + direct return, force-detach failure fallback
- `reply-run-registry.test.ts`: `skipNotify`, `isReplaced` branch, alias preservation during force-supersede

## Related

Part of a 3-PR fix set for interrupt/steer message delivery:
- **PR A:** #65010 — steer gate fix (`isStreaming` → `isActive`)
- **PR B (this):** #65221 — interrupt scheduling race fix (core, independent of A)
- **PR C:** #65222 — Telegram delivery bypass (depends on A + B)
- **Issue:** #65223 — tool abort signal design (future work)
- Supersedes #65021 (which mixed core + Telegram changes)

## AI Disclosure

- [x] AI-assisted (OpenClaw agent + Codex review)
- [x] Fully tested (29 tests across 3 test files)
- [x] Author understands all changes

## Summary

Adds a new skill at `skills/storyworld-references/SKILL.md` that owns
the storyworld-specific character-reference logic — HuggingFace
`venetanji/polyu-storyworld-characters` dataset, character codes
(`6166r`, `1822g`, …), per-character YAML lookup, multi-image
references with `.txt` captions, and the canonical "generate image of
character `<code>`" workflow.

This is the **add half** of a reconciliation pair with a sibling PR on
[`venetanji/creative-skills`](https://github.com/venetanji/creative-skills)
that **removes** the same storyworld-specific content from
`comfyui/SKILL.md`. Together they restore a clean split:

- `creative-skills/comfyui` — generic ComfyUI access (Flux2 / LTX-2.3,
  t2i / i2i / video, scripts, delivery conventions). Reusable on any
  ComfyUI server, no project assumptions.
- `polyu-storyworld/skills/storyworld-references` — this repo's
  per-character handling. Pairs with the comfyui skill: this one picks
  the reference image and builds the prompt fragment, the comfyui
  skill runs the actual workflow.

The new SKILL.md cites the generic skill via GitHub URL so the chaining
stays explicit at read time.

## What was lifted

From `creative-skills/comfyui/SKILL.md`:

- "## Character Reference Images (HuggingFace)" section — dataset
  name, ~84 characters / ~420 images, character-code convention,
  storage paths under `~/.openclaw/skills/storyworld/references/<code>/`,

body:
## Summary
Tracking down why Device B was still seeing `null` for `zs_fcal_urls` after the previous sync fix:

If a parent added a calendar URL (or any household state) **before the initial Tailscale ping resolved**, `CloudSync.push` silently no-op'd because `state.online` was still false. The local state never reached the server, so other devices never received it. "Push All to Cloud" in Parents Corner didn't fix it either — that button only walked per-kid keys.

## Changes
1. **`pushAllKids` / `pullAllKids`** now also run `pushHousehold` / `pullHousehold`, so the existing "Push All / Pull All from Cloud" buttons in Parents Corner cover shopping list, weekly menu, family-calendar URLs, sports matches, home location, and profile tombstones too.
2. **On the first online ping**, after `pullHousehold` completes, also fire `pushHousehold` — auto-uploading anything edited while offline so the next Device B refresh actually finds it on the server.
3. Cache busted: `sw.js` → `v5`, `sync.js?v=5` across hub / family / book-movie-check / math-galaxy.

## Recovery for state already stuck
After this merges and devices refresh, on Device A (where the URL is stuck locally):
- Open Parents Corner → tap **⬆️ Push All to Cloud** once. Or just hard-refresh — the new auto-push on connect will do it for you within a few seconds.
- Then on Device B, refresh once. Within ~10s the calendar surfaces.

## Test plan
- [ ] Reproduce: clear server, add URL on Device A while offline, come online → auto-push fires → Device B refresh shows it.
- [ ] Push All / Pull All buttons in Parents Corner now move shopping / menu / calendar URLs / sports matches.

author: bingqinglyu
body:
## Problem

In Telegram, grammY's `sequentialize` middleware serializes all updates for the same chat. When a run is active (e.g., executing a tool call), new messages queue behind it. This prevents:
- **Interrupt mode**: user message cannot reach the scheduling layer to trigger abort
- **Steer mode**: user message cannot be injected into the active run's steering queue

## Changes

### 1. Chat-session cache (`chatSessionCache`)
Maps Telegram chat IDs → OpenClaw session keys. Capped at 500 entries with LRU eviction. Populated when session state is resolved during message processing.

### 2. Per-message sequential key
When a run is active for the cached session key AND the queue mode is `interrupt` or `steer`/`steer-backlog`/`steer+backlog`, generate a unique per-message key instead of the per-chat key. This lets grammY process the new message concurrently with the running update.

### 3. Lightweight run-active-check module
New re-export path (`pi-embedded-runner/run-active-check.ts`) avoids pulling the full embedded-agent module graph into `reply-runtime.ts` → channel plugins. Addresses module boundary concern where `reply-runtime` is a lightweight SDK entry.

### 4. Live config for queue mode decisions
The sequential key bypass reads live config via `loadConfig()` instead of the outer config snapshot, so queue mode changes take effect without restart.

## Dependencies

Clean 3-commit stack on top of the latest prerequisite commits; will rebase away once both merge:
- #65010 — steer gate fix (`isStreaming` → `isActive`/`isStopped`)
- #65221 — interrupt scheduling race fix (force-detach + ReplyOperation hardening + seq+identity-gated retry)

## Tests

- Telegram scoped tests (`sequential-key.test.ts`, `bot.create-telegram-bot.test.ts`, etc.): pass
- Full Telegram suite: 1281/1281 pass
- Auto-reply scoped (`runs.test.ts`, `get-reply-run-queue.test.ts`, `reply-run-registry.test.ts`, `agent-runner.steer-guard.test.ts`): 52/52 pass
- oxlint: 0 errors (previously failing on unused `isStreaming`/`isInterruptMode`)

## Known Limitations

- `chatSessionCache` maps chat ID → session key; group chats with multiple senders sharing one chat ID work correctly (cache is per-chat, not per-sender)
- The bypass only activates when `isRunActiveForSessionKey` returns true; if the cache misses (first message in a chat), the fallback is normal per-chat serialization

## Related

Part of a 3-PR fix set for interrupt/steer message delivery:
- **PR A:** #65010 — steer gate fix (`isStreaming` → `isActive`/`isStopped`)
- **PR B:** #65221 — interrupt scheduling race fix (core)
- **PR C (this):** #65222 — Telegram delivery bypass
- **Issue:** #65223 — tool abort signal design (future work)
- Supersedes Telegram-specific parts of #65021

## AI Disclosure

- [x] AI-assisted (OpenClaw agent + Codex review)
- [x] Fully tested (see Tests section above)
- [x] Author understands all changes

body: ## 📋 Description Comprehensive audit of the Abdullah Properties website identifying and fixing bugs, broken links, SEO issues, build warnings, and code quality problems across 12 files. ### Changes: 1. **Social media links fixed** — Footer, Contact page, and Maintenance page were using generic placeholder URLs (`https://facebook.com`, `https://instagram.com`, etc.) instead of the actual company profile URLs defined in `src/lib/constants.ts`. Now all social links use the centralized `SOCIAL_LINKS` constants. 2. **Duplicate global error handlers removed** — `main.tsx` registered `error` and `unhandledrejection` event listeners that duplicated the same handlers already in `App.tsx`'s `GlobalFeatures` component, causing every error to be logged twice. 3. **Aggressive offline redirect removed** — `App.tsx` was doing `window.location.href = "/offline"` on the `offline` event, which disrupted whatever page the user was on. The `OfflineIndicator` component already handles offline state gracefully with a non-disruptive banner. 4. **Supabase client crash fixed** — When `VITE_SUPABASE_URL` or `VITE_SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY` env vars were missing, the client would `throw` during module import AND redirect to `/server-error`, causing an app crash loop (since ServerError also imports supabase).
