author: tenstorrent-github-bot
body: ## Summary Previously every regression notification for a run was collapsed into a single Slack thread, so every auto-triage dispatch (one per failing job) piled up under the same `thread_ts`. **This PR makes every failing *job* its own top-level Slack message**, with auto-triage replies threading under the matching per-job message. A single pipeline with 10 failing jobs now produces 10 top-level messages and 10 cleanly isolated threads. ## Slack threading model | Before | After | | --- | --- | | 1 top-level message per run (later: per regressed pipeline) | 1 top-level message **per failing job** | | `slack_ts_map = {}` or `{pipeline_name: ts}` | `slack_ts_map = {" / ": ts, ...}` | | All auto-triage replies share one thread | Each auto-triage reply threads under its job's own message | Regressions that arrive with zero failing jobs (edge case) still produce one workflow-level message keyed by `` alone; the trigger action's fallback chain (`slack_ts_map[workflow_name] -> slack_ts_map[workflow_file] -> global slack_ts`) handles them. ## Changes ### `slack-report-analyze-workflow-data/action.yaml` - Per-JOB build loop: every failing job emits one chunk + one boundary file keyed `" / "`. - Dropped the overflow-accumulation logic (single-job messages are tiny). A job message that somehow exceeds the Slack block budget falls back to a minimal body with a loud warning. - `slack_ts_map` output description updated to document the boundary-key format. - Send step's `TS_MAP` is now boundary-keyed; threading comment rewritten to match. ### `trigger-auto-triage-for-regressions/action.yml` + `index.js` - The `slackTsMap[" / "]` lookup — previously dead code — is now the live path. Workflow-level and global fallbacks preserved for the zero-failing-jobs edge case. - Misleading "per-pipeline" comments rewritten. - **New input `max_dispatches`**: optional hard cap on successful `createWorkflowDispatch` calls per invocation. Empty/unset = unlimited. Failed dispatches don't consume the budget (transient GHA errors shouldn't eat the cap). Safe-testing companion to `failures_to_elevate`. ### `analyze-workflow-data/action.yml` + `analyze-workflow-data.js` - **New input `failures_to_elevate` (TEST MODE)**: when set to `N>0`, this **exclusively replaces** the regression output for the run. Real `Pass→Fail` regressions and `detectJobLevelRegressions`-synthesized entries are discarded; `regressedDetails` becomes exactly the `N` elevated jobs. - Walks `stayedFailingDetails` in order, takes `failing_jobs.slice(0, remaining)` from each pipeline, subtracts from the budget, and stops when the budget hits zero. A single stayed-failing pipeline with many jobs can absorb the whole budget; pipelines with 0 enriched failing jobs are skipped. - The `alert-all-message.txt` (which feeds the trailing `"N other pipelines are failing"` Slack footer) is also forced empty in test mode so the test channel shows only the elevated regressions. - Diagnostic logs: `failures_to_elevate=N (TEST MODE): elevated K job(s) across P pipeline(s); replacing R real/synthesized regression entry(ies).` and (if the pool is too small) `Only K stayed-failing job(s) were available to elevate (requested N).` - Empty/unset `failures_to_elevate` is a strict no-op: the schedule path (every 10 minutes) is unchanged. ### `aggregate-workflow-data.yaml` - New `workflow_dispatch` inputs: `failures-to-elevate` and `max-auto-triage-dispatches`, plumbed to the `analyze-data` and `trigger-auto-triage` steps respectively. Defaults are empty, so the scheduled path is unaffected. - `slack-channel-id` input (pre-existing) routes both the regression messages and the auto-triage dispatches; no default, falls back to `secrets.SLACK_METAL_INFRA_CHANNEL_ID`. ## Permanent test scaffolding `failures-to-elevate` and `max-auto-triage-dispatches` stay in the final code as permanent `workflow_dispatch`-only test scaffolding. They require admin access to dispatch and are no-ops on the schedule path. Combined with `slack-channel-id`, they let an operator exercise the full notification pipeline safely against a test channel at any time. Typical dispatch for end-to-end validation: | Input | Value | | --- | --- | | `slack-channel-id` | `C09EC0QNSB0` (or any test channel) | | `failures-to-elevate` | `3` | | `max-auto-triage-dispatches` | `3` | Result: exactly 3 top-level Slack messages in the test channel, 3 auto-triage dispatches each threading under its matching message. ## Proof runs Dispatched on `brain/per-pipeline-slack-threads` against test channel `#C09EC0QNSB0`: | Run | Result | Observations | | --- | --- | --- | | [25177772833](https://github.com/tenstorrent/tt-metal/actions/runs/25177772833) | success | First per-job dispatch. Surfaced an early bug: elevation was additive on top of real regressions, producing 19 top-level messages instead of 3. Drove the exclusive-replacement fix. | | [25178192008](https://github.com/tenstorrent/tt-metal/actions/runs/25178192008) | success | Intermediate fix attempt (overlap-skip): 14 unique boundaries instead of 19, but still not the requested 3. Drove the second fix (full replacement + alert-all suppression). | | [25178668423](https://github.com/tenstorrent/tt-metal/actions/runs/25178668423) | success | Final behavior: `failures_to_elevate=3 (TEST MODE): elevated 3 job(s) across 1 pipeline(s); replacing 2 real/synthesized regression entry(ies).` `Created 3 chunk(s)`. `slack_ts_map` has exactly 3 entries keyed `" / "`. 3 auto-triage dispatches, each `Using per-job ts=...`. No alert-all footer. | ## Test plan - [x] Defaults are empty: schedule-triggered runs behave exactly as before - [x] `workflow_dispatch` with `failures-to-elevate=N` produces **exactly N** top-level Slack messages (real and synthesized regressions are replaced, not appended) - [x] Each top-level message corresponds to exactly one failing job; `slack_ts_map` keys have the form `" / "` - [x] Every auto-triage dispatch threads under its job's own message (`Using per-job ts=...` log line, never the global fallback) - [x] `max_dispatches=M` caps total successful `createWorkflowDispatch` calls at M, with a clear warning and a final `Total auto-triage dispatches this run: M/M` summary - [x] In test mode, the trailing `"N other pipelines are failing"` footer is suppressed - [x] When `failures_to_elevate` exceeds the available stayed-failing job pool, the run continues with as many as were available and emits an `Only K stayed-failing job(s) were available` warning - [x] Regressions with zero failing jobs (production edge case) still send a workflow-level message; fallback chain in `index.js` resolves them

body:
# V1 pilot EQ & SNR

While using the latest Python reference `main` to test the C port https://github.com/peterbmarks/radae_nopy, a SNR estimator ctest fail lead Claude on a merry chase that found a bug in the Python equalisation code.  The C code implementation is correct. The effects of the bug were surprisingly subtle, mainly a difference in the Python and C SNR estimator outputs. This PR is a fix to the Python code, including re-calibration of the SNR estimator.  We will also need to re-calibrate the C SNR estimator.

Thoughts:
- One reason the subtle error slipped through for 12 months was it was in complex code, has no measurable effect on performance, and no one on the FreeDV team was able to review my work. The availability of AI agents has helped close that gap.
- This is a strength in maintaining implementations in more than one language - it tends to trap bugs.

# Merge nopy tests

Merge NoPy ctest functionality from https://github.com/drowe67/radae/pull/66, as discussed in https://github.com/peterbmarks/radae_nopy/issues/13

### Motivation

- Provide an end-to-end foundation to convert STP/NC1 inputs into EMI 2400 ROP V1.4 `.CNC` programs with deterministic linear nesting and operator-facing artifacts. 
- Establish a parser-first workflow that preserves NC1 semantics (BO/KO/AK rows, flat flags, rotational offsets) and keeps unknown EMI semantics explicit until shop-validated. 
- Add operator tooling (CLI + Tkinter GUI), packaging assets, and a machine-profile mechanism to map PieceMaker/EMI commands without hard-coding. 
- Equip the repo with documentation and a comprehensive automated test suite to validate parser, nesting, writer and workflow behavior.

### Description

- Project layout and packaging: added `pyproject.toml`, `src/stptocnc` package, entry points (`stptocnc`, `stptocnc-gui`), `.gitignore`, README and `AGENTS.md`, demo `docs/` samples and `docs/emi_machine_profile.sample.json`. 
- Importers & parsers: implemented an NC1 parser (`src/stptocnc/importers/nc1_parser.py`) and inspectors (`parsers/*`) that preserve AK/BO/KO records, extract dimensions, flat flags, rotational offsets and quantity heuristics. 
- Domain + nesting: added domain models (`models/*`), deterministic Best-Fit-Decreasing linear nesting (`nesting/packer.py`) with adjacency rules and trim logic (`nesting/rules.py`), instance expansion and move/reassignment helpers. 
- Post processor / writer: added an EMI-oriented writer (`post/emi_writer.py`) that emits nested `.cnc` programs using a configurable `EmiMachineProfile` and block helpers, plus cutlist XLSX export (`reports/cutlist_xlsx.py`). 
- Workflows & UI: added CLI (`cli/main.py`) commands for inspection, conversion, finalize, calibration and operator-run flows, a Tkinter desktop operator GUI (`gui/app.py`), and packaging helper scripts/specs for PyInstaller/Inno Setup. 
- Tests: added a large test suite under `tests/` covering NC1 parsing, inspectors, nesting behavior, manual reassignment, EMI emission, finalize/calibration workflows, CLI behavior and packaging assets. 

### Testing

- Added automated tests across parser, nesting, writer, workflows, CLI and packaging in `tests/` (e.g., `test_nc1_parser.py`, `test_nested_emi_writer.py`, `test_finalize_workflow.py`, `test_operator_run.py`).
- Unit tests exercise NC1 field extraction, AK/BO/KO preservation, end-condition inference, deterministic BFD packing with trim rules, reassignment validation, EMI emission and cutlist XLSX formatting. 
- No automated test run was executed as part of this change (the test suite is included and ready for CI execution). 
- Manual invocation hints for packaging are documented in `README.md` and `AGENTS.md` (`python packaging/tools/build_exe.py` and `python packaging/tools/build_installer.py --iscc <path>`).

author: copybara-service[bot]
body:
Replace `std::set` with `absl::btree_set` in IntervalMap

Per description. `btree_set` is a lot more efficient and cache friendly.

This CL also changes the implementation of `Erase` (renamed `EraseInternal`), calling `erase(first, last)` instead of iterating through all relevant elements. Asymptotically this makes `Erase` go from O(n*lgn) to O(lgn) because the iterator increment in the original implementation has time complexity O(lgn) and we call it n times, while `upper_bound` has time complexity O(lgn).

The CL also changes the signature of a few of the methods to avoid dangling references. Unit tests showing that this is a real problem with `btree_set` were added (they break if the relevant method signatures are reverted to references).

Benchmarks confirm that this change improves performance and significantly reduces memory allocations and peak memory usage.

This CL also introduces the compiler flag `GTL_INTERNAL_INTERVAL_MAP_BTREE_OPTOUT`, which can be set to revert the code to using `std::set`. This is a "break glass" option that can be removed once all clients are stable.

author: mdmtseng
body:
## Friction Loop round 2 — `crash_recovery`

Agent built a plugin that does `*(volatile int*)nullptr = 42` on certain inputs (3 deliberate crashes mixed with 7 happy frames). Verdict: **PASS** — backend stayed up, all 7 happy frames returned the right count, post-recovery exchange + re-run works.

3 friction points, all fixed in this PR:

### F-1 (P1) — stale "Crash isolation?" Q&A in adding-a-plugin.md
The guide still described `_set_se_translator` as the in-proc protection and called process isolation a "spike branch" opt-in. PR #8 made process the default; this Q&A was missed in the doc sweep. Rewrote it to describe the actual two-layer recovery.

### F-2 (P1) — silent crash on the script side
**The most valuable finding of round 2.** When the worker SEH catches a crash and replies "crashed" over the pipe, the script's `xi::use(...).process(...)` returned an empty Record — observationally identical to a plugin that returned nothing. Agent had to scrape backend stderr to know a crash happened.

`service_main`'s `use_process_cb` now injects `{"error": "<message>"}` into the Record. Verified end-to-end against the agent's own case:

```python
# Before this PR: agent's RESULTS showed
#   frame_02.png: status=error, count=None, detail="no count VAR / count == -1"
#
# After this PR (rerun against the agent's inspect.cpp / driver):
>>> run.var("error")
{'name': 'error', 'kind': 'string',
 'value': 'plugin crashed: ACCESS_VIOLATION (...)'}
```

### F-3 (P2) — instance-model.md auto-respawn description was misleading
The doc said "a buggy plugin crashes its worker; auto-respawn 3/60s" without distinguishing the in-worker SEH catch from the worker-process-death path. In practice layer 1 handles all in-process AVs without the worker dying; the respawn only fires for OOM kills, async aborts, etc. Rewrote to describe both layers.

## Test plan
- [x] Verified `error` VAR surfaces on crash frame against the agent's inspect.cpp + driver
- [ ] Regression: re-dispatch fresh agent on a similar crash-recovery brief; verify F-1 / F-2 / F-3 don't reappear

author: hash7in
body:
## Summary

Adds `sendMessageDraft` transport for Telegram DM streaming, with a critical fix for draft-vanish on tool calls and fast draft dismissal on stream end.

## Motivation

Current streaming uses `edit_message_text` which has flood-control limits and causes visible flicker. Telegram Bot API 9.3+ exposes a native draft API that renders progressively without rate-limit pressure.

## Key advantages

### 1. Draft-vanish fix on tool calls

When the LLM calls a tool mid-stream (e.g. web_search → answer), the ephemeral draft **vanishes** on the Telegram client because any real message posted by the bot dismisses it. This causes a jarring UX: partial text appears, disappears when the tool runs, then reappears.

This PR handles this at the segment-break boundary:
```python
if self._draft_mode and got_segment_break and self._accumulated:
    # Flush accumulated draft text as a real message before
    # tool-progress commentary closes the ephemeral draft.
    await self._send_new_chunk(self._accumulated, None)
```

Without this fix, DM users see text disappear on every tool call — a common pattern for search-and-answer workflows.

### 2. No "draft lingers" delay on stream end

When the stream finishes, the consumer now:
- **Skips** the redundant final `sendMessageDraft` update (avoids forcing the client to animate draft content right before the real message)
- **Sends the real message directly** in the `got_done` block instead of deferring to the gateway path

This eliminates the visible delay where the draft appears to "hang" after the real message arrives.

## Changes

### `gateway/platforms/telegram.py` (+53 lines)
- New `send_draft_message()` adapter method
- Plain text during streaming (no MarkdownV2 parse failures on incomplete content)

### `gateway/stream_consumer.py` (+128/-8 lines)
- New `transport` config field on `StreamConsumerConfig` (`"auto"`, `"draft"`, `"edit"`, `"off"`)
- New `_resolve_draft_mode()` method — resolves transport from config + adapter capability + chat_type
- New `_send_or_edit_draft()` method as draft transport path
- `__draft__` sentinel for `_message_id` (draft has no real message_id)
- **Draft-aware segment break handling** — flushes accumulated text as real message before commentary closes the draft
- **Draft-aware `got_done` handling** — skips redundant final draft update, sends real message directly
- All `__no_edit__` guards extended to include `__draft__`

### `gateway/run.py` (+20 lines)
- Enables `transport="auto"` for Telegram private chats
- Group chats / supergroups stay on standard edit path
- Passes `chat_type` as metadata so the consumer can resolve transport mode

## Behavior

| Phase | Transport | Formatting |
|-------|-----------|------------|
| Streaming (intermediate) | sendMessageDraft | Plain text |
| Segment break (tool call) | send (real message) | Plain text |
| Stream end (got_done) | send (real message) | Full MarkdownV2 |

## Test plan

```bash
pytest tests/gateway/test_stream_consumer_draft.py tests/gateway/test_stream_consumer.py -v
```

Tests cover:
- Draft resolution for DM vs group, with/without adapter support, force modes
- End-to-end draft streaming: tokens delivered via send_draft_message, real message sent on stream end
- Draft failure: consumer stays on draft path, sends real message best-effort
- Edit transport (group chat): no drafts used, standard edit path

author: anchapin
body:
💡 What: Wrapped blocking operations like `generator.generate`, `pdf_path.read_bytes`, and `resume_yaml_path.write_text` in FastAPI async endpoints using `anyio.to_thread.run_sync` combined with `functools.partial`.
🎯 Why: Synchronous operations inside an `async def` FastAPI route block the ASGI event loop, preventing concurrent handling of incoming HTTP requests and causing severe performance degradation under load.
📊 Impact: Eliminates event loop blocking during heavy operations like PDF rendering and AI tailing. Expected to drastically improve throughput and reduce latency spikes for concurrent API requests.
🔬 Measurement: Run a load test against the API with parallel requests (e.g., using `wrk` or Locust). Verify that response times for fast endpoints remain low even while slow endpoints (like PDF rendering) are running concurrently.

Add `overwrite` boolean field to the `/transcribe` request body. When `true`, passes `--overwrite` to the transcription script, allowing re-transcription of URLs whose transcript file already exists. ```json {"url": "https://youtu.be/...", "overwrite": true} ```

Greptile Summary

This PR adds an `overwrite` boolean to the `/transcribe` request body and correctly plumbs it through `handler.go` → the shell script → the new unified `transcribe.py`. It also introduces `transcribe.py` as a replacement for `faster-whisper-transcribe.py`, adding automatic Apple Silicon detection with mlx-whisper fallback.

Confidence Score: 5/5

Safe to merge; the overwrite flag is correctly implemented end-to-end and all findings are non-blocking style suggestions. All issues found are P2 (style/cleanup): a pip-install-on-every-run pattern in transcribe_mlx and an orphaned faster-whisper-transcribe.py. No logic bugs or security issues were identified. tools/transcribe.py — runtime pip install pattern; tools/faster-whisper-transcribe.py — now orphaned and could be deleted.

Important Files Changed

| Filename | Overview | |----------|----------| | internal/transcriber/handler.go | Correctly adds `overwrite` bool field to `jobRequest` and the HTTP request struct, maps it through, and appends `--overwrite` to the script args when set. | | scripts/video-transcript-summary-faster-whisper.sh | Switches `TRANSCRIBE_SCRIPT` from `faster-whisper-transcribe.py` to the new unified `transcribe.py`; all existing args (including `--overwrite`) are correctly forwarded. | | tools/transcribe.py | New unified dispatcher that tries mlx-whisper on Apple Silicon then falls back to faster-whisper; `--overwrite` flag is handled. Minor concern: mlx-whisper is pip-installed at runtime on every Apple Silicon run, inconsistent with the uv-script dependency model declared in the file header. | | tools/mlx-whisper-transcribe.py | New standalone mlx-whisper script for Apple Silicon; `--overwrite` guard is correctly implemented. Note: `--beam-size` is accepted but not forwarded to `mlx_whisper.transcribe()` (flagged in a prior review). |

Path: tools/transcribe.py Line: 66-70 Comment: **pip install runs on every Apple Silicon invocation** `subprocess.run([sys.executable, "-m", "pip", "install", ...])` is called unconditionally inside `transcribe_mlx`, so every transcription job on Apple Silicon incurs a pip-invocation RTT (even when the package is already installed). - GitHub Security Advisory: [GHSA-9qr9-h5gf-34mp](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/security/advisories/GHSA-9qr9-h5gf-34mp)
- React Advisory: [CVE-2025-55182](https://react.dev/blog/2025/12/03/critical-security-vulnerability-in-react-server-components)
- Next.js Advisory: [CVE-2025-66478](https://nextjs.org/blog/CVE-2025-66478)

This automated pull request upgrades the affected React and Next.js packages to patched versions that fully remediate the issue.

body:
Team detail pages were intermittently returning 404 or 500 because getServerSideProps fanned out to ~5 Tableland/RPC calls per request and either crashed unhandled or silently returned null on transient failures.

- Cache the pretty-link to tokenId map in-process with a short TTL and a stale fallback so a single Tableland blip does not 404 every team page. Numeric URLs now skip the lookup entirely.
- Wrap Safe.init/getOwners in try/catch and render with an empty signer list instead of 500-ing when the team owner Safe cannot be read.
- Wrap the optional ?job/?listing hydrators in try/catch for the same reason.
- Stop swallowing infrastructure errors in fetchTeamWithOwner; only return null when the team genuinely does not exist. Tolerate a failing ownerOf by rendering with owner: ''.
- Bind the Tableland signer's wallet to the configured RPC provider (ethers' Wallet.connect returns a new instance, so the previous code was leaving the wallet provider-less and falling back to the public validator).

author: alig4lfe
body:
Restore origin/main merge and ship 0.58 GovCloud/headless fixes
  
  Base: fork/develop  •  Head: update/main-0.58-clean
  
  Why this PR exists
  
  The update/main-0.58 branch carried all the features we want on top of the fork — but at some point during its life, a merge of origin/main lost a large chunk of the branch's git history. That
  branch still has the right file contents, but its log is broken enough that we don't want to push it as-is.
  
  This PR rebuilds the same end-state on a clean branch:
  
  1. Started fresh from fork/develop (full history preserved).
  2. Merged origin/main (v0.5.8) into it.
  3. Resolved 5 merge conflicts by taking the update/main-0.58 version of each file (that's the content we eventually want).
  4. Cherry-picked 4 targeted fixes from fork/Update/main-0.57 that were needed to make idp-cli deploy --from-code . --headless actually succeed for fresh and existing GovCloud stacks.
  5. Added the end-to-end test script that lives on Update/main-0.58 but was never on fork/develop.
  6. Added one new CLI fix discovered while exercising the above end-to-end: headless new-stack creation was blocked by an unused --admin-email requirement.
  
  End result: a clean branch that is a strict superset of origin/main v0.5.8, keeps every feature from fork/develop, and has working idp-cli deploy for both new and existing GovCloud/headless
  stacks.
  
  What's in this PR
  
  1. origin/main v0.5.8 merged in
  
  Commit bee44a91 Merge origin/main into update/main-0.58-clean
  
  Brings in everything from upstream through v0.5.8: unified pattern architecture, idp-cli/idp_sdk refactor, MCP integration, multi-document discovery, threat-modeling docs, the TypeScript UI
  migration, updated Bedrock model support, and ~700 other commits.
  
  Conflicted files resolved by taking the Update/main-0.58 version (byte-identical to our reference):
  
  - docs/govcloud-deployment.md — superset blend of fork's "Deployment Packages" structure + upstream's operational content
  - patterns/unified/template.yaml — +99 lines of 0.58 features on top of upstream
  - scripts/README.md — upstream version (byte-identical on Update/main-0.58)
  - scripts/generate_govcloud_template.py — upstream version (byte-identical)
  - template.yaml — +645 lines of 0.58 features on top of upstream (bastion host, headless API, VPC-secured mode, etc.)
  
  Both template YAMLs were validated as syntactically correct after the merge.
  
  2. Bring over the e2e test script
  
  Commit aea82775 Add scripts/e2e_test_headless.py from Update/main-0.58
  
  scripts/e2e_test_headless.py existed on Update/main-0.58 but not on fork/develop. It's byte-identical to d33fc9d1 on Update/main-0.58. Exercises the full headless Jobs REST API: OAuth → POST
  /jobs → presigned upload → status poll → download.
  
  3. cfn-lint fix — skip UI/AppSync templates in headless mode
  
  Commit f4f504df fix(publish): cfn-lint skips UI/AppSync templates in headless mode
  
  IDPPublisher._validate_cfn_lint always ran against idp-main.yaml and all nested templates, even with --headless. For GovCloud (us-gov-*) regions this always failed because those templates contain
  AWS::AppSync::*, AWS::CloudFront::*, and related resource types that don't exist in GovCloud — even though those resources are stripped later by HeadlessTemplateTransformer.
  
  Fix:
  
  - IDPPublisher gains a headless attribute (default False)
  - operations.publish.PublishOperations.build() sets publisher.headless before invoking publisher.run()
  - In headless mode, _validate_cfn_lint lints idp-headless.yaml if present and skips idp-main.yaml and nested/appsync
  - Non-headless behavior unchanged
  
  Resolves: E3006 Resource type AWS::AppSync::... does not exist in us-gov-west-1 during idp-cli deploy --from-code . --headless to GovCloud regions.
  
  4. cfn-lint fix — correct E/W classification and JobTracker target
  
  Commit 0117a5a0 fix(publish): correct cfn-lint E/W classification and JobTracker target
  
  Two related fixes:
  
  1. template.yaml: Moved the optional JobTracker target on WorkflowStateChangeRule from a conditional Arn field (which cfn-lint flags as E3003 'Arn' is a required property when
  DeployApiGateway=false) to a conditional target (the entire target dict is wrapped in !If so it's either complete or AWS::NoValue).
  2. lib/idp_sdk/idp_sdk/_core/publish.py: The E/W classifier in _validate_cfn_lint used substring match ":E" in line, which also matched resource prefixes like AWS::EC2::, causing W-level warnings
  with EC2 references to be counted as errors and fail the build. Fixed with a regex that matches ^E\d{4} / ^W\d{4} anchored at line start.
  
  5. CLI convenience — --headless auto-sets EnableHeadless=true
  
  Commit a727684a feat(cli): --headless flag auto-sets EnableHeadless=true stack parameter
  
  Previously users had to pass --headless (to strip UI/AppSync/Cognito from the template) AND EnableHeadless=true in --parameters (to turn on the Jobs REST API). These are always used together, so
  the CLI now sets EnableHeadless=true automatically when --headless is specified. Explicit --parameters values still win.
  
  6. Jobs API correctness — gate SUCCEEDED on results upload
  
  Commit f7470c25 fix(jobs): gate SUCCEEDED status on results.zip being uploaded
  
  GET /jobs/{id} could briefly return status=SUCCEEDED before results.zip was actually available in S3, causing racy downstream consumers (including the e2e test) to issue a download that would
  404. Now SUCCEEDED is only reported once the results object is present; otherwise we report IN_PROGRESS.
  
  7. CLI fix — headless new-stack creation ignores --admin-email
  
  Commit 46431200 fix(cli): --headless new-stack creation ignores --admin-email
  
  idp-cli deploy --headless --stack-name <new-stack> --from-code . failed on new stacks because the CLI required --admin-email, but the headless template strips the Cognito stack and does not
  declare an AdminEmail parameter. Passing --admin-email through to CloudFormation then produced:
  
  ValidationError: Parameters: [AdminEmail] do not exist in the template
  
  Fix:
  
  - For new stacks with --headless, skip the --admin-email requirement
  - If --admin-email is supplied with --headless, print a note and drop it (set to None) so it never reaches CFN
  - Non-headless new-stack behavior is unchanged (still required)
  
  Testing
  
  - ✅ Full repo merge: git diff --stat origin/main..HEAD clean, both YAML templates parse
  - ✅ Existing-stack update via idp-cli (headless, GovCloud): idp-cli deploy --stack-name my-idp-govcloud-stack --region us-gov-west-1 --from-code . --headless --wait completed in ~3 min
  (UPDATE_COMPLETE)
  - ✅ E2E against existing stack: scripts/e2e_test_headless.py my-idp-govcloud-stack samples/irs_documents.zip — jobId=25ec2930-… → SUCCEEDED, 7.4 MB results downloaded
  - ✅  Fresh-stack create via idp-cli (headless, GovCloud): pending (blocked earlier by the AdminEmail bug; ready to retry with commit 46431200)
  - ✅  E2E against fresh stack

author: deimanst
body:
1) Se soluciono el problema de los números infinitos en el input de salario neto y años trabajados:

Si bien había condición en el cual controlaba que el campo de texto "salario neto" no estuviera vacío, aun así había un problema simple pero que es grave en sí.

El hecho de que no tuviera limites es algo grave, cosa que se pudo solucionar poniendo dos condiciones más (si salario es menor o igual a 0 o salario mayor a 9999999).

De igual forma los problemas aun seguían, ya que en el input por algún motivo se podía poner mas de 7 caracteres incluso limitando con restricciones de "min" y "max". El problema es que la restricción solamente sirve para el slider, y cuando ingresamos por teclado, esa restricción no lo detecta, cosa que se soluciono poniendo un "oninput" que se ejecuta cada vez que escribas, también te permite poner código de js, por lo tanto lo que hice fue que, si el largo del valor es igual o mayor a 7, que el valor se limite hasta 7 caracteres.

Después pensé que se había finalizado, hasta que probé usando estos caracteres especiales ['e', 'E', '-'], el problema era que al poner esos caracteres, por algún motivo, rompía o filtraba mis restricciones. Tuve que buscar como solucionar, y ver como hacer para poder desactivar esos caracteres especiales, y vi que existe el evento "onkeydown", lo que hace el evento es que detecta que presionaste. A partir de ahí podes hacer una condición en el cual, si una tecla es presionada y esa misma esta restringida, devuelve falso. Lo mismo hice con años trabajados.

En los años trabajados lo que hice una condición que compare dos valores, si el valor comparado es menor a 60, no se le aplica restricción, pero si el valor es mayor a 60, se restringe ese valor.

2) Descarga de pdf no restringida

Me di cuenta que el botón de descargar pdf no estaba desactivado cuando no había cálculos, por lo cual tuve que desactivar por defecto, crear una id "downloadPDF" y en la función de cálculos hice que, al presionar el botón calculo, active el botón de crear pdf.

3) Añadido de salario mínimo actual:
Puse un párrafo que muestre el salario mínimo actual, y que al hacer click, te envíe al gub.uy.

4) Arreglo en el estilo (css):

Arreglé el canva, que quedaba un poco raro en el inicio, y es que no estaba bien centrada y además estaba un poco pequeño, también hice que todo el texto esté centrado.

Con eso concluyo con uno de mis aportes.

## Summary

Routine upstream tracking. Per CLAUDE.md update strategy, Immich is intentionally pinned (tight ML/postgres coupling); server and ML must be bumped together to the same version.

- `immich-server:v2.6.3` → `v2.7.5`
- `immich-machine-learning:v2.6.3` → `v2.7.5`
- `postgresql-immich` and `redis-immich` untouched — no version coupling required for this bump

## Procedure (already executed on host)

1. `podman pull` both images first — image fetch is the most likely failure mode and runs against unchanged units
2. Edit both quadlet `Image=` lines on a feature branch
3. `systemctl --user daemon-reload && systemctl --user restart immich-server immich-ml`
4. Wait for `(healthy)` from both containers, verify migrations ran cleanly

### 📚 Description

When `mapId` or `colorScheme` change, the map is torn down and re-created. The standalone center watcher then re-fired against the new map instance, calling `setCenter` with the prop's initial center and discarding the user's pan. Persist the captured center into `centerOverride` before teardown so that `options.value.center` reflects the user's actual position; the watcher's lat/lng comparison guard then short-circuits.

Also re-emit `ready` after the new Map instance is constructed so consumers that attach imperative state via the exposed `map` ref (outside of declarative children) can re-bind to the new instance.

## Summary

author: nickborgers
body:
## Summary

- Detect when HEAD is a non-fixer commit on top of a cycle that already converged to GO; reset the cycle counter to 1 instead of consuming a fixer-retry slot
- Cap (`MAX=2`) stays as-is — it still bounds fixer convergence on stubborn NO-GO PRs and still fires on cap-exhausted state (verdict on `cycle_sha` = NO-GO blocks the reset)
- Document as §1.16 in `docs/agentic-pipeline-learnings.md` and cross-reference from §1.13 + the cap-check inline comment

## Motivation

PR #492 hit `cycle_capped` after a local commit was pushed on top of a cycle 2 GO. Walk-back found `prior=2`, computed `next=3 > MAX=2`, and finalized terminal NO-GO with `needs-human-review` — without ever running reviewers on the new content. The `review-entry.yml` GO short-circuit only matches the exact GO SHA, not a descendant, so contributors who tweak a converged PR brick it instead of getting a fresh review.

The cap exists to bound fixer-retry attempts (§1.13), not to penalize human follow-up. This change separates those concerns at the gather step.

## Detection

In `review-pipeline.yml` gather job, after the merge-from-main inherit detection:

1. Skip when `inherited=true` or `prior_cycle=0` (nothing to reset)
2. Read git author email of HEAD via `gh api`. If it equals `ci@hide-my-list.local` (the fixer's `git config user.email` in `review-fixer.yml`), this is a fixer commit — skip
3. Read `review/verdict` description on `cycle_sha`. If `GO`, set `reset=true`
4. `Compute next cycle` then stamps `cycle=1` instead of `prior+1`

Reviewers, fixer, and judge all run normally on the reset cycle — only the counter resets.

## Edge cases

- **Cap-exhausted (NO-GO) ancestor:** `review/verdict` on `cycle_sha` = NO-GO → reset doesn't fire. Cap stays in effect; `/review` and force-push escape hatches still apply.
- **Multiple consecutive human commits after GO:** each push triggers detection independently; each gets a fresh cycle 1 budget. Acceptable for contributor workflow.
- **Human commit on top of NO-GO (pre-cap):** reset doesn't fire (verdict ≠ GO). Existing behavior preserved.
- **Inherit-from-main path takes precedence:** `if: steps.delta.outputs.inherited != 'true'` guards the new step.

## Test plan

- [ ] CI passes (actionlint, internal validations)
- [ ] Pipeline runs cleanly on a no-op cycle 1 GO (no regression to short-circuit)
- [ ] Push a small follow-up commit on top of a cycle 1 or cycle 2 GO and confirm pipeline runs cycle 1 fresh instead of capping
- [ ] Confirm cap-exhausted scenario still terminates correctly (verdict on cycle_sha = NO-GO)

## Summary

- Adds \`render_spdx(r)\` which emits an SPDX 3.0.1 JSON-LD document with \`profileConformance = [core, software, security]\`. Each canonical asset becomes a \`software_Package\`; each finding (the same predicates the SARIF renderer uses) becomes a \`security_Vulnerability\` plus a \`security_VexAffectedVulnAssessmentRelationship\` linking it to the host package.

## Summary

Lands the second-phase OEX voice port into hq-x as a single follow-up to #2. Brand-axis throughout. Four chunks of work shipped:

### 1. IVR engine
- `app/routers/ivr.py` — 6 TwiML endpoints (entry/step/gather/lookup/dial-action/record-action) under `/api/voice/ivr/{brand_id}/`. Twilio HMAC-SHA1 signature validated against the brand's decrypted `auth_token`.
- `app/routers/ivr_config.py` — flow / step / phone-config CRUD plus Supabase Storage audio-file management under `/api/brands/{brand_id}/ivr-config`.
- `migrations/0011_fmcsa_ivr_seed.sql` — idempotently creates an `fmcsa-stub` brand (keyed on stable name, ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING) and seeds the 10-step FMCSA Carrier Qualification flow (mirrors OEX migration 031).

### 2. Voice provisioning pipeline
- `app/services/pipelines/voice.py` — 7-step orchestration (Trust Hub Customer Profile → TwiML app → phone purchase → SHAKEN/STIR → A2P → phone-trust assignment → IVR template). Returns a structured per-step result dict.
- `app/routers/provisioning.py` — `POST /api/brands/{brand_id}/provisioning/voice` synchronous entry-point.
- `app/routers/twiml_apps.py` — Twilio TwiML application CRUD against the brand's creds.

### 3. Outbound calls
- `app/services/outbound_calls.py` — **pre-creates a `call_logs` row** (not `voice_sessions`, which is folded) and writes `outbound_call_configs.call_log_id` FK to `call_logs(id)` per the architectural decision in HANDOFF (point 12).
- `app/routers/outbound_calls.py` — REST POST/GET plus 5 TwiML token-validated endpoints. Preserves `_MAX_CONNECT_LOOPS = 5` dial-loop guard.

### 4. Voice CRUD
- `app/routers/voice.py` — dispositions, call actions (hangup/redirect/hold/unhold), session queries against `call_logs`, transfer-territory CRUD.
- `app/routers/voice_campaigns.py` — voice-AI campaign config upsert/GET, metrics readout.
- `app/routers/voice_analytics.py` — 5 readouts (summary, by-campaign, daily-trend, cost-breakdown, transfer-rate) over Postgres `call_logs`.

## Skipped per directive

- **Voice Access Token** (`GET /api/voice/token`) — dropped per directive §3 (deferred, no in-repo Twilio JS consumer).
- **Voice campaign batch loop** (`POST /{campaign_id}/batch`) — Agent B owns the unit-of-work batch service per directive §10.
- **Persistent provisioning ledger** (`company_provisioning_runs`, `provisioning_run_steps`, `_step_*` helpers from OEX `services/company_provisioning.py`) — not ported. The OEX ledger threaded `org_id`/`company_id`; hq-x has no `companies` table and is single-operator. The new pipeline returns a structured result dict; per-step persistence already lives in existing side-effect tables (`trust_hub_registrations`, `voice_phone_numbers`, `ivr_phone_configs`).
- **Live transcription / Intelligence Service / call-transcript endpoints** in `routers/voice.py` — `call_transcripts` and `live_transcription_utterances` tables are not ported (deferred).
- **`voicemail_drops` table lookup** in the AI voicemail-drop TwiML endpoint — table not ported (decision 13). Falls back to per-call `voicemail_audio_url` saved on `outbound_call_configs`.
- **ClickHouse query path** in `voice_analytics` — `app/clickhouse.py` exposes only the fire-and-forget writer; analytics reads go through Postgres. The query path can layer on without API-shape changes.

## Model adjustments

- `voicemail_drop_id` removed from `VoiceAiCampaignConfigRequest`, `VoiceCampaignConfigCreate`, `VoiceCampaignConfigResponse` — column does not exist on `voice_ai_campaign_configs` in hq-x.
- `IvrPhoneConfigCreate.partner_id` removed — column does not exist on `ivr_phone_configs`.

`migrations/0011_fmcsa_ivr_seed.sql` is idempotent and applied via the existing migration runner. No other schema changes.

## Summary

Worktrees spawned under `<main>/.claude/worktrees/<name>/` only carry the small `elasticFrame` example, not the ~2 GB `Test_NLShell` and `solid_partition_example` fixtures that live in the main checkout. As a result, ~32 fixture-gated integration tests silently skipped on every worktree-based PR run, masking real coverage.

`tests/conftest.py` now resolves `EXAMPLES_DIR` via a small helper that:

1. Uses `<repo_root>/stko_results_examples` if it has the heavier fixtures.
2. Otherwise, if `repo_root` lives under `.claude/worktrees/<name>/`, derives the main checkout path and uses its examples directory.
3. Otherwise, leaves the path as-is so the existing per-fixture `.exists()` skip logic still applies.

No fixture files are copied or symlinked — the resolver just points the same code at the existing main-checkout copy when needed. Behaviour outside worktrees is unchanged (the heavy-fixture check passes, so the local path is used).

## Test plan

- [x] Inside a `.claude/worktrees/...` worktree carrying only `elasticFrame`: `pytest -q` went from **570 passed, 32 skipped** to **602 passed, 0 skipped**.

| [`README.md`](src/data_pipelines_track/module-02-pipeline-orchestration-internals/README.md) | 103 | Module index, mission framing, learning outcomes, lesson summaries |

## Quiz format

Per the lesson learned from PR #14: every `Tracing`-typed question is a real "predict the stdout" exercise with a `prompt.program` field containing pure synchronous Rust and an `answer.stdout` matching that program's literal output. **Each Tracing program was compiled and run locally before commit; outputs verified.** No async/tokio code in any Tracing question.

| Lesson | Tracing topic | Verified output |
|---|---|---|
| L2 | Kahn's algorithm topo-sort over a small fan-in graph | `radar optical normalize dedup sink` |
| L3 | Decorrelated-jitter backoff schedule under upper-bound pinning | 6-line schedule, total 18900ms |
| L4 | Circuit breaker state evolution over a synthetic outcome sequence | 7-step transition with the trip on step 5 |

L1's quiz is all MultipleChoice — the lesson's topics (tokio runtime, spawn semantics, abort/cancel) are inherently runtime-dependent and don't fit a pure-sync Tracing exercise. Forcing it would just reproduce the M1 bug.

## Voice and structure

Every lesson follows the structure established in M1: `## Context` → `## Core Concepts` (3-5 subsections) → `## Code Examples` (2-3 code blocks with surrounding analysis) → `## Key Takeaways` → `{{#quiz}}` embed. NASA-internal-engineering-doc tone, direct technical prose, forward references to subsequent modules where relevant. Mission framing in the README's blockquote (OPS ALERT — SDA-2026-0119) and in the project brief's mission framing (OPS DIRECTIVE — SDA-2026-0119 / Phase 2 Implementation).

## Source attribution

Every lesson's frontmatter cites named source-book chapters (Async Rust by Flitton & Morton; DDIA by Kleppmann; Kafka: The Definitive Guide by Shapira et al.; Fundamentals of Data Engineering by Reis & Housley). Lesson 2 includes a `> **Source note:**` callout where DDIA's operator-graph execution model is referenced from training knowledge of the well-established material rather than a direct quotation. Lesson 4 includes a similar note for the supervisor pattern, which draws on Erlang/OTP design that predates and informed all the cited texts.

## Build verification

`mdbook build` runs clean against the full book — every quiz parses, every internal link resolves, no broken-link warnings. mdbook-quiz validates each Tracing question's `program` field as required.

- [x] Every quiz file parses as TOML with exactly 5 questions and unique UUIDs
- [ ] CI passes on this branch
- [ ] Sidebar visually shows the new Module 2 entries under Data Pipelines Track when site is regenerated

## Project arc continuity

This module is the connective tissue. The orchestrator interface established here is what M3, M4, M5, and M6 each build on — the next session's work continues with M3's event-time correlator (replaces M1's dedup operator behind the same orchestrator API). The "What Comes Next" section in the README and project brief explicitly tee up that continuity.

body:
## Summary

Vercel build at 8c31f65 (post-merge of #239) failed:

```
Module not found: Can't resolve './domain.js'
> 29 | import { usgToBbl, usgToMt } from './domain.js';
Import trace: packages/pricing/src/calculator.ts → DealEconomicsCard.tsx → Chat.tsx
```

Vex's source uses ESM-style `.js` extensions on relative imports because vex builds to `dist`. Procur's other workspace packages don't — they import without an extension. The `.js` suffix slipped past local `pnpm tsc --noEmit` (TypeScript bundler-mode is fine either way) but Next's production webpack does Node-style resolution and won't follow `.js` → `.ts`.

## Fix

Stripped `.js` from every relative import in `packages/pricing/src/{calculator.ts, benchmarks.ts, index.ts, calculator.test.ts}`.

## Verification

- `pnpm --filter app build` passes locally (Next 15 production build to mirror Vercel).
- `pnpm --filter @procur/pricing test` — 24/24 still pass under node:test + tsx.
- `pnpm --filter @procur/pricing --filter @procur/catalog --filter app type-check` — clean.

## Process note

Type-check alone wasn't enough to catch this — TS bundler resolution is permissive. Adding `pnpm --filter app build` to the pre-push checklist for any change that touches a workspace package imported by app would have caught it.

body:
## Summary

I fixed duplicate inline review rendering by normalizing Codex review status labels and hiding review-internal replay messages that should only be represented by structured review cards.

The specific broken shape was a Codex entered-review hint like `changes against 'main'`, while the composer had already rendered `Review changes against main`. Those did not match, so both cards stayed visible.

There was also a broader replay issue: Codex review prompts could surface as normal user messages, and review completion text could render once as a review card and again as an assistant message. The adapter and renderer now suppress those review internals for both live events and hydrated `thread/read` replay.

I added captured-protocol regressions for the later failures too: Codex sent an `exitedReviewMode` review containing review findings, then repeated the exact same text as `review_rollout_assistant`. The review UI now parses plain `Review comment:` and `Full review comments:` blocks into individual finding cards, and the duplicate assistant message is not shown.

## Changes

- Added shared review display-text normalization for review hints, base-branch labels, commit labels, and current-change labels.
- Applied that normalization in the Codex app-server adapter and renderer live event path.
- Changed optimistic review pruning to compare normalized review labels instead of raw strings.
- Suppressed review prompt user messages and duplicate assistant messages already represented by review output cards.
- Suppressed live pending assistant echoes when a review turn completes.
- Hid raw entered-review protocol text when it normalizes to the same review label already shown in the card header.
- Rendered plain Codex `Review comment:` and `Full review comments:` findings inside review cards with priority, title, path, and line range.
- Added captured-protocol replay coverage for one-finding and two-finding review outputs followed by duplicate `review_rollout_assistant` messages.

# [S-5.02] SessionEnd hook wiring — second E-5 lifecycle event **Epic:** E-5 — New Hook Events and 1.0.0 Release **Mode:** greenfield **Convergence:** CONVERGED after 9 adversarial passes (D-137; CLEAN_PASS_3_OF_3 at pass-9) ![Tests](https://img.shields.io/badge/tests-11%2F11-brightgreen) ![Coverage](https://img.shields.io/badge/coverage-n%2Fa-lightgrey) ![Mutation](https://img.shields.io/badge/mutation-n%2Fa-lightgrey) ![Holdout](https://img.shields.io/badge/holdout-N%2FA--wave--gate-blue) This PR delivers the second story in Epic E-5 (Tier G, Wave 16): the `SessionEnd` hook wiring. It creates a new WASM plugin crate (`crates/hook-plugins/session-end-telemetry/`) that emits `session.ended` telemetry (duration_ms, tool_call_count, timestamp) on every Claude Code session end. The dual-routing-table architecture (ADR-011) is used: Layer 1 (`hooks.json.template`) routes to the dispatcher binary; Layer 2 (`hooks-registry.toml`) routes to the WASM plugin. SessionEnd is simpler than SessionStart — no subprocess, no file reads, zero capability tables — and the lessons from S-5.01's 14-pass convergence were applied up-front, achieving convergence in 9 passes. 11/11 integration tests GREEN; clippy clean; no workspace regressions. --- ## Summary - S-5.02: SessionEnd hook wiring — second Tier G lifecycle hook event (FR-046, second of 5) - New crate: `crates/hook-plugins/session-end-telemetry/` (WASM plugin) - New `SessionEnd` entry in `plugins/vsdd-factory/hooks-registry.toml` - `hooks.json.template` `SessionEnd` entry was pre-existing (Task 4 was no-op) - Spec: 9-pass adversarial convergence (D-137; CLEAN_PASS_3_OF_3; saved 5 passes vs S-5.01) - Tests: 11/11 integration GREEN; clippy clean; no workspace regressions --- ## Architecture Changes ```mermaid graph TD HooksJsonTemplate["plugins/vsdd-factory/hooks/hooks.json.template\n(VERIFIED — SessionEnd entry pre-existing)"] HooksRegistryToml["plugins/vsdd-factory/hooks-registry.toml\n(MODIFIED — SessionEnd entry added)"] SessionEndPlugin["crates/hook-plugins/session-end-telemetry/\n(NEW — WASM plugin crate)"] IntegrationTests["crates/hook-plugins/session-end-telemetry/tests/integration_test.rs\n(NEW — VP-066 harness, 11 tests)"] HooksJsonTemplate -->|"Layer 1: routes to"| DispatcherBinary["factory-dispatcher binary\n(existing)"] HooksRegistryToml -->|"Layer 2: routes to"| SessionEndPlugin SessionEndPlugin -->|"emits"| SessionEndedEvent["session.ended event\n(3 plugin-set fields)"] IntegrationTests -->|"validates"| HooksRegistryToml IntegrationTests -->|"validates"| SessionEndPlugin style SessionEndPlugin fill:#90EE90 style IntegrationTests fill:#90EE90 style HooksRegistryToml fill:#FFFACD ```
ADR-011: Dual-Routing-Tables Architecture (applied to SessionEnd) **Context:** Claude Code hooks route to binaries (not WASM directly). The dispatcher provides WASM sandboxing. **Decision:** Two routing tables, strict layer separation: - **Layer 1** (`hooks.json.template`): Claude Code harness routing — references only the dispatcher binary; enforces once-per-session via `once: true` - **Layer 2** (`hooks-registry.toml`): Dispatcher routing — references only WASM plugin paths; provides capability declarations **Rationale:** Enforces that WASM filenames NEVER appear in Layer 1 (hooks.json.template); prevents capability bypass; enables dispatcher timeout < harness timeout. **SessionEnd timeout hierarchy (two-level):** `5000ms` (hooks-registry.toml dispatcher timeout) < `10000ms` (hooks.json.template harness timeout). Simpler than SessionStart's three-level hierarchy (no subprocess timeout). **S-5.01 lessons applied up-front:** - No SS-01 BCs needed (canonical patterns cover routing without new SS-01 work) - No new host fns (SessionEnd needs no file reads, no subprocess) - No dispatcher-side dedup (Layer 1 once-discipline handles idempotency) - Zero capability tables in hooks-registry.toml (simplest possible sandbox profile)

author: itensorbot
body:
## Summary

Test and integration-test workflows currently re-run on every tag push. The same commit was already tested on merge to `main`, and tags fire after registration — re-running adds no signal. Documentation keeps tag triggering for Documenter.jl's versioned-docs flow but restricts to `v*` so subdir-package tags don't pollute the docs build.

## Background

The original PkgTemplates.jl design ships a single combined CI workflow where `tags: '*'` was needed so Documenter.jl's versioned-docs deploy job would fire on tag pushes. Splitting tests and docs into separate workflow files inherited the trigger block on both sides, so the test workflows have been firing on every tag push as a side-effect rather than for any active reason.

This PR mirrors the corresponding skeleton change in [ITensorPkgSkeleton.jl#132](https://github.com/ITensor/ITensorPkgSkeleton.jl/pull/132).

## Changes

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `Tests.yml` | Drop `tags: "*"` |
| `IntegrationTest.yml` | Drop `tags: "*"` |
| `Documentation.yml` | `tags: "*"` → `tags: ["v*"]` |

body: ## PR: Story #43 — Seed course, degree, and department catalog tables Closes #43 --- ## Context Sprint 1 left a deferral in ADR-004: > "Courses belong to multiple degrees via a degree_courses junction. > Deferred. For Sprint 1 we assume each course belongs to exactly one > degree." This PR resolves that deferral, restructures the schema to reflect how Wits actually works, and replaces the two old migration/seed files with a single schema file and a single seed file. --- ## What changed ### Schema (`database/createSchema.sql`) Full rewrite of the old `migration-001-student-schema.sql`. - Added `departments` table (`dept_code`, `dept_name`, `faculty_name`) - Added `dept_code NOT NULL FK` to `degrees` — degrees now reference the school that offers them - Replaced `courses.degree_code` with `courses.dept_code` — courses are owned by a department (school), not a single degree program. This resolves the cross-program course problem: MECN4020 (taken by Mechanical, Industrial, Aeronautical, and Electrical/Information students) now exists as one row owned by MIA school. EIE students can still enroll via the `enrollments` junction - Removed `courses TEXT[]` JSON column from `staff` — same violation rejected for students in ADR-004, now fixed for staff too - Added nullable `dept_code FK` to `staff` - Added `staff_courses(staff_number, course_code)` junction table with composite PK and cascade deletes — replaces the JSON column - All other tables (`students`, `enrollments`, `consultations`, `consultation_attendees`) unchanged - DROP TABLE list updated to include `staff_courses` and `departments` in correct dependency order ### Seed (`database/seedVitalInfo.sql`) Full rewrite of the old `seed-001-degrees-and-courses.sql`. - 2 departments: EIE, MIA (both under Faculty of Engineering and the Built Environment) - 5 degrees across both departments: BScEng Information, BScEng Electrical, BScEng Mechanical, BScEng Industrial, BScEng Aeronautical - 36 courses total from the official May/June 2026 assessment timetable: 23 EIE courses (years 2–4) and 13 MIA courses (years 2–4) - 2 seed staff members with `dept_code` - 4 `staff_courses` assignments linking staff to courses - 1 seed student (unchanged) ### File renames - `migration-001-student-schema.sql` → `createSchema.sql` - `seed-001-degrees-and-courses.sql` → `seedVitalInfo.sql` - Path references updated in `setup.js`, `ConsultationDB.test.js`, and `studentData.test.js` ### Signup controller (`src/controllers/signup-controller.js`) - Removed `courses` from destructured body params and from the staff `INSERT` statement — column no longer exists on the `staff` table ### ADR - Added ADR-006 documenting the decision to move course ownership from degrees to departments, resolving the ADR-004 deferral --- ## Tests ### New: `tests/unit/departmentSchema.test.js` (17 tests) - `departments` NOT NULL and PRIMARY KEY constraints - `degrees` FK enforcement — rejects insert with invalid `dept_code` - `courses` FK enforcement — rejects insert with invalid `dept_code` - `staff_courses` composite PK — rejects duplicate pair - `staff_courses` FK enforcement — rejects invalid `staff_number` and invalid `course_code` - `staff_courses` cascade delete when staff member is deleted - `staff_courses` cascade delete when course is deleted - Cross-department enrollment — confirms an EIE student can enroll in a MIA course via `enrollments` with no FK violation ### New: `tests/unit/staffCourses.test.js` (6 tests) - "Which courses does a lecturer teach?" query returns correct results - "Which lecturers teach a course?" query returns correct results - Unassigned lecturer returns empty array, not an error - Course with no assigned lecturers returns empty array - Adding a second course to a lecturer increases their count correctly - Removing a `staff_courses` row does not cascade to staff or course ### Updated: `tests/unit/ConsultationDB.test.js` (1 new test) - `staff_courses` table exists and is queryable ### Updated: `tests/unit/studentData.test.js` and `ConsultationDB.test.js` - `beforeAll` blocks updated to insert department before degree (required by new NOT NULL FK) - `dept_code` added to degree inserts - `courses` column removed from staff inserts - `degree_code` → `dept_code` in course inserts --- ## Acceptance tests - [x] Departments table populated (2 departments) - [x] Degrees table populated with FK to departments (5 degrees) - [x] Courses table populated with FK to departments (36 courses) - [x] Student table has valid degree FK - [x] Staff courses reference valid course codes via junction table - [x] All existing tests pass - [x] `npm run setup` runs without errors on a fresh database

author: shakestzd
body:
## Summary

This PR is the registry-hardening half of the original bundle. The
indexer-removal half was split out per review feedback so each behavioral
change is reviewable in isolation.

**Scope (this PR):**

- **internal/registry**: `looksLikeRealProject` guard rejects test/temp dirs in `Upsert` so test runs cannot pollute the user's live registry. `Save` calls `Prune` before writing so stale entries auto-clean over time. `DefaultPath()` honors `XDG_DATA_HOME`; `Load` falls back to the legacy `~/.local/share/htmlgraph/projects.json` when the canonical path is missing, then `Save` migrates to the canonical path on the next cycle.
- **cmd/htmlgraph/projects**: `persistentPreRunE` wires `defaultRegistryPath` so all subcommands share the same indirection. `projects list` and `projects prune` use it; `serve_parent`, `serve_global`, and `main`'s registry upsert all flow through the same indirection now (no more `registry.DefaultPath()` direct calls in this binary).
- **cmd/htmlgraph/serve_parent**: stat-then-skip startup auto-prune — only `Save()` when `Prune()` actually removed entries, instead of rewriting the file unconditionally on every server boot.
- **cmd/htmlgraph/serve_child**: parent-supplied `HTMLGRAPH_REGISTRY_PATH` is honored so children share the parent's registry view.
- **internal/agent/detect**: also recognise `CLAUDECODE=1` (Claude Code 2.x ships the no-underscore name) so agent_id never silently falls back to "human". Discovered while debugging the yolo-guard during this PR — without this fix the research-first guard never sees Read/Bash/Edit events for orchestrator sessions, because the `agent_events` CHECK constraint silently rejects rows with `agent_id='human'`. Test added.
- **Test hygiene**: deleted `testmain_test.go`; XDG_DATA_HOME/XDG_CONFIG_HOME isolation inlined into `worktree_helpers_test.go` (consolidated TestMain). TestMain cleanup now runs before `os.Exit` rather than via deferred funcs that never fire. `withRegistryAtAndStale` calls a new `registry.WriteEntriesForTest` helper that shares the atomic-write path with `Save`, so the JSON format cannot drift between production and tests. Added `TestLoad_LegacyFallback` to cover the migrate-on-save behavior end-to-end.

**Out of scope (split into a separate PR):**

The NDJSON→SQLite indexer removal in `serve_child.go` (bug-28a9d7a7) was reverted on this branch and will land in its own PR with a proper title/summary so reviewers can evaluate it in isolation.

## Revision notes (post-review)

Addresses every issue from the PR #62 self-review:

1. 🔴 **Scope creep** — indexer removal reverted on this branch; will be filed as its own PR.
2. 🟡 **TestMain defer-after-os.Exit leak** — cleanup now runs before `os.Exit`. Also fixed a pre-existing build error: undefined `otelCollectTestBinaryTmpDir` reference replaced with `filepath.Dir(otelCollectTestBinary)`.
3. 🟡 **PR title overstated** — softened to drop "concurrent writes" (no locking added in this PR; only atomic temp+rename, which pre-existed) and "atomic write" framing.
4. 🟡 **Save() Prune side-effect naming** — godoc expanded to a prominent SIDE EFFECT block; rename deferred to keep call-site churn small.
5. 🟡 **DefaultPath migration gap** — Load now falls back to the legacy path when canonical is missing; Save migrates to canonical on the next cycle. Legacy file is intentionally left intact as a recovery copy. Test added.
6. 🟢 **serve_parent startup auto-prune** — stat-then-skip; reconciled `defaultRegistryPath` indirection across serve_parent / serve_global / main.
7. 🟢 **withRegistryAtAndStale format duplication** — extracted shared `writeEntriesAtomic` writer; tests now go through `registry.WriteEntriesForTest` which uses the same path as `Save`.
8. 🟢 **/api/indexer/status 404 test** — moved to the split-out indexer-removal PR (where the endpoint actually goes away). Restoring the indexer here means the endpoint still serves, so the test is irrelevant on this branch.

## Test plan

- [x] `go build ./... && go vet ./... && go test ./...` — all pass
- [x] `go test ./internal/registry/... -count=1` — 13 tests, all pass (TestLoad_LegacyFallback, TestNoRegistryPollution, TestDefaultPath/{fallback,xdg}, etc.)
- [x] Pre-commit hooks ran the full suite for every commit; all green

author: itensorbot
body:
## Summary

Test and integration-test workflows currently re-run on every tag push. The same commit was already tested on merge to `main`, and tags fire after registration — re-running adds no signal. Documentation keeps tag triggering for Documenter.jl's versioned-docs flow but restricts to `v*` so subdir-package tags don't pollute the docs build.

## Background

The original PkgTemplates.jl design ships a single combined CI workflow where `tags: '*'` was needed so Documenter.jl's versioned-docs deploy job would fire on tag pushes. Splitting tests and docs into separate workflow files inherited the trigger block on both sides, so the test workflows have been firing on every tag push as a side-effect rather than for any active reason.

This PR mirrors the corresponding skeleton change in [ITensorPkgSkeleton.jl#132](https://github.com/ITensor/ITensorPkgSkeleton.jl/pull/132).

## Changes

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `Tests.yml` | Drop `tags: "*"` |
| `IntegrationTest.yml` | Drop `tags: "*"` |
| `Documentation.yml` | `tags: "*"` → `tags: ["v*"]` |

## Summary
Fixes three issues with the AI visualizer reported from production testing:

1. **Color names hidden behind swatches** — tooltip now floats above the swatch with `z-index:20`, plus each color group's header carries a persistent selected-color chip so the name is always visible regardless of touch / focus state.
2. **Wrong colors for the selected Timberline line** — each line (NS, HDZ, UHDZ, Camelot II) now carries its own GAF-canonical color list. Switching the line repaints the picker and updates the header label.

author: luckypipewrench
body:
## Summary

Adds the `internal/contract/inference` package: pure Go statistical primitives for classifying behavioral-rule confidence from recorded observation events. Wires the deployment-configurable surface (exposure floors) into config, and the operational surface (verdict and floor-failure histograms) into the metrics bundle. No runtime wiring yet; that lands in a follow-up alongside `pipelock learn compile`.

## What's in the package

- **`wilson.go`**: Wilson score interval lower and upper bound for binomial proportion confidence on small or skewed samples (Newcombe 1998 closed form). The 0.95 z-score is fixed for the production path so identical recorder data uses the same statistical contract across deployments; the alpha-parameterized signature stays for testability. `DefaultWilsonAlpha = 0.05` is a named package constant rather than a config field. The confidence level is part of the statistical contract, and making it deployment-configurable would let two installs infer different classifications from identical recorder data.

- **`opportunity.go`**: Conditional-opportunity denominator picker per the contract design's hierarchy table (host stability to sessions, path-family stability to host sessions, method stability to host/path-family events, header shape / arg schema to tool-endpoint calls, sequence n-gram to source-action windows). Strict per-load validation at the boundary; unknown level rejects with `ErrUnknownOpportunityLevel`, negative input rejects with `ErrNegativeOpportunityCount`.

- **`floors.go`**: Three exposure-floor gates (min_sessions, min_events, min_windows, defaults 5 / 20 / 3) plus the `Classify` composer that AND-composes Wilson plus floors into a `never_confirmed` / `brittle` / `stable` verdict. Floors are deployment-configurable (traffic volumes differ across deployments); thresholds (tau_brittle = 0.50, tau_stable = 0.85) are hardcoded. Any floor failure forces `never_confirmed` regardless of Wilson, proven by the 8-row floor-pass/fail by Wilson-stable matrix test.

- **`budgets.go`**: p99, p95, median, max, sample_count statistics for numeric rate and size budgets, with caller-selectable headroom (`DefaultHeadroomRate = 0.20`, `DefaultHeadroomSize = 0.50`). Nearest-rank percentile via integer arithmetic, keeping results deterministic without floating-point ceil-rounding edges. Empty input returns a zero-valued Budget (no panic). `ThinSample(minEvents)` flag for the review-UX badge.

## Config surface

Adds `learn.inference.floors.{min_sessions, min_events, min_windows}` to the existing `learn:` block.

- Missing or zero resolves to defaults applied at runtime via `inference.Floors.Resolved()`.
- Negative is rejected at config-load with a precise YAML field-path error.
- The config validator deliberately duplicates the inference package's `Floors.Validate()` so operators see `learn.inference.floors.min_sessions: -1: must be non-negative` instead of an API-level field name. Layering rationale documented inline.

## Metrics surface

Two new counters in the existing `internal/metrics/learn.go` bundle (no new file, per-feature bundling stays intact):

- `pipelock_learn_inference_classify_total{outcome}`: outcome is one of `never_confirmed`, `brittle`, `stable`. Powers the review-UX verdict histogram.
- `pipelock_learn_inference_floor_failures_total{floor}`: floor is one of `sessions`, `events`, `windows`. Diagnostic for which floor is the bottleneck on a deployment's data volume.

Nil-safe recorder helpers parallel to the existing observation-pipeline pattern.

## Policy-hash impact

Adding floors to the `Learn` config flows into the canonical policy hash. Floors are detection-relevant: they decide stable vs never_confirmed at compile time, so verifiers must observe the schema change to detect deployments that loosen the exposure gates. Both `goldenHashDefaults` and `goldenHashRichConfig` shift in lockstep with `Defaults()`. Deliberately hash-pinned so the verifier's authenticated state matches the contract.

## Coverage and tests

- 100% line coverage on every function in `internal/contract/inference/` (wilson, opportunity, floors, budgets); 18 of 18 functions at 100%.
- 100% on the new config validator (`validateLearnInferenceFloors`) and on every new metrics helper (`RecordInferenceClassification`, `RecordInferenceFloorFailure`).
- 16-corner-case Wilson test pack matching the design table to 3 decimal places, plus property tests for monotonicity, determinism over 1000 invocations, and complementary symmetry of upper/lower bounds.
- 8-row floor-pass/fail by Wilson-stable matrix proving floor failure overrides Wilson regardless of confidence.
- `p99 >= p95 >= median`, `max >= p99` properties verified across 5 different windows.

## Cross-build

Linux and Windows, default and enterprise build tags, all four green. Inference is pure Go math plus `slices` stdlib, no syscall surface.

## Out of scope

- Runtime wiring (the inference engine consuming live recorder events): follows in a later PR.
- `pipelock learn compile` end-to-end CLI: follows in a later PR.
- Path-family normalization and cardinality cap: follows in a later PR.
- The verifier `verify.py` is not extended; this PR does not emit signed artifacts.
